declarations.doc: **One odd step, in the conjugated variable.** For `u` even, `g (u + 1) = 3 (u / 2) + 1`: the odd step subtracts, so on `u = y - 1` it is exactly halve-then-triple.
declarations.name: negT_step_succ

declarations.doc: **The run of an odd start, in closed form.** With `y = 2 ^ a * m + 1` and `m` odd, the first `a` iterates are `g^[k] y = 3 ^ k * 2 ^ (a - k) * m + 1`. This is the note's Lemma 1: the run identity `2 ^ k (g^[k] y - 1) = 3 ^ k (y - 1)` with no subtraction.
declarations.name: negT_run_iter

declarations.doc: The iterates stay odd for `k < a`.
declarations.name: negT_run_odd

declarations.doc: The iterate at `k = a` is even: the run has exactly `a` odd steps.
declarations.name: negT_run_even

declarations.doc: **A run of `a` odd steps starts at `y ≥ 2 ^ a + 1`** (the note's Lemma 1, last clause; Hercher's Lemma 8 with `y ≡ 1` in place of `y ≡ -1`, so the floor is larger by two).
declarations.name: negT_start_ge

declarations.doc: **The local maximum of the run** is `3 ^ a * m + 1`, so in the conjugated variable it is exactly `3 ^ a * m`: the run multiplies `u` by `(3/2) ^ a`.
declarations.name: negT_localMax

declarations.doc: **The decomposition Lemma 1 starts from.** An odd `y ≥ 3` is `2 ^ a * m + 1` with `m` odd and `a = v₂(y - 1) ≥ 1`; the note writes `u = y - 1` and `a = v₂(u)`.
declarations.name: negT_run_decomp

declarations.doc: **Lemma 1 of the note, packaged at an odd start.** For odd `y ≥ 3` there are `a ≥ 1` and `m` odd with `y = 2 ^ a * m + 1` such that the first `a` iterates are odd, the `a`-th is even (so the run has exactly `a` odd steps), the start satisfies `y ≥ 2 ^ a + 1`, and the local maximum is `3 ^ a * m + 1`.
declarations.name: negT_lemma_one

declarations.doc: **The chaining, in integers.** After the run's local maximum `3 ^ a * m + 1`, at least one halving follows; the next local minimum `y'` has `u' = y' - 1` with `2 * u' < 3 ^ a * m`. This is the exact form of the note's `u' < u ^ δ / 2`: no `X₀` enters the constant.
declarations.name: negT_chain_nat

declarations.doc: **The chaining, with the exponent.** `δ = log₂ 3`; for `u = 2 ^ a * m` the local maximum in the conjugated variable is `3 ^ a * m ≤ u ^ δ`, because `2 ^ δ = 3` and `m ≤ m ^ δ`. With the integer half this is the note's Lemma 3, `u' < u ^ δ / 2`.
declarations.name: negT_chain_real

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3 of the note, packaged.** From a local minimum `y = 2 ^ a * m + 1`, with at least one halving after the run carrying the local maximum to the next local minimum `y'`, the conjugated variables obey `u' < u ^ δ / 2` with `u = y - 1`, `u' = y' - 1`, `δ = log₂ 3`. The constant is exact: no verification floor enters it.
declarations.name: negT_lemma_three

declarations.doc: **The sign is the content.** `g 17 = 25`, where the shortcut `3n+1` map gives `26`: a sign flip in `negT` would falsify this, and with it every statement above.
declarations.name: negT_sign_is_minus

declarations.doc: The three known cycles of `g`.
declarations.name: negT_cycle_one

declarations.doc: The `17`-cycle read through Lemma 1: `17 = 2 ^ 4 * 1 + 1`, so the run has four odd steps, `17, 25, 37, 55`, and the local maximum is `82 = 3 ^ 4 * 1 + 1`.
declarations.name: negT_run_at_seventeen

declarations.doc: Lemma 1 at `17`, from the general statement rather than by computation: `a = 4`, `m = 1`.
declarations.name: negT_localMax_seventeen

declarations.doc: **The chaining is tight on the `17`-cycle.** One halving carries the local maximum `82` to the next local minimum `41`, so `u' = 40` against `u = 16`; the integer form of Lemma 3 gives `2 * 40 < 81`, which is the note's `16 → 40` against `16 ^ δ / 2 = 40.5…` with a single unit to spare. A weaker constant than `u ^ δ / 2` would not exclude it.
declarations.name: negT_chain_tight_at_17

declarations.doc: The corner floors satisfy `⌊A + B + ε⌋ - ⌊A⌋ - ⌊B⌋ ∈ {-1, 0, 1, 2}` whenever `|ε| < 1`. Here `A = Δ₁X`, `B = Δ₂X` and `ε = ΔΔX`, so this is the step that needs `|ΔΔX| < 1`.
declarations.name: corner_floor_range

declarations.doc: **`|j| ≤ 3`.** The net offset `j = β₁₂ - β₁ - β₂` combines the corner floor range with the three level-1 carries `κ ∈ {0,1}³`.
declarations.name: offset_abs_le_three

declarations.doc: `β = ⌊ΔX⌋ + κ = ⌊ΔX + θ⌋`: the level-1 carry is `⌊{ΔX} + θ⌋`.
declarations.name: carry_eq_floor_shifted

declarations.doc: **`-1 ≤ j ≤ 2`.** `j = ⌊A+B+ε+θ⌋ - ⌊A+θ⌋ - ⌊B+θ⌋` is `corner_floor_range` at `(A+θ, B+θ, ε-θ)`, and `|ε - θ| < 1` whenever `0 < ε < 1` and `0 ≤ θ < 1`.
declarations.name: offset_range_with_carries

declarations.doc: **`|j| ≤ 2`**, replacing the printed `|j| ≤ 3`.
declarations.name: offset_abs_le_two

declarations.doc: **`|ΔΔX| < 1`**, the hypothesis the offset bound needs. With shifts `d₁ = 2h₁`, `d₂ = 2h₂`, `|ΔΔX| ≤ d₁d₂ sup|X''| = 4h₁h₂·(3/4)P^(-1/2)`, so the condition is exactly the manuscript's `h₁h₂ ≤ P^(1/2)/3` — stated here with `q = P^(1/2)` and strict inequality.
declarations.name: double_difference_lt_one

declarations.doc: **The `β`-product bound.** From `β_i ≤ 3√2 h_i q + 1` with `q = P^(1/2)`, `h_i ≥ 1` and `q ≥ 10`, the product satisfies `β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂ q²`, which is what the manuscript carries: `(3√2)² = 18` is the product of the leading terms, and the `+1`s take it to `19`. `4.25 ≥ 3√2` is the rational substitute. Not an over-quantification, though it separates two variables one `n` determines: both factors are extremal at the same `n = 2P`, `β₁β₂/(h₁h₂P)` attains `18` exactly, and `4.25² = 18.0625` is the whole of the loss. See the note at Lemma 5.1(iii) and `decoration_budget.beta_inventory_attained`.
declarations.name: beta_product_bound

declarations.doc: `3√2 ≤ 4.25`, the rational substitute used above.
declarations.name: three_sqrt_two_le

declarations.doc: **The `β`-part of `G'`.** `(9/16)β₁β₂ s^(-7) ≤ 20 h₁h₂ p^(-3)`, the printed `20 h₁h₂P^(-3/4)`; the constant used is `(9/16)·19 = 10.6875 ≤ 20`.
declarations.name: Gprime_beta_bound

declarations.doc: **The cancellation in `G''`.** `G'' = F''(X)(X')² + F'(X)X''`, and the two `β`-contributions have opposite signs: `81/64` from the first and `-9/32` from the second, leaving `63/64`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_beta_cancellation

declarations.doc: **The printed `25` needs that cancellation.** With `β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂P`, the combined coefficient `63/64` gives `18.7 ≤ 25`; bounding the two `β`-terms separately gives `99/64`, i.e. `29.4`, which exceeds `25`. The manuscript's bound is correct, but its naive derivation is not.
declarations.name: Gsecond_naive_bound_fails

declarations.doc: **The `β`-part of `G''`.** `(63/64)β₁β₂ s^(-11) ≤ 25 h₁h₂ p^(-7)`, the printed `25 h₁h₂P^(-7/4)`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_beta_bound

declarations.doc: **The `j`-part of `G''`.** `(9/32)|j| s^(-5) ≤ 2|j| p^(-5)`, the printed `2|j|P^(-5/4)`; here too the two contributions cancel, `-27/32 + 9/16 = -9/32`.
declarations.name: Gsecond_j_bound

declarations.doc: **The offset term.** `(3/2)|j|A^(1/2)` with `P^(3/2) ≤ A ≤ 3.004 P^(3/2)` lies in `[1.5|j|P^(3/4), 2.6|j|P^(3/4)]`. Written with `w = A^(1/2)` and `p = P^(1/4)`, the hypothesis is `p³ ≤ w ≤ 1.7333 p³`; the manuscript's `2^(3/2)` gives `w ≤ 1.6818 p³`, so `2.6` has room.
declarations.name: offset_term_bounds

declarations.doc: **The second-difference term.** `(3/4)β₁β₂B^(-1/2)` with `9 h₁h₂P ≤ β₁β₂ ≤ 19 h₁h₂P` and `p³ ≤ u ≤ 1.7333 p³` (where `u = B^(1/2)`) lies in `[1.4 h₁h₂P^(1/4), 15 h₁h₂P^(1/4)]`: the lower end is `(3/4)·9/1.7333 = 3.89 ≥ 1.4`, the upper `(3/4)·19 = 14.25 ≤ 15`.
declarations.name: second_difference_term_bounds

declarations.doc: **The run-length arithmetic.** With `A = 2|j|p^(-1)` and `B = 20 h₁h₂ p^(-3)`, and `M = max((|j|+1)p^(-1), h₁h₂p^(-3))`, one has `A ≤ 2M` and `B ≤ 20M`, so `A + B ≤ 22M`. The `22` of the manuscript is exactly `2 + 20`.
declarations.name: run_length_arithmetic

declarations.doc: **The run-length conclusion.** If `G` moves at rate at most `22M`, then over an interval of length `1/(22M)` it moves by at most `1`, so `⌊G⌋` takes at most two values there: runs of `⌊G(n)⌋` have length at least `(1/22)min(P^(1/4)/(|j|+1), P^(3/4)/(h₁h₂))`.
declarations.name: run_length_conclusion

declarations.doc: The even-step charge of a word: an even letter contributes `3` to the power of the odd letters still to come, and every letter doubles what follows. Closed form: the sum over even positions `i` of `3 ^ (o - a_i) * 2 ^ i`, with `a_i` the odd letters before `i`.

declarations.doc: The odd-step constant and the even-step charge differ by the multiplier gap: `wordConst w + 2 ^ |w| = 3 ^ o + evenCharge w`.
declarations.name: wordConst_add_two_pow

declarations.doc: **The affine formula in the `x + 1` coordinate.** Every correction comes from an even step.
declarations.name: two_pow_mul_iter_add_one

declarations.doc: **The Collatz lower envelope**, the mirror of `power_bound_word`: the `+1`s only push up, so `3 ^ o · (x + 1) ≤ 2 ^ d · (C^d(x) + 1)` for every start and every depth.
declarations.name: three_pow_mul_add_one_le

declarations.doc: **The Collatz walk charge, exactly.** On a cycle the surplus `(x + 1)(2 ^ d - 3 ^ o)` is the even-step charge of the word. This is the counterpart of Paper A's finance inequality `n log n (3 ^ o - 2 ^ L) ≤ L 3 ^ o`, as an identity rather than a bound.
declarations.name: cycle_even_charge

declarations.doc: The trivial cycle `1 → 2 → 1` has word `OE`, charge `2`, and `(1+1)(4 - 3) = 2`.
declarations.name: trivial_cycle_charge

declarations.doc: The shortcut map on `ℤ`: `x / 2` on evens, `(3x + 1) / 2` on odds. Agrees with `shortcutC` on `ℕ`, and `3x + 1` is even whenever `x` is odd, so the division is exact on both branches.
declarations.name: shortcutZ

declarations.doc: `shortcutZ` iterated, in the peeled form `C^{k+1}(x) = C^k(C x)`.
declarations.name: shortcutZIter

declarations.name: parityWordZ

declarations.doc: One step of the `ℤ` map, cleared of its division.
declarations.name: two_mul_shortcutZ

declarations.doc: **The affine formula over `ℤ`**, for every integer start: `2 ^ d C^d(x) = 3 ^ o x + wordConst w`.
declarations.name: word_affine_int

declarations.doc: The `ℤ` parity word of depth `d` has length `d`.
declarations.name: parityWordZ_length

declarations.doc: The `x + 1` form over `ℤ`: `2 ^ d (C^d x + 1) = 3 ^ o (x + 1) + evenCharge w`.
declarations.name: two_pow_mul_iter_add_one_int

declarations.doc: **The cycle equation over `ℤ`**: `(x + 1)(2 ^ d - 3 ^ o) = evenCharge w` on every integer cycle.
declarations.name: cycle_equation_int

declarations.doc: **Negative cycles expand.** A cycle of the `ℤ` map at `x ≤ -2` of positive length has `2 ^ d < 3 ^ o` -- Juggler's sign -- because the right-hand side of the cycle equation is positive (the word has an even letter, else the cycle would sit at `-1`) and `x + 1 < 0`.
declarations.name: neg_cycle_expanding

declarations.doc: **The cycle equation in `ℕ`**, for positive cycles: `(x + 1)(2 ^ d - 3 ^ o) = evenCharge w`, hence `2 ^ d - 3 ^ o` divides the even-step charge of the word.
declarations.name: cycle_equation

declarations.doc: **The converse**: a start whose parity word satisfies the cycle equation returns. Together with `cycle_equation` this is the exact cycle condition as a statement about the word alone, once the word is realised: `2 ^ d - 3 ^ o` divides `evenCharge w` with the quotient `x + 1`.
declarations.name: cycle_of_equation

declarations.doc: **A contracting prefix bounds the minimum by its own rational cycle value.** If the orbit has not dropped below `x` by step `j`, then `(x + 1)(2 ^ j - 3 ^ a_j) ≤ evenCharge (prefix)`; so at a cycle minimum every contracting prefix caps `x + 1` by `evenCharge / (2 ^ j - 3 ^ a_j)`.
declarations.name: prefix_bound_of_min

declarations.doc: The `-17` word has seven odd and four even letters, and `2 ^ 11 < 3 ^ 7`: an expanding word of length `11` with four evens, the least length Paper A's Theorem 3.22 allows a Juggler cycle.
declarations.name: neg_seventeen_word_expanding

declarations.doc: A prefix of the `ℤ` word is the word of the prefix.
declarations.name: parityWordZ_take

declarations.doc: **A negative cycle word, read at its least `|x|`, has no contracting prefix.** If `x ≤ -2` and no iterate up to `K` lies closer to zero than `x`, then `2 ^ j ≤ 3 ^ a_j` for every `j ≤ K`. Exact: the even steps only subtract, so an expanding multiplier is the only way to stay away from zero.
declarations.name: neg_prefix_noncontracting

declarations.doc: **The word-level twin, exactly.** A negative cycle of the `ℤ` map of positive length, read at its least `|x|`, has a word that is prefix-noncontracting and expanding -- the Juggler cycle-word shape of Paper A, with no `delta` exception on this side.
declarations.name: neg_cycle_word_is_juggler_shape

declarations.doc: `-17` is the element of least `|x|` on its cycle, so the twin applies to it.
declarations.name: neg_seventeen_is_least

declarations.doc: Each prefix of `w`, extended in front by `m` letters carrying `a` odd ones, non-contracting, gives `2 ^ (m + 1) · evenCharge w ≤ (|w| - o) · 3 ^ (a + o)`.
declarations.name: evenCharge_le_aux

declarations.doc: **Half the multiplier per even letter.** On a word with no contracting prefix, `2 · evenCharge w ≤ (|w| - o) · 3 ^ o`: the even step at position `i` contributes `3 ^ (o - a_i) · 2 ^ i = 3 ^ o · 2 ^ (-h_i)` with height `h_i = a_i log2 3 - i ≥ 1`, because the prefix of length `i + 1` is non-contracting.
declarations.name: two_mul_evenCharge_le

declarations.doc: **The negative-cycle finance, uniformly.** On a cycle of the `ℤ` map at `x ≤ -2`, read at its least `|x|`: `2 (|x| - 1)(3 ^ o - 2 ^ K) ≤ (K - o) 3 ^ o`. Paper A's finance inequality on the other side of the linear form, with the even steps charged at `1/2` each; equivalently `|x| - 1 ≤ (K - o) / (2 θ_J)` with `θ_J = 1 - 2 ^ K / 3 ^ o`.

declarations.doc: Every cycle maximum carries a canonical peak descent `x --OE^r--> p` with `p < x`. Determined by the maximum, not by a itinerary search.

declarations.doc: Closed peak-ascent accounting: the peak lower cell plus the ascent envelope from `p` to `x` give `3^{o+1} ≥ 2^{k+r+1}`. This is the existing top-ascent law after appending the final `O`.
declarations.name: peak_ascent_scale

declarations.doc: The peak predecessor is reached by a prefix of the top ascent. Financing `OE^r` recovers the existing superquadratic law on that ascent, not a stronger envelope.
declarations.name: cycle_peak_finance

declarations.doc: Dual of `exists_first_odd_iterate`.
declarations.name: exists_first_even_iterate

declarations.doc: Top-window lower bound is strict: `p` odd and `M` even forbid equality `M = p^{2^r}`. Parity, not an envelope.
declarations.name: cycle_top_window_strict

declarations.doc: A cycle maximum cannot also be a cycle minimum.
declarations.name: cycleMax_not_cycleMin

declarations.doc: On a cycle maximum the rotated minimum satisfies `m^2 < M`. The laboratory sharpening is `cycleMax_min_succ_sq_le`.
declarations.name: cycleMax_min_sq_lt

declarations.doc: Distinguished cycle order: minimum, top landing, peak predecessor, maximum. The rotation witness is included so the laboratory sharpening `(m+1)^2 ≤ M` is a one-line corollary. Scale compositions beyond this package are envelope repackaging.
declarations.name: cycle_distinguished_order

declarations.doc: Cyclic closure keeps the remainders: `∑ρ + even gaps = odd gaps`. This is not the exponent envelope.
declarations.name: cycle_remainder_balance

declarations.doc: Dropping every remainder recovers the ordinary itinerary envelope.

declarations.doc: All-zero remainders are incompatible with a nontrivial cycle.

declarations.doc: Peak odd remainder is positive: `M` even and `x` odd forbid `x^3 = M^2`.
declarations.name: cycleMax_pred_cube_strict

declarations.doc: The dyadic one-step-preimage logarithm bound: if `z < (y+1)^2` then `log z ≤ 2 log y + 2/y`. The only analytic input of the finance inequality (`log(1+u) ≤ u`).
declarations.name: log_le_two_log_add

declarations.doc: Even step: `log x ≤ 2 log T(x) + 2/T(x)`.
declarations.name: log_step_even

declarations.doc: Odd step: `3 log x ≤ 2 log T(x) + 2/T(x)`.
declarations.name: log_step_odd

declarations.doc: The unrolled financing envelope along a `CycleMin` prefix: `3^{o_k} log n ≤ 2^k log x_k + k 3^{o_k} / n`. Division-free induction; each step spends one dyadic one-step-preimage logarithm bound and one prefix non-contraction fact.
declarations.name: cycleMin_log_envelope

declarations.doc: **Cycle finance inequality.** For any cycle taken at its minimum: `n log n (3^o - 2^L) ≤ L 3^o`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_finance

declarations.doc: On a `CycleMin`, every iterate through one period is at least two (the start is, and later states are at least the start).
declarations.name: cycleMin_iterate_ge_two

declarations.doc: Inv-sum envelope: each dyadic one-step-preimage defect is kept as `1/x_{i+1}` instead of being replaced by `1/n`. At `k = L` this is `(3^o - 2^L) log n ≤ 3^o ∑ 1/x_i`. Paper A Corollary 4.4c.
declarations.name: cycleMin_log_envelope_inv

declarations.doc: **Inv-sum finance inequality.** Same one-step-preimage-log defects as `cycleMin_finance`, remainders kept as `1/x_{i+1}`. `(3^o - 2^L) log n ≤ 3^o ∑ 1/x_i`.

declarations.doc: Reusable certificate: a deficit larger than the formal exponent gap forces `m < n` for `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: power_bound_compensated_contracts

declarations.doc: `−log(1−t) ≤ 1.2·t` for `0 ≤ t ≤ 1/6` — the paper's `6/5` majorant of `−log(1−δ)/δ` on `[0,1/6]`. Instance of the parameterized majorant `neg_log_one_sub_le_mul` at `c = 6/5`.
declarations.name: neg_log_one_sub_le_sixth

declarations.doc: Even step, upper side: `log T(x) ≤ (1/2)·log x` for even `x ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_even_le

declarations.doc: Odd step, upper side: `log T(x) ≤ (3/2)·log x` for odd `x ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_odd_le

declarations.doc: Even step, lower side in image form: for even `x ≥ 441`, `log T(x) ≥ (1/2)·log x − 1.2/T(x)`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_even_ge_sub

declarations.doc: Odd step, lower side in image form: for odd `x ≥ 9`, `log T(x) ≥ (3/2)·log x − 1.2/T(x)`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_odd_ge_sub

declarations.doc: On a minimum-based cycle, iterated logs never exceed the walk weight times the base log: `log x_k ≤ w_k·log n`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_log_le_weight

declarations.doc: Accumulated defect charge along the first `k` steps, priced at the images: `C_k = Σ_{i<k} 1.2·log n/(x_{i+1}·log x_{i+1})`. Depends only on the trajectory, not on the itinerary.
declarations.name: prefixCharge

declarations.doc: One-step recurrence for the running prefix charge.
declarations.name: prefixCharge_succ

declarations.doc: Closed sum form of the prefix charge.
declarations.name: prefixCharge_eq

declarations.doc: Charged transport invariant: `w_k·(log n − C_k) ≤ log x_k` with the running defect charge.
declarations.name: cycleMin_charge_prefix

declarations.doc: **Defect-sum finance inequality** (the certified identity of Paper A Theorem 4.6, Lean form): on a minimum-based cycle with minimum `n ≥ 400`, `1 − 2^L/3^o ≤ (6/5) · Σ_k 1/(x_k·log x_k)`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_defect_finance

declarations.doc: **The walk-charge kill criterion** (Paper A Theorem 5.9 mechanism, Lean form): every minimum-based cycle at `n ≥ 400` with positive reduced log-base `ν = log n − D` must satisfy `1 − 2^L/3^o ≤ (6/5) · Σ_k g(hugWeight k)` with the charge evaluated at the reduced base. The kill tables verify the numeric failure of this inequality per surviving length; that evaluation stays verified computation, the implication is Lean.
declarations.name: cycleMin_hug_kill_criterion

declarations.doc: Index of the first positive local remainder, or `w.length` if none.
declarations.name: firstDefectFrom

declarations.doc: Prefix remainders vanish; the selected index is the first positive one.
declarations.name: firstDefect_spec

declarations.doc: The prefix before the first defect is completely tight.
declarations.name: firstDefect_prefix_tight

declarations.doc: The tight prefix is an even or odd power-of-two tower.
declarations.name: firstDefect_prefix_extremal

declarations.doc: Canonical first-defect form of `ρ_j^{2^j} ≤ Δ`.
declarations.name: firstDefect_contribution

declarations.doc: A later even letter cannot follow a completely tight odd run.
declarations.name: firstDefect_lt_of_odd_run_then_even

declarations.doc: Exact cubic lift of an already-inserted defect.
declarations.name: odd_defect_lift

declarations.doc: Universal odd-step lower bound. The factor `3` is sharp as `D/scale → 0`.
declarations.name: odd_defect_lift_lower_bound

declarations.doc: Suffix lift of an already-inserted defect. Later remainders are dropped.
declarations.name: amplifyDefect

declarations.doc: After the first defect, the remaining suffix cannot shrink that contribution below the zero-remainder lift.
declarations.name: global_defect_lower_bound

declarations.doc: Normalized pair `(D, current^{2^k})`. The ratio is the natural dimensionless defect; Lean keeps both sides as natural numbers.
declarations.name: normalizedDefect

declarations.doc: Tight even preserves the pair. Tight odd cubes the scale and replaces `D` by the cubic lift.
declarations.name: normalizedDefect_step

declarations.doc: Scale-free residue bound: an even successor of an `x ≡ 2 (mod 4)` state forces remainder at least `2`.
declarations.name: conditional_remainder_lower_bound

declarations.doc: Conditional lower bound for the previously difficult mixed class `OOE`. This does not claim the bound exceeds the formal surplus.
declarations.name: expanding_defect_lower_bound

declarations.doc: Negative control: `Δ > n^{3^o} - n^{2^k}` is exactly `T_w(n) < n`.
declarations.name: global_defect_le_surplus_of_expanding

declarations.doc: **Per-cell bound.** On an interval, any value of `f` differs from the mean of `f` there by at most the variation of `f` there. This is the whole analytic content of Denjoy–Koksma.
declarations.name: value_sub_mean_le_variation

declarations.doc: **Variation is additive along a monotone chain of cut points.** Mathlib has the binary `eVariationOn.Icc_add_Icc`; this is the `n`-fold form.
declarations.name: sum_eVariationOn_Icc

declarations.doc: **Denjoy–Koksma, abstract form.** If one sample point is taken from each of the `n` cells of a monotone chain, the sample sum differs from the integral by at most the total variation. No rotation and no number theory: the arithmetic of the orbit enters only through the hypothesis that the points hit the cells one apiece.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_abstract

declarations.doc: **Denjoy–Koksma on the unit interval, uniform cells.** With one sample point in each of the `q` cells `[i/q, (i+1)/q]`, the sample sum differs from `q` times the integral by at most the sum of the cell variations. This is the shape Theorem 5.7 of Paper A applies per block.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_unit

declarations.doc: The cell the `k`-th orbit point lands in: `k·p mod q`, shifted back one when `δ = θ − p/q` is negative.
declarations.name: orbitCell

declarations.doc: The cell map is injective on `range q`, because `p` is invertible mod `q`.
declarations.name: orbitCell_inj

declarations.doc: **The orbit visits each cell once.** With cells anchored at `x`, the `k`-th orbit point lies in cell `orbitCell p q neg k`, once shifted by an integer.
declarations.name: orbit_mem_cell

declarations.doc: **Denjoy–Koksma with the cells reached through a map.** The `n` sample points are indexed by `k`, and `τ k` names the cell point `k` lands in; injectivity of `τ` on `range n` is what replaces "one point per cell". This is the form a rotation supplies, and taking it avoids having to invert the permutation.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_cellmap

declarations.doc: **Denjoy–Koksma for the rotation.** This is the inequality Paper A's Section 5.5 states and marks KNOWN: for a one-periodic `f` of bounded variation and a rational `p/q` within `1/q²` of `θ`, the ergodic sum of length `q` differs from `q` times the mean by at most the total variation, uniformly in the starting phase `x`.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_rotation

declarations.doc: **The mean over the window is the mean over `[0,1]`**, so this is Theorem 5.7's `C_*`: the ergodic sum of length `q` differs from `q·C_*` by at most the variation.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_rotation_mean

declarations.doc: **Blocks compose, because Denjoy–Koksma is uniform in the starting phase.** This is the step Paper A's Theorem 5.7 makes in prose: a length `L = Σ bⱼqⱼ` is cut into consecutive blocks whose starting phases differ, each block inherits whatever phase its predecessor left, and the inequality applies to each regardless. Repeating a pair in the list is the `bⱼ`. `V` is any uniform bound on the variation over a window of length one — for a one-periodic observable this is the variation on the circle, and for Paper A's `F` it is `2`.
declarations.name: denjoy_koksma_blocks

declarations.doc: The six coefficients of Step B, in the order they are printed: `n^(27/8)`, `m n^(15/8)`, `m^2 n^(3/8)`, `v n^(9/8)`, `v m n^(-3/8)`, `v m^2 n^(-15/8)`.
declarations.name: stepB

declarations.doc: At the base point `m = n^(3/2)`, `v = n^(9/4)` every term is a multiple of `n^(27/8)` and the six coefficients sum to `1`: the expansion reproduces `v^(3/2)` exactly there.
declarations.name: stepB_exact_at_base

declarations.doc: The `m`-derivative vanishes at the base point. It must: `v^(3/2)` does not depend on `m`, so the printed expansion would be wrong if it did not.
declarations.name: stepB_m_derivative_vanishes

declarations.doc: The total smooth `v`-coefficient is `(3/2) n^(9/8)`, so the monomial weight of Theorem 5.3 is `c = (3k/4) nu^(9/8)`. This is the identity printed in Step B.
declarations.name: stepB_v_coefficient

declarations.doc: The `m`-block, rewritten in `e`, is `-1/2 - (9/8)e - (45/64)e^2`.
declarations.name: stepB_m_block_in_epsilon

declarations.doc: The `v`-coefficient block, rewritten in `e`, is `3/2 + (9/8)e - (9/64)e^2`.
declarations.name: stepB_v_block_in_epsilon

declarations.doc: The `m`-block is the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of `-(1/2)(1+e)^(9/4)`: binomial coefficients `1, 9/4, (9/4)(5/4)/2 = 45/32` scaled by `-1/2`.
declarations.name: stepB_m_block_is_taylor

declarations.doc: The `v`-coefficient block is the degree-2 Taylor polynomial of `(3/2)(1+e)^(3/4)`: binomial coefficients `1, 3/4, (3/4)(-1/4)/2 = -3/32` scaled by `3/2`.
declarations.name: stepB_v_block_is_taylor

declarations.doc: The structural identity behind all of it: with `t2 = m^(3/2) - v`, `v^(3/2) = m^(9/4) - (3/2) m^(3/4) t2 + O(m^(-3/4))`, and eliminating `t2` gives `-(1/2) m^(9/4) + (3/2) m^(3/4) v`. Here as an identity in the two blocks, `M` standing for `m^(3/4)`, so that `m^(3/2) = M^2` and `m^(9/4) = M^3`.
declarations.name: stepB_structure

declarations.doc: Offset branches. The frozen-shape offset monomial `(9/8) k j nu^(15/8)` has curvature `(9/8)(15/8)(7/8) = 945/512`, the frozen kernel anchor is `27/16 = 864/512`, and the surviving offset is the difference `81/512`.
declarations.name: stepE_offset_survivor

declarations.doc: The total `theta`-coefficient `B = (27/32) k j nu^(3/8)` is `3/2` times the bare-kernel value `9/16`, and is not the moving-gap value `45/32`.
declarations.name: stepE_B_ratio

declarations.doc: The window-centre mode carries `B * X'' = (27/32)(3/4) = 81/128 = 324/512`, and the offset composite is single-signed: `81/512 - 324/512 = -243/512 <> 0`.
declarations.name: stepE_offset_composite

declarations.doc: The printed range `lambda_a' in [0.40, 0.52] k|j| P^(-1/8)` holds on a dyadic block: `243/512 = 0.4746` and `nu^(-1/8)` ranges over `[2^(-1/8), 1)`, inside `[0.917, 1]`.
declarations.name: stepE_lambda_a_range

declarations.doc: Zero-offset branches. `lambda_0' = (1095/1024) k h1 h2 nu^(-5/8)` and `nu^(-5/8)` ranges over `[2^(-5/8), 1)`, inside `[0.648, 1]`; the printed range `[0.60, 1.25]` contains the result.
declarations.name: stepE_lambda_0_range

declarations.doc: The interpolant coefficient scales exactly with the anchor it is built from: replacing `1215/1024` by `1095/1024` sends `b = -405/176` to `b' = -365/176`.
declarations.name: stepE_b_scales_with_anchor

declarations.doc: `S <= max(60 lambda_0', lambda_0', |w| P^(-1/2)) <= 65 P^(-1/2)` under (C1) `k h1 h2 <= P^(1/8)` and `|w| <= 2`; the paper prints the rounder `80`.
declarations.name: stepE_S_bound

declarations.doc: The `j = 0` middle band takes `V = (1/12) S^(1/2) P^(-11/24)` at `S >= 0.60 P^(-5/8)`, so `V >= 0.064 P^(-37/48)` -- and **not** `0.065`, which the draft printed. Squaring avoids the square root.
declarations.name: stepE_j0_V_constant

declarations.doc: Lemma 6.2's exponent bookkeeping: `m^(9/8)` at `X = n^(3/2)` is `n^(27/16)` with sawtooth coefficient exponent `3/16`, and `v^(1/4)` is `n^(9/16)`.
declarations.name: lemma62_exponents

declarations.doc: The residual `theta`-coefficient after the window expansion: `27k/32 - 9k/16 = 9k/32`, so one slow sawtooth survives.
declarations.name: oeoe_C_net

declarations.doc: Its window-centre `X`-mode has curvature `(9/32)(3/4) = 27/128 = 216/1024`.
declarations.name: oeoe_window_curvature

declarations.doc: The leading `n^(27/16)` coefficient of the combined phase is `k/2 - 3k/4`.
declarations.name: oeoe_leading_coefficient

declarations.doc: Its curvature is `-(1/4)(27/16)(11/16) = -297/1024`, the exponent dropping from `27/16` to `-5/16`.
declarations.name: oeoe_leading_curvature

declarations.doc: The composite does not vanish: `-297/1024 + 216/1024 = -81/1024 <> 0`. This is what makes the curvature single-signed, hence Lemma 3.3 applicable.
declarations.name: oeoe_composite_nonzero

declarations.doc: The superseded balance. `J^(1/2) P^(27/32) = P/J` is struck at `J = P^(5/48)` and gives `P^(43/48)`. It belongs to the proof that dropped the `jY/2` mode of the four-wave product and centered a Fourier frequency dynamically; kept because the manuscript's erratum at Theorem 6.3 quotes both ends of the correction.
declarations.name: oeoe_balance_superseded

declarations.doc: The surviving balance. Against the `1/|k|` Vaaler weights, truncation at `P^a` costs `P^(-a)` while the mixed term costs `P^(-1/32 + a/2)`; the two meet at `a = 1/48`, so the saving is `P^(-1/48)` and the exponent `47/48`.
declarations.name: oeoe_balance

declarations.doc: Corollary 6.4: the five disjoint certificate classes `E`, `OE`, `OOEE`, `OOOEE`, `OOEOE` have densities summing to `7/8`.
declarations.name: cor64_density

declarations.doc: The error is the worse of the two fifth-letter exponents, and `1 - 1/96` is the worse of them. After the Theorem 6.3 erratum the margin is one ninety-sixth: `47/48 = 94/96` against `95/96`, where the superseded `43/48 = 86/96` had nine.
declarations.name: cor64_error_exponent

declarations.doc: And the margin itself, which the manuscript now quotes.
declarations.name: cor64_error_margin

declarations.doc: **Step B's discard.** With `|err| <= (3/4) n^(-9/8)` in the phase `(k/2) v^(3/2)`, a block costs `2 pi (k/2)(3/4) P^(-9/8) * P = (3 pi k/4) P^(-1/8)`, which at `k <= 2 P^(1/96)` is under one unit as soon as `4.72 P^(-11/96) <= 1`. In `P = t^96` that is `4.72 <= t^11`, which holds from `t >= 1.16`. An earlier draft printed this cost as `<= 7 P^(7/8)`, which multiplied by the block length twice and additionally needed `k <= 7/(2 pi) = 1.11`.
declarations.name: stepB_discard

declarations.doc: **Paid for.** The Stage 5 collision-band sum is `3 R_0^(1/2) P^(3/4)`, which must stay inside the theorem's own `P^(23/24)`. At `a = 5/16` that is `3 P^(29/32) <= P^(23/24)`, i.e. `3 <= P^(5/96) = t^5`, from `t >= 1.25` (`P >= 2.0e9`).
declarations.name: row_st2_collision

declarations.doc: **Paid for.** The `q''` curvature of Step 5b(a) is `(1.85 k h P^(1/8) + R_0) * 3|j| P^(-5/4)`, whose ratio to the main curvature `0.35 P^(-3/4)` must clear the margin `1/4`. In `t` that is `126.86 t^28 + 68.57 t^30 <= t^48`; dividing by `t^28` gives the form below, which holds from `t >= 1.32` (`P >= 3.8e11`, still two and a half orders under `P_0`).
declarations.name: row_st5b_qpp

declarations.doc: **Bought.** Theorem 6.3's fifth-letter Lemma 3.7 window is opened at `T = R_0` against `|C| <= (9/8) 2^(3/16) P^(19/96)`, and its hypothesis `T >= 8(1 + |C|)` reads `8 + 10.25 t^19 <= t^30` at `a = 5/16`, since `8 * (9/8) * 2^(3/16) = 10.2491 <= 10.25`. It holds from `t >= 1.24` (`P >= 9.3e8`).
declarations.name: row_t63_window

declarations.doc: **Bought, and this is the one that binds.** The same window's *flat cost* is `8(1 + |C|)/T` per point, which over a block must stay inside `P^(1-1/96)`. That reads `8 t + 10.25 t^20 <= t^30`, holding from `t >= 1.27` (`P >= 9.2e9`). At `a = 1/4` the same line is `8 t + 10.25 t^20 <= t^24`, which does not hold until `1.8e24` --- ten orders above `P_0`, and the real reason Stage 2 is run at `P^(5/16)`.
declarations.name: row_t63_flat

declarations.doc: The superseded truncation `a = 1/4` really does fail, and it fails at `P_0`. There `t = P_0^(1/96) <= 1.4`, so `t^5 <= 5.38` and `t^24 = t^19 * t^5` cannot reach `10.25 t^19`, let alone `8 + 10.25 t^19`. This is the window hypothesis at `T = P^(1/4)`; the flat cost at that truncation fails by ten orders more.
declarations.name: row_t63_window_fails_at_quarter

declarations.doc: **Claim D of Lemma 5.2(ii) → (i).** Every index of the Claim C sum must be a legal shift for part (i), i.e. `h_3 <= P^(1/8)`, from `h_3 <= t^(1/3) P^(1/12)`. The exponent gap is `1/8 - 7/72 = 1/36`, so whatever constant stands in front of `P^(7/72)` is paid at the thirty-sixth power, and which bound on `t` is carried decides the row entirely: * the individual `|q_d| <= 4 P^(1/24)` over the four elements of `D` gives `|t| <= 16 P^(1/24)`, hence `16^(1/3) < 2.52` and a threshold `16^12 = 2.8e14` --- which would be the binding row of the whole paper; * the total frequency bound `|t| <= 3 P^(1/24)`, which Theorem 5.3 Step 4 (the only place (ii) is invoked) supplies because the wave modes arrive one per expansion layer from three layers at truncation `J_2 = P^(1/24)`, gives `3^(1/3) < 1.45` and a threshold `3^12 = 5.3e5`. Lemma 5.2(ii) carries the second as a hypothesis. In `P = t^72` the two exponents become `7` and `9`, so the requirement is `1.45 <= t^2`, holding from `t >= 1.205` (`P >= 6.8e5`).
declarations.name: claimD_shift_range

declarations.doc: The loose bound really would have cost a factor 3.15 in `P_0`: with `2.52` in front, the comparison fails at `P_0 = 8.95e13`, where `t = P_0^(1/72) <= 1.58` and `t^2 <= 2.4964 < 2.52`.
declarations.name: claimD_loose_bound_fails_at_P0

declarations.doc: Step 3(a)'s flat cost is `23 P^(19/24)`, which sits inside the Step 6 budget `P^(23/24)` from `23^6 = 1.5e8`, but **not** inside `P^(7/8)`, which an earlier draft printed and which would need `23^12 = 2.2e16`. In `P = t^24`: `23 t^19 <= t^23`.
declarations.name: st3a_flat_cost

declarations.doc: The standard additive character `e(θ) = exp(2πiθ)`.
declarations.name: e

declarations.doc: `e` kills the integers, so it is `1`-periodic.
declarations.name: e_intCast

declarations.doc: The stationary point of `α M^{3/2} - νM`: writing `M = s²` with `s ≥ 0`, the phase derivative `(3/2)αs` equals `ν` exactly at `s = 2ν/(3α)`.
declarations.name: stationary_point

declarations.doc: **The dual phase.** At the stationary point `M_ν = s²`, `s = 2ν/(3α)`, the Legendre value `α M_ν^{3/2} - ν M_ν` equals `-4ν³/(27α²)`: a cubic in the dual variable with coefficient rational whenever `α` is.
declarations.name: dual_phase

declarations.doc: `(s²)^{3/2} = s³` for `s ≥ 0`: the half-power bookkeeping that lets `dual_phase` be stated in the original variable `M = s²`.
declarations.name: rpow_three_halves_of_sq

declarations.doc: **The dual phase in the original variable.** For `α > 0`, `ν ≥ 0` and `M_ν = (2ν/(3α))²`, the phase `α M^{3/2} - νM` takes the value `-4ν³/(27α²)` at `M_ν`. This is `dual_phase` with the half-power written as a half-power.
declarations.name: dual_phase_rpow

declarations.doc: At `α = 1/2` the dual phase is `-16ν³/27`: modulus `27`.
declarations.name: dual_phase_half

declarations.doc: The primitive `27`-th root of unity used by the dual sum.
declarations.name: zeta27

declarations.doc: Powers of `ζ` only see the exponent modulo `27`.
declarations.name: zeta27_pow_mod

declarations.doc: `ζ⁹` is a primitive cube root of unity, so `1 + ζ⁹ + ζ¹⁸ = 0`. This is the whole reason the complete cubic sum is real and equal to `9`.
declarations.name: zeta27_nine_sum

declarations.doc: Each term of the dual sum, as a power of `ζ` with reduced exponent.
declarations.name: dual_term

declarations.doc: **The complete cubic Gauss sum of the depth-one dual is `9`.** `∑_{r mod 27} e(-16r³/27) = 9`. Nine residues cube to `0`, and the remaining eighteen contribute two triples in arithmetic progression of difference `9`, each killed by `zeta27_nine_sum`.
declarations.name: completeCubicSum_eq_nine

declarations.doc: The constant the note prints, `(4√8/27)(3/4)^{3/2}`, written with the half-power expanded.
declarations.name: depthOneConstant

declarations.doc: `depthOneConstant` is the constant the note prints, half-power and all.
declarations.name: depthOneConstant_eq_printed

declarations.doc: **The constant is exactly `√6/9`.** Numerically `0.2721655…`, matching the four digits the note measures.
declarations.name: depthOneConstant_eq_sqrt_six_div_nine

declarations.doc: Reindexing a complete sum by an invertible affine substitution. This is the step the note calls "`2ν+1` runs over a complete residue system".
declarations.name: sum_affine_reindex

declarations.doc: `2` is invertible modulo `27k²` whenever `k` is odd: the modulus of the twisted dual sum is odd, so the half-integer shift is a permutation.
declarations.name: two_isUnit

declarations.doc: The trap in one line: at the singular mode a divided bound does not bound `x`, it kills it.
declarations.name: le_one_div_zero_iff

declarations.doc: Away from the singular mode the multiplicative and divided forms are the same bound.
declarations.name: mul_le_one_iff_le_one_div

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.7's display is false at its own singular mode.** With `π|u+B| = 0` the printed `min` collapses to `0`, so read literally the display asserts that the coefficient vanishes at the one mode where it is largest. Witness: a coefficient of modulus `1` meets both branches of the intended bound and violates the printed one.
declarations.name: window_divided_form_fails_at_singular_mode

declarations.doc: **And is the same bound everywhere else.** Off the singular mode the multiplicative pair is exactly the printed `min`, so nothing is lost by stating Lemma 3.7 the safe way.
declarations.name: window_forms_agree

declarations.doc: **Weight form.** `CircleMethod.aux_sum_min_le` abstracts Vaughan's Lemma 2.2 over an arbitrary weight rather than over the `min`, because after Weyl differencing the inner sums have shift-dependent lengths and a fixed-length statement cannot be applied to them. Paper B differences twice (`H₁ = P^(1/48)`, `H₂ = P^(1/24)`), so its window sums want the same abstraction: a `min`-bounded weight satisfies the three hypotheses that form takes, the third multiplicative for the reason above.
declarations.name: weight_form_of_min_bound

declarations.doc: Even `n` maps to `Nat.sqrt n`; odd `n` maps to `Nat.sqrt (n^3)`.
declarations.name: floorPower

declarations.doc: On an even state `J` is the integer square root.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_eq

declarations.doc: On an odd state `J` is `⌊√(n³)⌋`, the integer form of `⌊n^{3/2}⌋`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_eq

declarations.doc: `J` does not leave the positive integers.
declarations.name: floorPower_pos

declarations.doc: Integer obstruction: `k^4 ≤ n^3` and `n ≥ 2` forbid `k ≥ n`. This is iterated `Nat.sqrt` of `n^3`, not `T^2` on the odd-to-odd branch.
declarations.name: sqrt_sqrt_n_cubed_lt

declarations.doc: On the odd-to-even branch, `T^2(n) < n`. Not a halt theorem for the full map.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_even_two_step_lt

declarations.doc: Integer comparison: `(n+1)^2 ≤ n^3` for `n ≥ 3`. Threshold for odd-branch growth.
declarations.name: succ_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: On the odd branch, `n ≥ 3` implies `T(n) > n`. Independent of the parity of `T(n)`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_gt

declarations.doc: The odd branch is nondecreasing: `k ≤ T(k)` when `k` is odd and positive.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_nondecreasing

declarations.doc: On the odd-to-odd branch with `n ≥ 3`, `T^2(n) > n`. Dual of `floorPower_odd_even_two_step_lt`. Not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_odd_two_step_gt

declarations.doc: Combined odd-state two-step direction for `n ≥ 3`. Not a macro-transition law, not a halt theorem, and not a divergence theorem. The case `n = 1` is excluded: `floorPower 1 = 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_macro_direction

declarations.doc: Even branch: `T(n)^2 ≤ n`. Exact floor bound, not a real square root.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_sq_le

declarations.doc: Odd branch: `T(n)^2 ≤ n^3`. Exact floor bound, not a real 3/2-power.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: Odd squares attain the one-step envelope: odd `m` implies `T(m^2)^2 = (m^2)^3`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_eq_cube_of_sq

declarations.doc: Smallest mixed-equality witness: word `O` at `n=9`.
declarations.name: floorPower_nine_odd_eq

declarations.doc: Packet seed: `T(13) = 46`.
declarations.name: floorPower_thirteen_step

declarations.doc: Named expansion of the OOOEE envelope `n5 ^ 32 ≤ n ^ 27`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooee_pow_chain

declarations.doc: Even-step composition of a square upper bound.
declarations.name: pow_sq_le

declarations.doc: Odd-step composition of a square-vs-cube upper bound.
declarations.name: pow_sq_le_cube

declarations.doc: For `n ≥ 2`, a strictly larger exponent yields a strictly larger power.
declarations.name: pow_lt_of_two_le

declarations.doc: Weak one-sided bound `m^{2^k} ≤ n^{3^o}`. Equality is allowed.
declarations.name: PowerBound

declarations.doc: Free-exponent envelope `x^A ≤ n^B`. `PowerBound` is the special case `A = 2^k`, `B = 3^o`. Word algebra only.

declarations.doc: Even letter: `(A, B) → (2A, B)` from `T(x)^2 ≤ x`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.even

declarations.doc: Odd letter: `(A, B) → (2A, 3B)` from `T(x)^2 ≤ x^3`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.odd

declarations.doc: Empty-itinerary envelope: `n^1 ≤ n^1`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.refl

declarations.doc: One realized letter.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.map_letter

declarations.doc: Compose an envelope along a realized itinerary.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.map_itinerary

declarations.doc: Word envelope from `map_itinerary` on `refl`.
declarations.name: EnvelopeState.of_follows

declarations.doc: Weak composition: every realized finite itinerary obeys the one-sided bound.

declarations.doc: Unfolded form of `power_bound_follows`. Naming alias only.
declarations.name: power_bound_word

declarations.doc: Repeated realized `OE` blocks: `T^{2r}(x)^{4^r} ≤ x^{3^r}`.
declarations.name: repeated_oe_scale

declarations.doc: Cell comparison: `x^A ≤ n^B` and `B < k·A` force `x < n^k`.
declarations.name: envelope_lt_pow

declarations.doc: Word-stat form: `3^{oddCount w} < k · 2^{|w|}` yields `T_w(n) < n^k`. Implemented by `EnvelopeState.of_follows`. `power_bound_contracts` is the `k = 1` case.
declarations.name: power_bound_lt_pow

declarations.doc: Strict block contraction from the exponent gap. Domain `n ≥ 2`. The `k = 1` case of `power_bound_lt_pow`. Not a claim that every trajectory meets a negative-drift word.
declarations.name: power_bound_contracts

declarations.doc: On the OOOEE branch itinerary, `T^5(n) < n` for `n ≥ 2`. Wrapper of `floorPower_oooee_of_follows`. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooee_five_step_lt

declarations.doc: Power comparison for the OOOEEEOO floor-power block: five odd steps and three even steps give `n8 ^ 256 ≤ n ^ 243`. Canonical exponents of the itinerary exponent `243/256`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooeeeoo_pow_chain

declarations.doc: On the OOOEEEOO branch itinerary, `T^8(n) < n` for `n ≥ 2`. Wrapper of `floorPower_oooeeeoo_of_follows`. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: floorPower_oooeeeoo_eight_step_lt

declarations.doc: An all-even realized itinerary of length `k ≥ 1` contracts for `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: even_itinerary_contracts

declarations.doc: Even-run envelope: `T^r(m)^{2^r} ≤ m`. No minimality.
declarations.name: even_run_pow_le

declarations.doc: An all-odd realized itinerary of length `k ≥ 1` expands for `n ≥ 3`.
declarations.name: odd_itinerary_expands

declarations.doc: A realized return to `x ≥ 2` forces `2^r ≤ 3^o`.
declarations.name: cycle_envelope

declarations.doc: Equality `2^r = 3^o` is impossible for a nonempty itinerary, so every nontrivial cycle is strictly expanding in the exponent.
declarations.name: cycle_strict_envelope

declarations.doc: Contracting words cannot close a cycle.
declarations.name: cycle_not_contracting

declarations.doc: Even branch: `T(n)^2 = n` iff `n` is a perfect square.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_sq_eq_iff_square

declarations.doc: Odd branch: `T(n)^2 = n^3` iff `n` is a perfect square.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_sq_eq_cube_iff_square

declarations.doc: Equality form of the one-sided envelope. Independent of `PowerBound`.
