declarations.doc: Odd append: composite equality forces the previous equality and local tightness.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_of_append_odd

declarations.doc: Local tightness of one realized letter.
declarations.name: localTight

declarations.doc: Every local branch inequality along a realized itinerary is tight.
declarations.name: localsTight

declarations.doc: Global envelope equality forces every local branch inequality to be tight.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_local_eq

declarations.doc: Global envelope equality forces every relevant itinerary state to be a square.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_square

declarations.doc: Even square: the even branch is exact as an image, not only as a power.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_even_sq

declarations.doc: Odd square: the odd branch maps `s^2` to `s^3`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_odd_sq

declarations.doc: Exact even branch on a `2^r`-th power, `r ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_pow_two_depth_even

declarations.doc: Exact odd branch on a `2^r`-th power, `r ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_of_pow_two_depth_odd

declarations.doc: A cube that is a `2^m`-th power is the cube of a `2^m`-th power's base.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_of_cube

declarations.doc: Even exact step drops 2-adic depth by one.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_even_exact

declarations.doc: Odd exact step drops 2-adic depth by one (`a^{3·2^{r-1}} = (a^3)^{2^{r-1}}`).
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_odd_exact

declarations.doc: Depth at least 2 forces the exact image to remain a square.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_ge_two_image_square

declarations.doc: Depth exactly one: the exact image need not be a square.
declarations.name: hasPowTwoDepth_one_image_sq_iff

declarations.doc: Envelope equality of length `k` forces the start to be a `2^k`-th power.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_pow_two_depth

declarations.doc: A contracting equality itinerary of length `k` at `n ≥ 2` is at least `2^{2^k}`.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_contracts_pow_two_lb

declarations.doc: An exact step on a square keeps the parity of the state.
declarations.name: floorPower_sq_preserves_parity

declarations.doc: Exact even or odd branch on `a^{2^r}` keeps the parity of `a`.
declarations.name: floorPower_pow_two_depth_preserves_parity

declarations.doc: Envelope equality forces a monochrome word.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_implies_monochrome

declarations.doc: Equality saturates iff the itinerary is an exact even or odd tower.
declarations.name: power_bound_eq_iff_extremal

declarations.doc: Among \(n\ge 3\), an all-odd equality of length `k` is at least `3^{2^k}`.
declarations.name: odd_equality_three_pow_le

declarations.doc: A uniformly bounded trajectory repeats. Finite pigeonhole on the prefix of length `M + 2`.
declarations.name: bounded_trajectory_eventually_cycles

declarations.doc: No nontrivial cycle implies no bounded nontermination. This is not a no-cycle theorem and not a halt theorem: unbounded escape remains.
declarations.name: no_nontrivial_cycle_no_bounded_nonterm

declarations.doc: Same square-cell comparison as the human `OOEOOE` corridor, with no `CycleMin` return hypothesis.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: The itinerary `OOEOOEO` has the square-cell gap `256 > 243`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeo_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: Even `OOEOOE` landing is the shared square trap, hence `FiniteProgress`. No cycle-return hypothesis.
declarations.name: finiteProgress_of_ooeooe_even_landing

declarations.doc: Even `OOEOOE` landing is descent, hence impossible on a CE.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: On a CE, `OOEOOE` forces another `OO`. The next completed letter after the forced `O` cannot be `E`.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooe_forces_oo

declarations.doc: A CE never realizes a formally contracting itinerary. Contrapositive of `power_bound_contracts`.
declarations.name: minimal_nonterm_not_exponentGap

declarations.doc: Every realized prefix of a CE is prefix-noncontracting. Concatenating expanding residual blocks therefore cannot create an exponent certificate on a CE. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_nonterm_prefix_noncontracting

declarations.doc: The itinerary `OOEOOEOO` has the cube-cell gap `768 > 729`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeoo_image_lt_cube

declarations.doc: The completed third `OOE` has the square-cell gap `1024 > 729`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, a completed third `OOE` cannot land even: the landing is below `n^2`, so an even landing is descent. This is not a PE theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: The escaped-even `OE` after a third `OOE` has the square-cell gap `4096 > 2187`. This is not a length-11 cycle census.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoe_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, the `OE` landing after a third `OOE` cannot be even. The landing is below `n^2`, so an even landing is descent. This does not kill an odd landing such as `1517`.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooeoe_not_even_landing

declarations.doc: After an odd `OE` landing the next `O` still has the square-cell gap `8192 > 6561`. Another escaped even is impossible on this step.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoeo_image_lt_sq

declarations.doc: On a CE, the next image after an odd `OE` landing is odd and below `n^2`. An even image would be descent. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_ooeooeooeoeo_not_even

declarations.doc: The second `O` after the new `OO` loses the square cell (`19683 > 16384`) but keeps the cube-cell gap `24576 > 19683`. The square comparison `3^9 < 2 · 2^13` fails; see `ooeooeooeoeoo_loses_square`. A cube-cell even landing is therefore not `FiniteProgress`.
declarations.name: follows_ooeooeooeoeoo_image_lt_cube

declarations.doc: The per-run constant of Theorem 3.31: a run of `m` odd letters costs `(3/2)^m`, and a suffix with `k` even letters can pay `2^k`, so `m ≤ k · log 2/log(3/2)`.
declarations.name: runCapConst

declarations.doc: `5/3 < runCapConst`, which is `3^5 < 2^8` — that is, `243 < 256`.
declarations.name: runCapConst_gt

declarations.doc: `runCapConst < 12/7`, which is `2^19 < 3^12` — that is, `524288 < 531441`. This is the inequality that pins the `e = 7` cap at 11: `7 · runCapConst < 12`.
declarations.name: runCapConst_lt

declarations.doc: Paper A's table of run bounds: the cap on a run whose suffix carries `k` even letters.
declarations.name: runCap

declarations.doc: **The table is the floor.** For every suffix length the paper uses, `runCap k = ⌊k · log 2/log(3/2)⌋`.
declarations.name: runCap_eq_floor

declarations.doc: The caps fall as the suffix shortens, so the proof may apply them run by run.
declarations.name: runCap_antitone

declarations.doc: **Formal expansion first holds at length 22.** `2^22 < 3^14`.
declarations.name: expansion_holds_at_22

declarations.doc: And at no shorter length: `2^L < 3^(L−8)` fails for every `L < 22`.
declarations.name: expansion_fails_below_22

declarations.doc: **Theorem 3.31's second half.** A cycle with at least eight even letters and formal expansion `2^L < 3^o` has period at least twenty-two.
declarations.name: period_ge_22_of_even_count

declarations.doc: Trailing odd-run of any itinerary: the prefix is empty or ends even.
declarations.name: exists_trailing_odds

declarations.doc: A CycleMin itinerary cannot end `O^a E` for `a ≥ 2`. This is `no_cycleMin_odd_run` when the prefix is empty and `no_cycleMin_bootstrap_last_gap` after an internal even.
declarations.name: cycleMin_not_last_odd_run_ge_two

declarations.doc: On a CycleMin itinerary ending `O^a E` with `a ≥ 1` and the preceding letter not odd, the last odd-run has length exactly one. Paper A §3 writes that last excursion as unconstrained `O^{a_e}E`; this is the `OOEOOE` sandwich of Theorem 3.6 at an arbitrary last valley.
declarations.name: cycleMin_last_odd_run_eq_one

declarations.doc: Every CycleMin itinerary ends `O^a E` with `a ≤ 1`. The case `a = 0` is a trailing even run of length at least two.
declarations.name: exists_cycleMin_last_odd_run

declarations.doc: **Even-count assembler.** No `n ≥ 2` realizes a cycle itinerary with at most three even letters. This is not a length census and not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: no_cycle_itinerary_even_count_le_three

declarations.doc: A nontrivial cycle itinerary has length at least eleven: four evens plus the expansion demand \(2^{|w|}<3^{\#O}\).
declarations.name: cycle_itinerary_length_ge_eleven

declarations.doc: Return on the first `O^a E` is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary.
declarations.name: no_cycle_itinerary_oddEvenBlock_one

declarations.doc: On a `MinimalNonTerm` start the first even residual always overshoots. The return cell is an even-count-1 cycle itinerary. This is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: minimal_first_even_overshoots

declarations.doc: On a `CycleMin` the first even residual overshoots. Return would be an even-count-1 cycle itinerary.
declarations.name: cycleMin_first_even_overshoots

declarations.doc: Every `CycleMin` itinerary is a first-even block plus a nonempty tail.
declarations.name: cycleMin_exists_oddEven_split

declarations.doc: On a cycle minimum the maximum sits at or above `(n+1)^2`. The first even residual already overshoots, so the first-cell family `n^2 < M < (n+1)^2` is impossible. Not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: cycleMin_max_ge_succ_sq

declarations.doc: On a cycle maximum the rotated minimum satisfies `(m+1)^2 ≤ M`.
declarations.name: cycleMax_min_succ_sq_le

declarations.doc: The maximum cannot collapse to the minimum in one even step.
declarations.name: cycleMax_landing_gt_min

declarations.doc: Laboratory sharpening of `cycle_distinguished_order`: first-even overshoot replaces `m^2 < M` by `(m+1)^2 ≤ M`.
declarations.name: cycle_distinguished_order_succ_sq

declarations.doc: Formal expansion of an `O^a E^b` block is an odd-density bound.
declarations.name: expanding_implies_odd_density

declarations.doc: Largest even-run length compatible with formal expansion.
declarations.name: maxExpandingEvens

declarations.doc: For `a ≥ 1`, `O^a E^b` expands if and only if `a+b ≤ log₂(3^a)`.
declarations.name: expanding_oddEvenBlock_iff_log

declarations.doc: Persistence is already expansion: a contracting residual cannot overshoot `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: persistent_odd_residual_expanding

declarations.doc: On `n ≥ 2`, the expanding qualifier of a persistent residual is redundant.
declarations.name: persistent_expanding_iff_odd

declarations.doc: Type-level self-loop of the minimal expanding residual. This is not an infinite trajectory: the realized chain at 365 leaves the odd-to-odd frontier after three `OOE` blocks.
declarations.name: expanding_type_ooe_self_loop

declarations.doc: Integer exponent surplus. Zero in `ℕ` when the itinerary is not formally expanding.
declarations.name: expansionSurplus

declarations.doc: Pair `(n^{3^o}, T^{2^k})`. The log of the ratio is the weighted slack; Lean keeps the product form.
declarations.name: logSlack

declarations.doc: Integer form of the block-growth identity: on an expanding itinerary, `n^{3^o} = n^{2^k + E(w)}`.
declarations.name: block_growth_identity

declarations.doc: An expanding residual block has strictly fewer evens than odds.
declarations.name: expanding_oddEvenBlock_even_lt_odd

declarations.doc: Formal block multiplier `λ = 3^{#O} / 2^{|w|}` as the pair `(A, B) = (3^{#O(w)}, 2^{|w|})`.
declarations.name: blockMultiplier

declarations.doc: Formal expansion margin `μ = λ - 1` as the pair `(A - B, B)`. The first component is `0` in `ℕ` when the itinerary is not expanding.
declarations.name: expansionMargin

declarations.doc: Log-free pair for `ℓ = log(1+q)`. Same pair as `onePlusSlack`.
declarations.name: blockLogSlack

declarations.doc: Log-free pair for the slack tax `c = ℓ / B`. Same pair as `onePlusSlack`; the weight `B` is `(blockMultiplier w).2`.
declarations.name: blockSlackTax

declarations.doc: Concatenated `1+q`. In logs this is the weighted slack `C`.
declarations.name: weightedSlack

declarations.doc: Concatenated `1+q`. In logs this is the normalized budget `B = C / Λ`.
declarations.name: normalizedSlackBudget

declarations.doc: Multiplier product `Λ_{uv} = Λ_u Λ_v`.
declarations.name: blockMultiplier_mul

declarations.doc: Exact power identity `n^A = T^B + Δ`. This is `slack_identity` in multiplier coordinates.
declarations.name: block_power_identity

declarations.doc: Log-free form of `log T = λ log n - c`.
declarations.name: block_log_growth

declarations.doc: Exact concatenation law in multiplier coordinates. This is the Nat form of `ℓ_{uv} = A_v ℓ_u + B_u ℓ_v` and of `C_{uv} = λ_v C_u + C_v`.
declarations.name: weighted_slack_concat

declarations.doc: Two-block form of the weighted cocycle. Same identity.
declarations.name: weighted_slack_cocycle

declarations.doc: Normalized budget identity: concatenated `1+q` is the product of the block slacks with the exact expansion weights. In logs this is `y_m = Λ_m (y_0 - B_m)`.
declarations.name: normalized_budget_identity

declarations.doc: Local compatibility `c < μ log n` iff `T > n`. This is the endpoint comparison on one block, not a sequence constraint.
declarations.name: block_growth_compat

declarations.doc: Four consecutive expanding persistent residual blocks. This kills any uniform run bound `M ≤ 4`.
declarations.name: four_block_pe_1999

declarations.doc: Four consecutive persistent expanding residual blocks exist: `1999` to `5169` by `OOE`, `5169` to `50093` by `OOOOEE`, then `50093` to `193753` and `193753` to `887471` by `OOE`. Each step is a `PersistentExpandingResidual`.
declarations.name: four_consecutive_persistent_expanding_exists

declarations.doc: Length of the `k`-th fan member: `q₁₂ + k q₁₃`.
declarations.name: fanLength

declarations.doc: Odd count of the `k`-th fan member: `p₁₂ + k p₁₃`.
declarations.name: fanOdd

declarations.doc: The linear form `Λ k = o k · log 3 − L k · log 2`.
declarations.name: fanLambda

declarations.doc: The paper's three frontiers are the first three members.
declarations.name: fan_frontiers

declarations.doc: The endpoint is the next convergent: `L 55 = q₁₄` and `o 55 = p₁₄`.
declarations.name: fan_endpoint

declarations.doc: One step past the fan lands on `q₁₅`, `p₁₅`.
declarations.name: fan_past_endpoint

declarations.doc: `Λ` is affine in `k`: the step is `Λ' = 190537 log 3 − 301994 log 2`, independent of `k`.
declarations.name: fanLambda_affine

declarations.doc: `3^190537 < 2^301994`: consecutive convergents lie on opposite sides, so `Λ' < 0`.
declarations.name: fan_step_pow

declarations.doc: Hence the affine step of `Λ` is strictly negative and `Λ` is strictly decreasing.
declarations.name: fanLambda_step_neg

declarations.doc: **The fan has exactly 56 members.** `Λ k > 0` for `k ≤ 55` and `Λ k < 0` for `k ≥ 56`.
declarations.name: fan_positive_iff

declarations.doc: One even first letter is already infeasible: `u₁ = step·0 − 1 = −1 < 0`.
declarations.name: walk_first_letter_odd

declarations.doc: With `step < 2`, an even *second* letter is infeasible too: after one odd letter `u₂ = step − 2 < 0`. So every nonnegative exponent walk begins `OO`, for structural reasons and with no input from the Juggler map.
declarations.name: walk_second_letter_odd

declarations.doc: The constant the previous lemma needs: `log₂ 3 < 2`, i.e. `3 < 4`.
declarations.name: step_lt_two

declarations.doc: At four even letters, expansion first allows `L = 11`: this is Corollary 3.23.
declarations.name: expansion_e4

declarations.doc: At five even letters it first allows `L = 14`, so an even-count of five would give period at least fourteen.
declarations.name: expansion_e5

declarations.doc: At six, `L = 17`.
declarations.name: expansion_e6

declarations.doc: The growth rate, certified by integers rather than by bounds on logarithms. Expansion at even count `e` needs `L log(3/2) > e log 3`, so the threshold grows by `log 3 / log(3/2)` per even letter. That constant lies in `(2.70, 2.71)`: * `(3/2)^(27/10) < 3` is `3^17 < 2^27`, giving `2.70 < log 3 / log(3/2)`; * `3 < (3/2)^(271/100)` is `2^271 < 3^171`, giving `log 3 / log(3/2) < 2.71`. Both are integer comparisons, so they are exact and need no analytic input. The second is tight: `2^271` and `3^171` agree to four significant figures.
declarations.name: expansion_rate_lower

declarations.doc: The paper's `E(m')`: the even `m` with `m'² ≤ m < (m'+1)²`.
declarations.name: blockE

declarations.doc: The odd integers of the paper's `I(m') = [m'^{8/3}, (m'+1)^{8/3})`, written exactly with the landing window of Appendix D.1.
declarations.name: oddBlock

declarations.doc: Membership in the block is the exact condition `m'² ≤ ⌊n^{3/4}⌋ < (m'+1)²`.
declarations.name: mem_oddBlock

declarations.doc: The fiber of `⌊n^{3/4}⌋` over `m`, among the odd integers, is the paper's `Φ(m)`.
declarations.name: mem_oeFiber_iff_cell34

declarations.doc: `U(m')`: the odd `n` of the block whose two floors are both even.
declarations.name: U

declarations.doc: **The proposition's first sentence, exactly.** `U(m')` is the disjoint union of the even-image parts of the fibers `Φ(m)` over the even `m` of the block, so its size is the sum of the even-image counts of Lemma 4.2.
declarations.name: U_card_eq

declarations.doc: The parity wave `ψ(z) = (-1)^{⌊z⌋}`, at an integer floor value.
declarations.name: psi

declarations.doc: `Σ ψ(n^{3/4})`, the slow sum.
declarations.name: slowSum

declarations.doc: `Σ ψ(n^{3/2})`, the fast sum.
declarations.name: fastSum

declarations.doc: `Σ ψ(n^{3/4}) ψ(n^{3/2})`, the product sum.
declarations.name: productSum

declarations.doc: **Expanding the two indicators**, exactly: `4|U(m')| = M + S₁ + S₂ + S₁₂`, where `M` is the number of odd integers of the block. This is the identity the paper's proof starts from; the three sums are what its exponential-sum estimates bound.
declarations.name: four_card_U

declarations.doc: **Proposition 4.4, equation (4.1), given the exponential-sum bounds.** If each of the three parity sums is at most `B` in absolute value, then `|U(m')|` is within `3B/4` of a quarter of the odd integers of the block. Exact; the content of the proposition is that `B` may be taken to be `C m'^{11/9} log(m'+1)`, which is the hypothesis, not the conclusion.
declarations.name: block_average_of_bounds

declarations.doc: Proposition 4.4 in the paper's shape: with each parity sum bounded by `C m'^{11/9} log(m'+1)` — the analytic input, assumed here — equation (4.1) holds with `C_B = 3C/4`.
declarations.name: block_average_bound

declarations.doc: Inside the block, the fiber of `⌊n^{3/4}⌋` over `m` is `Φ(m)`.
declarations.name: oddBlock_filter_eq

declarations.doc: **The slow sum, fiber by fiber.** `S₁ = Σ_{m'² ≤ m < (m'+1)²} ψ(m) |Φ(m)|`: the parity of `⌊n^{3/4}⌋` is constant on a fiber, so the slow sum is an alternating sum of fiber sizes.
declarations.name: slowSum_eq_fibers

declarations.doc: Consecutive fibers differ by at most two members (`m ≥ 1`): the fiber bounds `(2/3)m^{1/3} - 1 ≤ |Φ(m)| ≤ (2/3)(m+1)^{1/3} + 1` overlap, and `(m+2)^{1/3} - m^{1/3} ≤ (2/3) m^{-2/3} ≤ 2/3` by Bernoulli.
declarations.name: oeFiber_card_succ_diff

declarations.doc: An alternating sum over `2k` consecutive terms whose neighbours differ by at most `d` is at most `k d` in absolute value: each pair telescopes to one difference.
declarations.name: abs_alt_sum_le

declarations.doc: **The slow sum is `O(m')`.** `|S₁| ≤ 2m' + (2/3)(m'+1)^{2/3} + 1`: the block is `m'` pairs of consecutive fibers, each contributing at most `2`, plus one fiber left over. This is the paper's "pair consecutive fibers, whose odd-point counts differ by at most 3, and bound the remaining end fiber", with `2` in place of `3`.
declarations.name: slowSum_abs_le

declarations.doc: `M ≤ (2m'+1)((2/3)(m'+1)^{2/3} + 1)`: every fiber of the block has at most `(2/3)((m'+1)²)^{1/3} + 1` members.
declarations.name: oddBlock_card_le

declarations.doc: `(2m'+1)((2/3)m'^{2/3} - 1) ≤ M`: every fiber of the block has at least `(2/3)(m'²)^{1/3} - 1` members.
declarations.name: oddBlock_card_ge

declarations.doc: A quarter of the block is `m'^{5/3}/3` up to `m' + 1`: the "in particular" of the proposition, before the parity sums enter.
declarations.name: oddBlock_quarter_close

declarations.doc: **Proposition 4.4, equation (4.1), given the two exponential-sum bounds.** The slow sum is proved (`slowSum_abs_le`); the fast sum and the product sum remain hypotheses.
declarations.name: block_average_two_bounds

declarations.doc: **The asymptotic form of Proposition 4.4 with an explicit error**, given the two bounds: `|U(m')|` is within `B/2 + 2(m'+1)` of `m'^{5/3}/3`. With `B = C m'^{11/9} log(m'+1)` this is the paper's `|U(m')| = m'^{5/3}/3 (1 + O(m'^{-4/9} log(m'+1)))`.
declarations.name: block_average_asymptotic

declarations.doc: Proposition 4.4 in the paper's shape with only the two exponential-sum hypotheses: for `m' ≥ 2` and both remaining sums at most `C m'^{11/9} log(m'+1)`, equation (4.1) holds with `C_B = C/2 + 2`.
declarations.name: block_average_bound_two

declarations.doc: A finite set of natural indices confined to `[A, B]` has at most `B - A + 1` elements. The hypothesis `0 ≤ B - A + 1` covers the empty set, where `B < A` is allowed.
declarations.name: card_le_of_bounds

declarations.doc: A finite set of natural indices all `< B` has fewer than `B + 1` elements. The bound is strict, which is what makes the half-count of `gridPoint_half_count` land at `1/2` rather than at `1`.
declarations.name: card_lt_of_upper

declarations.doc: A set of natural indices `< q` all bounded below by `A ≤ q` has at most `q - A` elements.
declarations.name: card_le_of_lower

declarations.doc: Monotonicity of a filtered count in its predicate.
declarations.name: card_filter_le_card_filter

declarations.doc: Two filtered counts differ by at most the number of indices where the two predicates disagree. This is what converts the grid count into the displaced count in `block_count`.
declarations.name: card_filter_abs_sub_le

declarations.doc: Reindexing a filtered count along a bijection `g : s → t`.
declarations.name: card_filter_reindex

declarations.doc: The residue index of the grid point `c + k/q`: the unique `l < q` with `{c + k/q} = (l + {q c})/q` (`fract_grid`).
declarations.name: gridRes

declarations.doc: The residue index is an index of `Finset.range q`.
declarations.name: gridRes_lt

declarations.doc: **The grid normal form.** `{c + k/q} = (gridRes q c k + {q c})/q`: the fractional parts of the points `c + k/q`, `k ∈ ℤ`, are exactly the `q` points of the `1/q`-grid translated by `{q c}/q`. This is (1.2) of the note, in the form the two counts below use.
declarations.name: fract_grid

declarations.doc: Multiplication by a `p` coprime to `q` permutes the residue indices of the grid: the algebraic half of the note's "the points `y + i p/q` are a translate of the `1/q`-grid". The same algebra as `OstrowskiSandwich.residue_mul_bijective`, in a different type: that one permutes `ZMod q`, this one indexes `Finset.range q` through `gridRes`. Read the refutation recorded after it there -- "the grid-cell reading of the block permutation is false" -- before reusing either. It does NOT apply here, and the reason is this file's architecture. There the points are `k θ` for an IRRATIONAL `θ ≈ p/q`: each sits within `1/q` of a grid point and may fall just below it, so the cells are not permuted. Here the points are the EXACT rational grid `c + i p/q` and `gridRes` is their exact residue index, so the permutation is the honest one. `block_lock` never puts the displacement inside the indexing: the exact grid carries `grid_reindex`, and `e_i` is handled apart by `grid_near_count` and `fract_lt_half_congr`. That separation is what the Ostrowski refutation says is mandatory, so the two records agree rather than conflict.
declarations.name: gridRes_mul_inj

declarations.doc: **The grid reindexing.** For `gcd(p, q) = 1` the map `i ↦ gridRes q c (i p)` is a bijection of `Finset.range q`, so a count over the grid points `c + i p / q` is a count over the plain `1/q`-grid.
declarations.name: grid_reindex

declarations.doc: **The half count, normal form.** An arc of length `1/2` holds `⌊q/2⌋` or `⌈q/2⌉` of the `q` points `(l + s)/q`, `l < q`: the count is within `1/2` of `q/2`. This is the first of the note's two elementary counts.
declarations.name: gridPoint_half_count

declarations.doc: The points of the circle at which a displacement of size at most `ε` can move the indicator `1[{·} < 1/2]`: within `ε` of `0` (from either side) or within `ε` of `1/2`.
declarations.name: Unstable

declarations.doc: **The near count, normal form.** At most `2εq + 1` of the `q` grid points `(l + s)/q` lie within `ε` of a fixed point of the circle, hence at most `4εq + 2` lie within `ε` of `0` or of `1/2`. This is the second of the note's two elementary counts.
declarations.name: gridPoint_near_count

declarations.doc: **The half count.** For any `c` and any `q ≥ 1`, the number of `l < q` with `{c + l/q} < 1/2` is within `1/2` of `q/2`: an arc of length `1/2` holds `⌊q/2⌋` or `⌈q/2⌉` points of a translate of the `1/q`-grid. Lemma 1 of the note, first elementary count.
declarations.name: grid_half_count

declarations.doc: **The near count.** At most `4εq + 2` of the points `{c + l/q}`, `l < q`, lie within `ε` of `0` or of `1/2` on the circle. Lemma 1 of the note, second elementary count.
declarations.name: grid_near_count

declarations.doc: A displacement of size at most `ε` does not move the indicator `1[{·} < 1/2]` at a point that is not `Unstable`. This is the note's "a perturbation of size at most `ε` changes the indicator only at points within `ε` of `0` or of `1/2`".
declarations.name: fract_lt_half_congr

declarations.doc: **The block displacement, (1.2) of the note.** `i` steps in `[a, a + η]` move `x` by `i a + r` with `0 ≤ r ≤ i η`.
declarations.name: span_bounds

declarations.doc: **Lemma 1, one block.** On `q` consecutive indices the good count is within `4 (ρ + qη) q + 5/2` of `q/2`. This is the heart of the note's Lemma 1: the block's points are a translate of the `1/q`-grid displaced by at most `ε = ρ + qη`, the grid is split evenly by the arc `[0, 1/2)` up to `1/2` (`gridPoint_half_count`), and at most `4εq + 2` of the indicators move (`gridPoint_near_count`, `fract_lt_half_congr`).
declarations.name: block_count

declarations.doc: The first `b` full blocks: the good count over `[0, bq)` is within `b (4 (ρ + qη) q + 5/2)` of `bq/2`.
declarations.name: block_chain

declarations.doc: **Lemma 1 (block lock).** `docs/theory/juggler_oe_poor_fiber_tail_note.md`, (1.1), in the cleared form. If the first `H` steps of `x` lie in `[a, a + η]` and `a` is within `ρ/q` of the rational `p/q` with `gcd(p, q) = 1`, then the number of `j < H` with `{x j} < 1/2` differs from `H/2` by at most `4 (ρ + qη) H + 5H/(2q) + q`. Dividing by `H` and substituting `ρ = ‖qa‖` gives the note's `|σ - 1/2| ≤ 4‖qa‖ + 5/(2q) + q(1 + 4ηH)/H`; that division is left to the caller so that this statement carries no nonzero-denominator side condition and stays true at `H = 0`.
declarations.name: block_lock

declarations.doc: **An upper bound on a logarithm, certified by integers.** If `E ≤ e` and `x^n ≤ E^m` then `n log x ≤ m`.
declarations.name: log_le_of_pow_le

declarations.doc: **A lower bound on a logarithm, certified by integers.** If `e ≤ E` and `E^m ≤ x^n` then `m ≤ n log x`.
declarations.name: le_log_of_pow_le

declarations.doc: The same for a base-two logarithm: `x^n ≤ 2^m` gives `log₂ x ≤ m/n`.
declarations.name: logb_two_le

declarations.doc: And `2^m ≤ x^n` gives `m/n ≤ log₂ x`.
declarations.name: le_logb_two

declarations.doc: **A sandwich on `p` gives a lower bound on `D(p ‖ 1/2)`.**
declarations.name: klHalf_ge_of

declarations.doc: **A sandwich on `p` gives an upper bound on `D(p ‖ 1/2)`.**
declarations.name: klHalf_le_of

declarations.doc: **The certified instance.** `e(30) > 39/50`, with no audit script in the chain; in particular `e(30) > 39/50`, comfortably past the `27/40` side condition of every unconditional criterion.
declarations.name: chernoffExponent_thirty_gt

declarations.doc: `e(30) < 13/10`, so the side condition `A > C + e(C)` is met by `A ≥ 32`.
declarations.name: chernoffExponent_thirty_lt

declarations.doc: **The conjecture from a cylinder bound at `C = 30`.** If every `O`-rooted `L(y)`-bad cylinder of depth `⌈30 L(y)⌉` holds at most its fair share plus `y (log y)^{-A}`, at all large scales above a certified floor, for some `A ≥ 32`, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: cylinder_bound_thirty

declarations.doc: **The conjecture from the pressure hypothesis at `C = 30`.** If the live pressure at the tilt `p_30/(1 - p_30)` and depth `⌈30 L(y)⌉` is at most `2y a_θ^{d(y)}` at all large scales above a certified floor, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: pressure_thirty

declarations.doc: At `q = 1/2` the relative entropy is the paper's `D(p ‖ 1/2)`.
declarations.name: klDiv_half

declarations.doc: Hence the one-sided exponent at `q = 1/2` is the Chernoff exponent.
declarations.name: oneSidedExponent_half

declarations.doc: `log₂` of the re-centring tilt at `C = 30`, `q = 1/2`, is at most `13/20`: from `(61/39)^20 ≤ 2^13`.
declarations.name: logb_tilt_thirty_le

declarations.doc: **The conjecture from the one-sided hypothesis at `C = 30`, `q = 1/2`.** If no `L(y)`-bad cylinder of depth below `⌈30 L(y)⌉` sends more than half of its members, plus `y (log y)^{-A}`, to an odd next letter, at all large scales above a certified floor, for some `A ≥ 52`, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: one_sided_thirty

declarations.doc: Markov tilt on the constant weight: at most `(1 + x)^d / x^k` words of length `d` have at least `k` odd letters, for any `x ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: count_oddCount_ge_le

declarations.doc: The same with a real threshold `p d` on the odd count and a real exponent.
declarations.name: count_oddCount_ge_real_le

declarations.doc: Binary entropy in nats, `h(p) = -p log p - (1-p) log (1-p)`.
declarations.name: entropyLog

declarations.doc: Relative entropy to the fair coin, `D(p ‖ 1/2) = log 2 - h(p)`.
declarations.name: klHalf

declarations.doc: Gibbs' inequality for the fair coin: `h(p) ≤ log 2`, i.e. `D(p ‖ 1/2) ≥ 0`.
declarations.name: klHalf_nonneg

declarations.doc: At the tilt `x = p/(1-p)`, `(1 + x)^d / x^{p d} = exp (d h(p))`.
declarations.name: tilt_value

declarations.doc: **Lemma 8.2, the count.** For `1/2 ≤ p < 1`, at most `exp (d h(p))` words of length `d` have at least `p d` odd letters.
declarations.name: count_oddCount_ge_le_exp

declarations.doc: The same in the paper's form `2^d exp(-d D(p ‖ 1/2))`.
declarations.name: count_oddCount_ge_le_kl

declarations.doc: `w` is `L`-bad: the exponent walk `o_t log₂ 3 - t` stays above `-L` at every prefix `1 ≤ t ≤ |w|`.
declarations.name: LBad

declarations.doc: The paper's `p_C = (1 - 1/C)/log₂ 3`.
declarations.name: pC

declarations.doc: The paper's Chernoff exponent `e(C) = C D(p_C ‖ 1/2)/log 2`.
declarations.name: chernoffExponent

declarations.doc: An `L`-bad word of length `d ≥ C L` has at least `p_C d` odd letters.
declarations.name: LBad_oddCount_ge

declarations.doc: **Lemma 8.2 (Chernoff), exact form.** For `C ≥ 5` and `d ≥ C L` with `d ≥ 1`, the number of `L`-bad words of length `d` is at most `2^d · 2^{-e(C) L}`.
declarations.name: LBad_count_le

declarations.doc: The cylinder of `w` at scale `y`: odd starts in `(y, 2y]` whose realized itinerary of length `d` is `w`.
declarations.name: cylinder

declarations.doc: The odd starts in `(y, 2y]` that do not reach `1`.
declarations.name: oddFailures

declarations.doc: `w` fails the envelope comparison against the floor `N₀` at the scale `Y` at every prefix: `N₀^{2^t} < Y^{3^{o_t}}` for all `t ≤ |w|`. This is the integer form of `L(Y)`-badness.
declarations.name: EnvelopeBad

declarations.doc: **Lemma 8.1 in covering form.** If every start up to `N₀` reaches `1`, an odd failure in `(y, 2y]` lies in the cylinder of an envelope-bad word.
declarations.name: oddFailures_subset_bad_cylinders

declarations.doc: **Theorem 8.3, the union bound.** Under a floor `N₀` and a bound `M` on every envelope-bad cylinder of depth `d`, the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most (the number of envelope-bad words) times `M`.
declarations.name: oddFailures_card_le

declarations.doc: Envelope-badness at the scale `Y` is `L`-badness with `L = log₂ (log Y / log N₀)`, for `N₀ ≥ 2` and `Y ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: LBad_of_envelopeBad

declarations.doc: **Theorem 8.3, exact composite.** Floor `N₀ ≥ 2`, scale `y ≥ 1`, depth `d ≥ 1` with `d ≥ C L`, `L = log₂ (log 2y / log N₀)`, `C ≥ 5`; if every `L`-bad cylinder of depth `d` holds at most `M` starts, then the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `2^d · 2^{-e(C) L} · M`.
declarations.name: oddFailures_card_le_chernoff

declarations.doc: `Λ(y) = log 2y / log N₀`.
declarations.name: scaleRatio

declarations.doc: The paper's `L(y) = log₂ (log 2y / log N₀)`.
declarations.name: scaleL

declarations.doc: The paper's depth `d(y) = ⌈C L(y)⌉`.
declarations.name: depth

declarations.doc: Odd starts have first letter `O`: an `E`-rooted cylinder of positive depth is empty.
declarations.name: cylinder_even_root_empty

declarations.doc: **Theorem 8.3, explicit form.** Floor `N₀ ≥ 2`, scale `y ≥ 2`, `C ≥ 5`, depth `d = ⌈C L(y)⌉ ≥ 1`. If every `O`-rooted `L(y)`-bad cylinder of depth `d` holds at most `2^{-(d-1)} y/2 + y (log y)^{-A}` starts (the hypothesis `H(C, A)` at this `y`), then the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y Λ^{-e(C)} + 2 Λ^C y (log y)^{-A}`, `Λ = log 2y / log N₀`. The paper's `(y/2) Λ^{-(e(C)-ε)}` for large `y` follows by absorbing the factor `2` into `Λ^ε` and the second term into the first when `A > C + e(C)`; that absorption is not formalized.
declarations.name: oddFailures_card_le_explicit

declarations.doc: The fiber of the value `v` at depth `t`: the starts of `S` whose `t`-th iterate is `v`.
declarations.name: fiber

declarations.doc: The starts of `S` whose `t`-th iterate lies in the window `[a, b]`.
declarations.name: window

declarations.doc: The next-letter bias of the window: the starts of the window whose `t`-th iterate is odd (next letter `O`) minus those whose `t`-th iterate is even.
declarations.name: windowBias

declarations.doc: The starts of the window whose iterate satisfies `p` are counted by the fibers over the values of `[a, b]` satisfying `p`.
declarations.name: card_filter_window

declarations.doc: The bias is the alternating sum of the fibers.
declarations.name: windowBias_eq_sum

declarations.doc: Summation by parts: `|Σ_{i<n} (-1)^i h_i| ≤ Σ_{i<n-1} |h_{i+1} - h_i| + h_{n-1}` for nonnegative `h`.
declarations.name: abs_alt_sum_le

declarations.doc: **The bias is bounded by the variation of the fiber profile.**
declarations.name: abs_windowBias_le

declarations.doc: A preimage of `v` under the map lies below `(v+1)²`.
declarations.name: lt_sq_succ_of_floorPower_eq

declarations.doc: The preimages of `v` under the map.
declarations.name: pre

declarations.doc: The fiber at depth `t+1` is the sum of the depth-`t` fibers over the preimages.
declarations.name: fiber_succ

declarations.doc: The even preimages of `v` are the even numbers of `[v², (v+1)²)` (Lemma 3.1's even block, in fiber form).
declarations.name: pre_filter_even

declarations.doc: The even branch: the depth-`t` mass of the even numbers of `[v², (v+1)²)`.
declarations.name: blockSum

declarations.doc: The odd branch: the depth-`t` mass of the odd preimages of `v`.
declarations.name: oddPart

declarations.doc: `fiber(t+1, v) = blockSum + oddPart`.
declarations.name: fiber_succ_eq

declarations.doc: The number of even numbers of `[v², (v+1)²)`.
declarations.name: evenCount

declarations.doc: **The even branch smooths.** If the depth-`t` profile lies between `m` and `M` on the double block `[v², (v+2)²)`, consecutive block sums differ by at most `(v+1)(M-m) + 2M`.
declarations.name: blockSum_sub_le

declarations.doc: The variation of the odd branch over a window is at most twice its mass.
declarations.name: sum_abs_oddPart_sub_le

declarations.doc: **The collapsed component is nearly fair.** If the depth-`t` fiber profile lies between `m v` and `M v` on the double block `[v², (v+2)²)` for every `v` in `[a, b)`, the next-letter bias of the starts whose `(t+1)`-st iterate lies in `[a, b]` is at most `Σ_{v ∈ [a,b)} ((v+1)(M v - m v) + 2 M v)`, plus twice the mass arriving through odd preimages, plus one fiber.
declarations.name: collapse_bias_le

declarations.doc: **A sandwich propagates through an even step.** If the depth-`t` profile lies between `m` and `M` on the block `[v², (v+1)²)` and the odd branch at `v` carries at most `P`, then `v m ≤ fiber(t+1, v) ≤ (v+1) M + P`.
declarations.name: fiber_succ_sandwich

declarations.doc: **Two even steps.** If the depth-`t` profile lies between `m w` and `M w` on the block `[w⁴, (w+2)⁴)` and the odd branch at depth `t` is at most `P w` on `[w², (w+2)²)`, for every `w` in `[a, b)`, the next-letter bias of the starts whose `(t+2)`-nd iterate lies in `[a, b]` is bounded by the propagated sandwich `w² m w ≤ fiber(t+1, ·) ≤ (w+2)² M w + P w`: the relative oscillation of the profile is not amplified by an even step, and the loss is a relative `O(1/w)`.
declarations.name: collapse_bias_two_step

declarations.doc: `A` is closed under taking one-step preimages.
declarations.name: BackwardClosed

declarations.doc: Divergence is also forward-closed: an unbounded orbit stays unbounded.
declarations.name: escapes_floorPower

declarations.doc: Even block: `J n = m` for every even `n ∈ [m^2, (m+1)^2)`.
declarations.name: floorPower_even_block

declarations.doc: The even block of `m` has at least `m` elements.
declarations.name: even_block_card

declarations.doc: OE fiber: an odd `n` with `m^4 ≤ n^3 < (m+1)^4` and even `⌊n^{3/2}⌋` has `J (J n) = m`. The middle state is `Nat.sqrt (n^3)`; the second step is `Nat.sqrt` of it, i.e. the transparent nesting `⌊n^{3/4}⌋ = m`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oe_fiber

declarations.doc: The OE fiber of `m` is the set of odd `n` in the fourth-power cell; its elements are pairwise `2` apart, hence the fibers of distinct `m` are disjoint (the cells are).
declarations.name: oe_fiber_disjoint

declarations.doc: `m` lies on a cycle of positive period. (`Seam.lean` already uses the name `OnCycle` for membership in a given cycle word.)
declarations.name: Periodic

declarations.doc: Every positive start has exactly one of three fates: it reaches `1`, it enters a nontrivial cycle (through some state `m ≥ 2` on that cycle), or its orbit is unbounded. This is the Lean form of Lemma 1.1 of the finite-dynamics note with the basins named; it is not a halt theorem.
declarations.name: fate_trichotomy

declarations.doc: `A` is closed under one forward step.
declarations.name: ForwardClosed

declarations.doc: Odd generation: in a forward-closed class, every member `n ≥ 1` reaches an odd member of the class through even steps only.
declarations.name: exists_odd_ancestor

declarations.doc: If the class excludes `1`, the odd ancestor is at least `3`.
declarations.name: exists_odd_ancestor_ge_three

declarations.doc: A class closed both ways and excluding `1` is nonempty iff it contains the image `⌊m^{3/2}⌋ = Nat.sqrt (m^3)` of some odd `m ≥ 3`.
declarations.name: nonempty_iff_odd_image_mem

declarations.doc: The odd members of a class closed both ways are exactly the odd preimages of its members: for odd `n`, `n ∈ A ↔ ⌊n^{3/2}⌋ ∈ A`.
declarations.name: odd_mem_iff

declarations.doc: Realized-itinerary form: if the first `k` letters of the orbit of `n` satisfy the envelope comparison against `N₀`, and every start up to `N₀` reaches `1`, then `n` reaches `1`.

declarations.doc: **The ladder coefficients are the increments of (5.9)**: `c_k - (2/9) c_{k-1} = 3^{-(k+1)}` with `c_k = 3^{-k}`. The `2/9` is the depth-two `OE` coefficient, so each ladder term is what the word contributes *beyond* what that family already counts.

declarations.doc: The same coefficients in closed form, `3^{-(k+1)}`: the increment collapses.

declarations.doc: The paper's `ζ(λ) = Σ_i c_i e_i^λ - 1`; Theorem 5.3 holds for every `λ` with `ζ(λ) > 0`.
declarations.name: zeta

declarations.doc: `ζ` is antitone: every `e_i ≤ 1`.
declarations.name: zeta_antitone

declarations.doc: A rational lower bound for a rational power: `r ≤ x^{p/q}` from `r^q ≤ x^p`.
declarations.name: le_rpow_div_of_pow_le

declarations.doc: `ζ(0.49) > 0`: the eight production terms at `λ = 49/100` sum to more than `1`, by exact rational lower bounds (`e_i^{49} ≥ r_i^{100}`). The paper's root is `λ** = 0.4926…`.
declarations.name: zeta_pos_49

declarations.doc: The seed constant `c_A` of Lemma 5.2.
declarations.name: seedConst

declarations.doc: The paper's `g_A(t)`: the log-mass of `A` on `(√x, x]` at `x = e^t`, on the integers of `(⌊√⌊x⌋⌋, ⌊x⌋]`.
declarations.name: gA

declarations.doc: Lemma 5.2 in the form `g_A(t) ≥ c_A` for `t ≥ 4 log(m+1)`.
declarations.name: gA_seed

declarations.doc: `g_A(log x)` is at most the full log-mass up to `x`.
declarations.name: logMass_ge_gA

declarations.doc: **Paper C Theorem 5.3, given the production inequality (5.2).** Let `A` be backward-closed with a positive member, `0 < λ ≤ 0.49`, and suppose `g_A(t) ≥ Σ_i (c_i - η_i(t)) g_A(e_i t) - η₀(t)` for all `t ≥ t₀`, with errors `η_i(t), η₀(t) ≥ 0` that tend to `0`. Then `g_A(t) ≥ K t^λ` for all large `t`, some `K > 0`. The proof is the paper's: the seed of Lemma 5.2 on `[e_min t₁, t₁]`, the recursion lemma with `ζ(λ) ≥ ζ(0.49) > 0`, and `t₁` large enough that the errors are below `ζ/24` and `(2ζ/3) c_A`.
declarations.name: contagion_of_production_inequality

declarations.doc: Theorem 5.3 given (5.2), in the form Theorem 7.2 consumes: `Σ_{n ≤ x, n ∈ A} 1/n ≥ K (log x)^λ` for all large `x`.
declarations.name: logMass_contagion_of_production

declarations.doc: Every positive integer reaching `1` empties the odd failures of every block.
declarations.name: oddFailures_eq_empty

declarations.doc: **Paper C Theorem 7.3 (equivalence), with the contagion bound of Theorem 5.3 as a hypothesis.** Every positive integer reaches `1` iff the odd failures satisfy a Tao-type rate `y (log y)^{-e}` with some `e > 1 - λ` at all large scales.
declarations.name: tao_rate_iff_conjecture

declarations.doc: **Corollary 8.4 with Theorem 5.3 discharged through the production inequality.** If the cylinder hypothesis `H(C, A)` holds at all large scales with `C ≥ 5`, `A > C + e(C)` and `1 - λ < e(C)` for some `0 < λ ≤ 0.49`, and the failure set (if nonempty) satisfies the production inequality (5.2) with vanishing errors, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: conjecture_of_cylinder_bound_of_production

declarations.doc: The cylinder hypothesis `H(C, A)` at the scale `y`: every `O`-rooted `L(y)`-bad cylinder of depth `d(y) = ⌈C L(y)⌉` holds at most `2^{-(d-1)} y/2 + y (log y)^{-A}` starts.
declarations.name: CylinderBound

declarations.doc: The depth is positive as soon as `2y > N₀`.
declarations.name: one_le_depth

declarations.doc: **The absorption.** Under `H(C, A)` at all large scales, with `A > C + e(C)`, the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y (log y)^{-e}` for every `e < e(C)` and all large `y`.
declarations.name: oddFailures_eventually_le

declarations.doc: **Corollary 8.4.** If the cylinder hypothesis `H(C, A)` holds at all large scales with `C ≥ 5` and `A > C + e(C)`, and the contagion bound of Theorem 5.3 holds for the failure set with an exponent `λ` satisfying `1 - λ < e(C)`, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: cylinder_bound_implies_conjecture

declarations.name: bias

declarations.name: sum_bias_sq

declarations.doc: `#(A ∩ (y/2, y])`, the count on the dyadic block of Corollary 5.4.
declarations.name: blockCount

declarations.doc: A block's log-mass is at most `2 #(A ∩ (y/2, y]) / y`, because every member exceeds `y/2`.
declarations.name: block_logMass_le

declarations.doc: Every `1 ≤ n ≤ X` lies in the block `(X/2^{j+1}, X/2^j]` with `j = ⌊log₂(X/n)⌋`.
declarations.name: block_index

declarations.doc: The shell `(√X, X]` is covered by the blocks `(X/2^{j+1}, X/2^j]`, `j < J`, that reach above `√X`, whenever `X < 2^J`; so its log-mass is at most the sum of their log-masses.
declarations.name: halfLogMass_le_blocks

declarations.doc: **Paper C Corollary 5.4, the pigeonhole.** If the shell log-mass of `A` at `X ≥ 3` is at least `K (log X)^λ` with `0 < λ ≤ 1`, then some block `(y/2, y]` with `√X < y ≤ X` holds at least `(K/12) y (log y)^{λ-1}` members of `A`.
declarations.name: exists_block_of_shell

declarations.doc: **Paper C Corollary 5.4 (natural density, infinitely often), from a shell bound.** If `g_A(t) ≥ K t^λ` for all `t ≥ t₁`, with `0 < λ ≤ 1`, then there is `c > 0` such that for every large `X` some `y` with `√X < y ≤ X` has `#(A ∩ (y/2, y]) ≥ c y (log y)^{λ-1}`; the blocks found are distinct for `X` running through powers of `4`, so there are infinitely many.
declarations.name: natDensity_of_shell_bound

declarations.doc: **Paper C Corollary 5.4 for every `0 < λ ≤ 100/203`, with no hypothesis.** For every nonempty backward-closed `A`, on a dyadic block inside every shell `(√X, X]` with `X` large, `A` has natural density at least `c (log y)^{λ-1}`. Theorem 5.18 (`contagion_averaged`) supplies the shell bound.
declarations.name: natDensity_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(1), log-mass form.** The reach-one class `R` is backward-closed and contains `1`, so `Σ_{n ∈ R, n ≤ x} 1/n ≥ K (log x)^λ` for every `0 < λ ≤ 100/203`.
declarations.name: reachesOne_logMass_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(1), dyadic-block form.**
declarations.name: reachesOne_natDensity_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(2), dyadic-block form.** If some start `a` does not reach `1`, the failures have natural density at least `c (log y)^{λ-1}` on a dyadic block inside every large shell; the log-mass form is `Production.failures_logMass_averaged`.
declarations.name: failures_natDensity_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(3) for a cycle, log-mass form.** The basin of a state `m ≥ 1`, the starts whose orbit passes through `m`, is backward-closed and contains `m`; for a periodic `m` it is the basin of that cycle.
declarations.name: basin_logMass_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(3) for a cycle, dyadic-block form.**
declarations.name: basin_natDensity_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(3) for divergence, log-mass form.** If some orbit diverges, the divergent starts carry log-mass at least `K (log x)^λ`.
declarations.name: escapes_logMass_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(3) for divergence, dyadic-block form.**
declarations.name: escapes_natDensity_averaged

declarations.name: OneSidedShareExc.mono_err

declarations.name: mass_violators_le

declarations.doc: **Energy implies exceptional atoms.** If the bad energy at every depth `1 ≤ t < d` is at most `(q - 1/2)² exc² / 2^t`, the bad violators of the share bound `#[wO] ≤ q #[w]` have total mass at most `exc` at each depth, so the one-sided hypothesis holds with exceptional atoms of mass `exc` and no error term.

declarations.doc: The word count of `CylinderEnergy` over the odd starts of `(y, 2y]` is the cylinder.
declarations.name: wordCount_cylinder

declarations.doc: The unrestricted bias energy is the paper's `C_{t+1}/2 - C_t/4`, with `C_t = Σ_{|w|=t} #[w]²` (`CylinderEnergy.sum_bias_sq`).
declarations.name: biasEnergy_eq

declarations.doc: The energy hypothesis at the scale `y`: at every depth `1 ≤ t < d(y) = ⌈C L(y)⌉`, the bias energy of the `L(y)`-bad words is at most `(q - 1/2)² (y (log y)^{-B})² / 2^t`.
declarations.name: EnergyBound

declarations.doc: The energy hypothesis gives `H_q(C, A)` with exceptional atoms of mass `y (log y)^{-B}`, for every `A`.
declarations.name: oneSidedBoundExc_of_energy

declarations.doc: **The conjecture from the energy bound, with the contagion bound as a hypothesis.**
declarations.name: energy_conj_of_contagion

declarations.doc: **The conjecture from the energy bound, with nothing else assumed.** If at all large scales above a certified floor the bias energy of the `L(y)`-bad words at every depth `1 ≤ t < ⌈C L(y)⌉` is at most `(q - 1/2)² y² (log y)^{-2B} / 2^t`, with `C ≥ 5`, `1/2 < q < p_C`, `B > C log₂ x + 1 + e` and `27/40 < e < e_{C,q}`, then every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: energy_implies_conjecture

declarations.doc: The fiber's even-image count, as a count of half-cells. `evenImageCount` is defined by `Nat.sqrt (n^3) % 2 = 0`; `block_lock` counts `Int.fract (x j) < 1/2`. The two agree termwise, by the cell identity.
declarations.name: evenImageCount_eq_fract

declarations.doc: **(F3) of the note.** `ε_m H_m ≤ 0.6769` for `m ≥ 10^6`: the total drift of the fiber's step, `η_m H_m`, is bounded by an absolute constant well under one. Paper C's own form of this carries `1.02 m^{-1/3}` for the step gap and lands at `0.6903`; Lean's `upper_step_le` gives the sharper `ε_m = m^{-1/3}`, so the constant here is smaller and the note's `3.77` keeps room. It is the reason the block lock's `q/H` term has a bounded coefficient at all: without it, `q η_m H_m` could grow with `m`.
declarations.name: eps_mul_Hlen_le

declarations.doc: **Dirichlet's approximation theorem, reduced.** For every real `ξ` and `n ≥ 1` there is a fraction `p/q` in lowest terms with `1 ≤ q ≤ n` and `|q ξ - p| ≤ 1/(n+1)`. Mathlib's `Real.exists_nat_abs_mul_sub_round_le` supplies `q` and `p = round (q ξ)` without the coprimality, and `block_lock` needs it, since `gcd(p,q) = 1` is what makes the `q` points `y + i p/q` a full `1/q`-grid rather than a coarser one. Dividing through by `g = gcd(p,q)` costs nothing: `q/g ≤ q` and `|(q/g) ξ - p/g| = |q ξ - p| / g ≤ |q ξ - p|`, so both sides of the conclusion only improve. The division is done multiplicatively, through the witnesses of `g ∣ q` and `g ∣ p`, to keep integer-division casts out of it.
declarations.name: exists_coprime_approx

declarations.doc: **The block lock on a fiber.** For `m ≥ 1` and any rational approximation `p/q` to the fiber's lower step `A_m`, with `|q A_m - p| ≤ ρ` and `gcd(p, q) = 1`, \[ \Bigl| G_m - \frac{H_m}{2} \Bigr| \le 4(\rho + q\,\varepsilon_m) H_m + \frac{5 H_m}{2q} + q . \] This is `BlockLock.block_lock` with `x = xval ∘ nseq`, `a = A_m` and `η = ε_m`; the step interval is `step_ge` and `step_le`, and the count is matched by `evenImageCount_eq_fract`. Dividing by `H_m` gives the note's (1.1).
declarations.name: fiber_block_lock

declarations.doc: **Lemma 2 (lock).** A fiber whose parity share misses `1/2` by `η₀` or more has `A_m` within `32/(η₀ H_m)` of a rational with denominator at most `3.77/η₀`. The note's proof, with Dirichlet in place of the continued fractions it first used: take `θ = η₀/16` and `H₀ = ⌊θ H_m⌋`, get `q ≤ H₀` and `‖q A_m‖ ≤ 1/(H₀+1)` from `exists_coprime_approx` (which also supplies the coprimality `block_lock` wants), and feed them to `fiber_block_lock`. Of the three terms there, `4ρH ≤ 128/η₀` is at most `η₀H/10` exactly when `H_m ≥ 1280/η₀²`, and `4qε_mH + q ≤ 3.71q` by (F3), which is at most `0.232 η₀ H` because `q ≤ θH`. What is left is `0.668 η₀ ≤ 5/(2q)`.
declarations.name: fiber_lock

declarations.doc: The image `⌊n^{3/2}⌋` is even iff `{x(n)} < 1/2`, i.e. iff the half-cell of `x(n)` is even.
declarations.name: cell_xval_even_iff

declarations.doc: **Family 3 at the averaged coefficient.** For `U = ⌊√y''⌋ ≥ 10^6` satisfying Lemma 2's block hypotheses, and any shell `(s, y]` containing every fiber `Φ(m)` with `U < m ≤ y'' - 1`, the even-image parts of the non-poor fibers of the members of `A` in `(U, y'' - 1]` are disjoint odd members of `A` in the shell, of total log-mass at least `(c - ε_U)(Σ_{m ∈ A ∩ (U, y''-1]} 1/m - 2100 ε_U/η₀²)` with `c = (2/3)(1/2 - η₀)`.

Compare `errOE`, which carries `25/2` times the same `ε_U` because Paper C's pointwise Lemma 4.2 has to pay for goodness at every `m`.
declarations.name: errOEavg

declarations.doc: The additive error at the averaged coefficient. The first two terms are the boundary terms of the two drops, as in `errAdd`. The third is the poor-fibre tail `2100 ε_U/η₀²` carried through a coefficient of at most `1/3`; it is the only place `η₀` enters an error, and it is why the recursion's starting scale grows like `16 log(1/η₀)`.
declarations.name: errAddAvg

declarations.doc: **The production inequality with two productions, at the averaged coefficient.** For `0 < η₀ ≤ 1/4`, `t ≥ 40` and `t` past the scale where Lemma 2's block hypotheses bite, `(1 - errE t) g_A(t/2) + ((2/3)(1/2 - η₀) - errOEavg t) g_A(3t/4) - errAddAvg η₀ t ≤ g_A(t)`. Family 1 is Paper C's Lemma 3.1 unchanged; family 3 is `family_OE_averaged`, so the `2/9` of `production_two` is replaced by `(2/3)(1/2 - η₀)`, which exceeds `1/3 - 10^{-4}`. The shell geometry -- the three scales `t/2`, `3t/4`, `t`, the fibres landing in the shell, the two boundary drops -- is `production_two`'s, step for step. It is inlined rather than shared, because factoring it out would add a declaration to `FateProduction.lean`, one of the 83 inputs pinned by Paper C's release manifest. The copy is therefore deliberate, and `test_oe_rest_average.test_the_two_production_proofs_share_the_same_shell_geometry` re-extracts both blocks and fails if they ever drift apart. `hT` is the one new hypothesis, and it is exactly Lemma 2's two block conditions rewritten at `U = ⌊e^{3t/8}⌋`: `3(1280/η₀² + 1) ≤ e^{t/8}` gives `1280/η₀² ≤ (2/3)U^{1/3} - 1`, and that in turn gives `32/(η₀((2/3)U^{1/3} - 1)) ≤ 32/5120 < 1/2`. It is the whole cost of the averaging: it forces `t ≳ 16 log(1/η₀)`, and nothing else in the statement depends on `η₀`.
declarations.name: production_two_averaged

declarations.name: errorsAvg_le

declarations.doc: `ζ` is antitone in `λ` at the averaged coefficient too: both rates lie below `1`.
declarations.name: zeta2avg_antitone

declarations.doc: **Contagion at the averaged coefficient.** For every nonempty backward-closed `A`, every `0 < η₀ ≤ 1/4` and every `λ > 0` with `ζ(λ, η₀) = 2^{-λ} + (2/3)(1/2 - η₀)(3/4)^λ - 1 > 0`, there are `K > 0` and `t₁` with `g_A(t) ≥ K t^λ` for all `t ≥ t₁`. This is the statement the note actually proves, and it is the one worth reading: the exponent is not a constant of the argument but whatever `ζ` allows, so the supremum over `η₀ → 0` is the root of `2^{-λ} + (1/3)(3/4)^λ = 1`, `λ_ideal = 0.49265798…`. The supremum is approached and not attained, `η₀` being fixed before `x` -- exactly as Paper C's published statement is. The cost of a small `η₀` is entirely in `t₁`, which absorbs `8 log(3(1280/η₀² + 1))`: at the `η₀` that beats Paper C's `λ** = 0.4925715…` the starting scale is around `250`, so the implied `K` is tiny. Nothing else degrades.
declarations.name: contagion_averaged

declarations.doc: `ζ(100/203) > 0` at `η₀ = 10^{-5}`, by two rational bounds at the 203rd power: `0.710737 ≤ 2^{-100/203}` since `0.710737^{203} ≤ 2^{-100}`, and `0.867868 ≤ (3/4)^{100/203}` since `0.867868^{203} ≤ (3/4)^{100}`; then `0.710737 + (49999/150000)(0.867868) = 1.0000205 > 1`. `100/203 = 0.4926108…`, against the true root `λ_ideal = 0.4926579801…` of `2^{-λ} + (1/3)(3/4)^λ = 1`, and above Paper C's published `λ** = 0.4925715447…`, which is what this certificate exists to clear. It is chosen for margin, not minimality: `67/136` also lies in `(λ**, λ_ideal)` and has the smaller denominator, but leaves only `6.3·10^{-6}` of `ζ` at `η₀ = 0` against this one's `2.71·10^{-5}`, so it would force both a tenfold smaller `η₀` and sharper rational bounds for no gain in the theorem. (`33/67`, the previous convergent, falls just short of `λ**` outright.) The margin here, `2.05·10^{-5}`, is what `η₀ = 10^{-5}` leaves of that `2.71·10^{-5}`; break-even is `η₀ = 4.69·10^{-5}`. `oe_rest_average.exponent_certificate` re-derives all of it in exact arithmetic.
declarations.name: zeta2avg_pos

declarations.doc: **Contagion above Paper C's published exponent, as a log-mass bound, unconditionally.** For every nonempty backward-closed `A` and `0 < λ ≤ 100/203 = 0.4926108…` there are `K > 0` and `x₀` with `Σ_{n ∈ A, n ≤ x} 1/n ≥ K (log x)^λ` for all `x ≥ x₀`. This is Theorem 5.3 of Paper C at an exponent above its `λ** ≈ 0.4925715`, and with the hypothesis removed. What leaves the critical path is Proposition 4.4 and its two exponential-sum bounds -- the manuscript's largest unformalized gap -- together with the six-word ladder and Appendix D. Compare `logMass_contagion_elementary`, which is unconditional at `13/40 = 0.325` because it pays Lemma 4.2's pointwise `2/9`; the whole gain is that the poor fibres have finite total logarithmic mass, so the coefficient may be averaged instead.
declarations.name: logMass_contagion_averaged

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(2) at exponent `100/203`, unconditional.**
declarations.name: failures_logMass_averaged

declarations.doc: **Theorem 7.2 with its contagion hypothesis discharged at the averaged exponent.** If the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y (log y)^{-e}` for all large `y`, for some `e > 103/203 = 0.50739…`, then every positive integer reaches `1`. The threshold is `1 - λ`, so this is what the exponent buys: `conjecture_of_tao_rate` needs `e > 27/40 = 0.675` and Paper C's *conditional* form needs `e > 0.51`. The averaged coefficient puts the unconditional threshold below the manuscript's conditional one.
declarations.name: conjecture_of_tao_rate_averaged

declarations.doc: **Theorem 4 (poor-fiber tail), one dyadic block.** For `u ≥ 10^6` and `η₀ ∈ (0, 1/2]`, if the block's smallest fiber already satisfies Lemma 2's hypothesis (`1280/η₀² ≤ (2/3)u^{1/3} - 1`) and the resulting width is below `1/2`, then the `η₀`-poor `m ∈ (u, 2u]` are counted by Lemma 3 at the uniform width. The two lemmas meet here and nowhere else: `poor_resonant` turns poorness into resonance at this fiber's width, `resonant_mono` widens it to the block's, and `resonance_count_le'` counts. The note's `420 u^{2/3}/η₀²` is this bound with the arithmetic done; it is left symbolic so that the constant is the reader's to check against the note rather than Lean's to assert.

declarations.doc: `B_u = (2/3) u^{1/3} - 1 ≥ 0.6566 u^{1/3}` for `u ≥ 10^6`: the `-1` costs at most a hundredth of the main term once `u^{1/3} ≥ 100`.
declarations.name: B_ge

declarations.doc: **Theorem 4, the block count with an explicit constant.** `430 u^{2/3}/η₀²`. The note claims `420`. That figure assumed the second term of Lemma 3 was `Q(Q+1)/2`, the Gauss sum; `resonance_count_le'` delivers `Q(Q+1)`, because `arc_count_le` counts a half-open arc while `‖q A_m‖ ≤ δ` is closed, so each of the `Q` arcs is widened by one point. Carried through, `2·3.77·61.5 + 18 = 481.71` against `0.8825 u^{2/3}` gives `425.11`, so `420` is false and `430` is the honest constant. Nothing downstream moves: the note already records that only the positivity of the exponent matters, never the size of the constant.
declarations.name: poor_count_le'

declarations.doc: The block hypothesis only gets easier as `u` grows: `B_u` is increasing.
declarations.name: hB_mono

declarations.name: h

declarations.name: poor_block_logMass_le

declarations.doc: **(4.2) of the note.** For `U ≥ 10^6` satisfying the block hypotheses, and every `N`, the `η₀`-poor `m ∈ (U, N]` carry `1/m`-weighted mass at most `2100 U^{-1/3}/η₀²`. This is the summability that makes the poor set logarithmically finite, which is the whole content of the branch: there is nothing for an adversary to concentrate on. The argument is `bad_logMass_le`'s with a different summand.
declarations.name: poor_logMass_le

declarations.doc: **The non-poor fiber bound.** A fiber that is not `η₀`-poor carries even-image log-mass at least `(c - ε_m)/m`, where `c = (2/3)(1/2 - η₀)` is the note's §5 coefficient. This is `good_fiber_logMass_ge` with its input replaced: there the even count is `H_m/3 - 2` from Lemma 4.2, here it is `(1/2 - η₀)H_m` from not being poor, and `H_m` is `oeFiber_card_ge` in both. The error is written absolutely, `c - ε_m`, rather than relatively as the `2/9(1 - (25/2)ε_m)` of the original: a relative form carries a constant of size `1/c`, which blows up as `η₀` approaches `1/2`, while the absolute form has no constant at all.
declarations.name: nonpoor_fiber_logMass_ge

declarations.doc: The pressure hypothesis `P_θ(C)` at the scale `y`, with the paper's `e^{o(d)}` quantified as `(log y)^ε`: the live pressure of `{1, …, 2y}` at the tilt `x = p_C/(1-p_C)` and depth `d(y) = ⌈C L(y)⌉` is at most `2y a_θ^{d(y)} (log y)^ε`.
declarations.name: PressureBound

declarations.doc: The no-momentum hypothesis `M_{θ,q}(C)` at the scale `y`: on the live weight of `{1, …, 2y}` at the re-centring tilt `x = p_C(1-q)/(q(1-p_C))`, the excess odd shares `(s_x(t) - q)^+` over the depths `t < d(y)` sum to at most `δ d(y)`.
declarations.name: NoMomentumBound

declarations.doc: The exponent `C (D(p_C ‖ q) - c_x δ) / log 2` of Proposition 9.3 under no momentum, with `c_x = (x - 1)/a_q` at the re-centring tilt.
declarations.name: momentumExponent

declarations.doc: **The shared absorption.** A bound `2y e^{-d(y) D} (log y)^ε` on the odd failures of `(y, 2y]` at all large scales, with `d(y) = ⌈C L(y)⌉` and `D ≥ 0`, is below `y (log y)^{-e}` for every `e < C D / log 2 - ε` and all large `y`.
declarations.name: absorb

declarations.doc: **Theorem 9.2 absorbed.** Under `P_θ(C)` at all large scales with the loss `ε`, the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y (log y)^{-e}` for every `e < e(C) - ε` and all large `y`.
declarations.name: oddFailures_le_of_pressure

declarations.doc: **Theorem 9.2's corollary, with the contagion bound as a hypothesis.**

declarations.doc: **Theorem 9.2's corollary with nothing else assumed.** The pressure hypothesis `P_θ(C)` at all large scales above a certified floor, with `C ≥ 5` and a loss `ε` such that `27/40 < e < e(C) - ε` for some `e` (a negative `ε` is a stronger hypothesis), gives that every positive integer reaches `1`.
declarations.name: pressure_implies_conjecture

declarations.doc: **Proposition 9.3 absorbed.** Under `M_{θ,q}(C)` at all large scales with the momentum `δ`, the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y (log y)^{-e}` for every `0 ≤ e < C (D(p_C ‖ q) - c_x δ) / log 2` and all large `y`.

declarations.doc: **Proposition 9.3's corollary, with the contagion bound as a hypothesis.**

declarations.name: noMomentum_implies_conjecture

declarations.doc: `ζ(13/40) = 2^{-13/40} + (2/9)(3/4)^{13/40} - 1 > 0`, by two rational bounds: `0.798 ≤ (1/2)^{13/40}` since `0.798^{40} ≤ 2^{-13}`, and `0.91 ≤ (3/4)^{13/40}` since `0.91^{40} ≤ (3/4)^{13}`; then `0.798 + (2/9)(0.91) = 1.000222 > 1`. `13/40 = 0.325` against the true root `0.3261209621…` of `2^{-λ} + (2/9)(3/4)^λ = 1`, so this certificate reaches `99.6%` of what the two-production inequality can give. The earlier certificate was `λ = 3/10`, which reached `92%`.
declarations.name: zeta2_pos

declarations.doc: `ζ` is antitone in `λ`: both rates lie below `1`.
declarations.name: zeta2_antitone

declarations.doc: The errors vanish: past `T = max 0 (8 log(139/ε))` all three are at most `ε`.
declarations.name: errors_vanish

declarations.doc: **Elementary contagion.** For every nonempty backward-closed `A` and `0 < λ ≤ 13/40` there are `K > 0` and `t₁` with `g_A(t) ≥ K t^λ` for all `t ≥ t₁`. No hypothesis: the seed is Lemma 5.2, the recursion is Lemma 5.1 on the two productions `E` and `OE`, and the production inequality is `production_two`, whose inputs are Lemmas 3.1, 4.2 and 4.3.
declarations.name: contagion_elementary

declarations.doc: **Elementary contagion, as a log-mass bound.** For every nonempty backward-closed `A` and `0 < λ ≤ 13/40` there are `K > 0` and `x₀` with `Σ_{n ∈ A, n ≤ x} 1/n ≥ K (log x)^λ` for all `x ≥ x₀`. This is Theorem 5.3 of the paper with `13/40` in place of `λ** ≈ 0.4926`, and with no hypothesis: the block-average family and the ladder, which need the exponential sums, are what lift the exponent.
declarations.name: logMass_contagion_elementary

declarations.doc: **Corollary 5.5(2) at exponent `13/40`, unconditional.** If some positive integer does not reach `1`, the failures have log-mass at least `K (log x)^{13/40}` up to `x` for all large `x`: the failure set is backward-closed (Lemma 2.1) and nonempty.
declarations.name: failures_logMass_ge

declarations.doc: **Theorem 7.2 with its contagion hypothesis discharged.** If the odd failures in `(y, 2y]` number at most `y (log y)^{-e}` for all large `y`, for some `e > 27/40`, then every positive integer reaches `1`. The contagion bound at exponent `13/40` is `failures_logMass_ge`, so nothing is assumed beyond the rate; the paper's conditional form needs `e > 0.51` and the production inequality (5.2). The threshold is `1 - λ` for the `λ` the contagion bound reaches, so lifting that exponent to `13/40` lowered it from `7/10` to `27/40`.
declarations.name: conjecture_of_tao_rate

declarations.doc: **Corollary 8.4 with its contagion hypothesis discharged.** A cylinder bound `H(C, A)` at all large scales with `A > C + e(C)` and `e(C) > 27/40`, above a certified floor `N₀`, gives the conjecture; nothing else is assumed.
declarations.name: conjecture_of_cylinder_bound

The reason is that `V_i` closes with a second `E` exactly where `V_j`, for `j > i`, opens another `OE`.

declarations.doc: `m` is `(Q, δ)`-resonant: some `q` with `1 ≤ q ≤ Q` has `‖q A_m‖ ≤ δ`, the distance from `q A_m` to the nearest integer. Written as `∃ P : ℤ, |q A_m - P| ≤ δ`, the house spelling of `‖·‖` (compare `Good`, which unpacks the same notion into `Int.fract` inequalities).
declarations.name: Resonant

declarations.doc: `1 / ε_n = n^{1/3}`; the form in which the note writes the step floor of a dyadic block.
declarations.name: one_div_eps

declarations.doc: The Gauss sum behind Lemma 3, already multiplied through by the per-arc bound: `Σ_{q < Q} W (2δ/E + 2(q+1)) = W (2Qδ/E + Q(Q+1))`.
declarations.name: sum_range_arc_terms

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3, the reduction.** If `|q A_m - P| ≤ δ` for some integer `P`, with `1 ≤ q` and `0 ≤ δ < 1/2`, then `A_m` lies within `δ/q` of the grid point `p/q` for some `p < q`, modulo one; after the shift by `δ/q` that two-sided arc is the single non-wrapping arc `[0, 2δ/q]`. This is the `q`-fold form of `bad_mem_arc`, and the shift is the same trick.
declarations.name: resonant_mem_arc

declarations.doc: **The window count.** On `(u, 2u]` the shifted sequence `A_m + c` meets at most `0.882 u^{2/3} + 2` integer windows, for every real shift `c`: the shift cancels in `A_{2u} - A_{u+1}`, so this is `Am_double_sub_le` with two floors. It is the disjunction-free form of the `hwin` block inside `bad_count_le`.
declarations.name: Am_window_le

declarations.doc: **The shifted arc count.** For `u ≥ 10^6`, a real shift `c` and a width `w ≥ 0`, the `m ∈ (u, 2u]` with `{A_m + c} < w` number at most `(0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(w/ε_{2u} + 1)`: the step floor on the block is `ε_{2u}` (`Am_step_ge`, `eps_antitone`), so this is `arc_count_le` composed with `Am_window_le`.
declarations.name: shifted_arc_count_le

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3, one denominator.** For `u ≥ 10^6`, `1 ≤ q` and `0 ≤ δ < 1/2`, the `m ∈ (u, 2u]` with `‖q A_m‖ ≤ δ` number at most `(0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(2δ/ε_{2u} + 2q)`. The set is covered by the `q` arcs `{A_m - p/q + δ/q} < 2δ/q + ε_{2u}`, `p < q` (`resonant_mem_arc`), and each of them is counted by `shifted_arc_count_le`.
declarations.name: resonance_count_one

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3 (arc count).** For `u ≥ 10^6`, every `Q` and every `δ` with `0 ≤ δ < 1/2`, the `(Q, δ)`-resonant `m ∈ (u, 2u]` number at most `(0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(2 Q δ / ε_{2u} + Q(Q+1))`. The denominators are indexed as `q + 1` over `Finset.range Q`, and each contributes `resonance_count_one`; the Gauss sum `Σ_{q < Q} 2(q+1) = Q(Q+1)` is `sum_range_arc_terms`.
declarations.name: resonance_count_le

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3, the note's form.** The same count with `1/ε_{2u}` written as `(2u)^{1/3}`: `#{m ∈ (u, 2u] : ∃ q ≤ Q, ‖q A_m‖ ≤ δ} ≤ (0.882 u^{2/3} + 2)(2 Q δ (2u)^{1/3} + Q(Q+1))`.
declarations.name: resonance_count_le'

declarations.doc: The fibre decomposition of a majorant that is constant on classes.
declarations.name: sum_comp_fin_six

declarations.doc: **Theorem 4.7's six-term bound.** Given the classification of the orbit — which is where Theorem 3.2 and the packing enter, and is a hypothesis here — the inverse-log sum is at most the count-weighted sum of the six class bounds. On a cycle the counts are the paper's `1, o−e−1, 2e−o, 1, o−e−1, e`.
declarations.name: sixTerm_bound

declarations.doc: A cycle state that is odd and is not the minimum is at least `n + 2`: minimality gives `≥ n`, and parity excludes `n + 1`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_odd_ne_ge

declarations.doc: The expensive valley: an odd state whose image is at least `n²` satisfies `n⁴ ≤ v³`.
declarations.name: odd_pow_ge_of_image_ge

declarations.doc: Paper A's `v`: the least odd integer whose cube is at least `n⁴`.
declarations.name: expensiveValley

declarations.doc: **The expensive valley, with no hypothesis left.** An odd cycle state whose successor is even satisfies `n⁴ ≤ v³`. Theorem 3.2 is not needed for this step: the successor *is* an even cycle state, and `cycleMin_even_ge_sq` already bounds every even state below by `n²`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_oe_start_pow_ge

declarations.doc: So an `OE`-start is at least `v`, which is the third of the six class bounds — and it is now a theorem rather than a hypothesis.
declarations.name: cycleMin_oe_start_ge

declarations.doc: **The first internal odd.** The successor of any odd cycle state is at least `t = J(n)`, since the state is odd and at least `n`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_internal_ge_t

declarations.doc: **The later internal odds.** If the odd predecessor is not the minimum it is at least `n + 2`, so the successor is at least `t₊ = J(n+2)`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_internal_ge_tplus

declarations.doc: **The packing bound.** At most `o − e` blocks have a run of two or more, where `o` is the total odd count `runs.sum` and `e` the number of blocks `runs.length`. Stated without natural subtraction.
declarations.name: blocks_ge_two_add_length_le_sum

declarations.doc: **Equality is exactly the packing.** The bound above is tight iff every run has length one or two — so `(o−e)` blocks of `OOE` with `(2e−o)` of `OE` is not one admissible configuration among many, it is the unique maximiser of the cheap-valley count.
declarations.name: blocks_ge_two_eq_sum_iff

declarations.doc: The two block types exhaust the blocks: a run has length one or at least two.
declarations.name: blocks_filter_split

declarations.doc: Hence at least `2e − o` blocks are single-odd `OE` circuits, which is the count of expensive valleys in Theorem 4.7's display.
declarations.name: blocks_eq_one_ge

declarations.doc: The expensive valley clears `n + 2`. Any odd `w ≤ n` has `w³ ≤ n³ < n⁴`, so the least odd `v` with `n⁴ ≤ v³` exceeds `n`; both are odd, so it clears `n + 2`.
declarations.name: le_expensiveValley

declarations.doc: **The swap.** With the valley total fixed, fewer cheap valleys means a smaller majorant.
declarations.name: valley_swap_le

declarations.doc: The cheap-valley majorant dominates the expensive one, which is what makes the swap downhill: `1/(v log v) ≤ 1/((n+2) log (n+2))` once `n + 2 ≤ v`.
declarations.name: expensive_le_cheap

declarations.doc: **Theorem 4.7's display from the packing inequality.** `sixTerm_bound` needs the six cardinalities exactly; the packing supplies the valley split as inequalities — at most `k₁` cheap valleys with the valley total fixed. Since `n + 2 ≤ v` the swap is downhill, so the paper's counts dominate whatever the actual split is.
declarations.name: sixTerm_bound_packed

declarations.doc: The cyclic predecessor of an index in `range L`.
declarations.name: cycPred

declarations.doc: **Every odd letter is a valley or an internal.**
declarations.name: valley_add_internal

declarations.doc: **Valleys inject into even letters** by taking the cyclic predecessor.
declarations.name: valley_le_even

declarations.doc: **Hence at least `o − e` internals**, which is the direction the majorant needs.
declarations.name: odd_le_internal_add_even

declarations.doc: **Majorization on three classes.** Decreasing contributions, partial sums dominated, equal totals.
declarations.name: majorize_three

declarations.doc: An odd state never exceeds its own image: `x ≤ J(x)`, since `x² ≤ x³`.
declarations.name: le_floorPower_odd

declarations.doc: The internal majorant is below the cheap-valley majorant: `1/(t₊ log t₊) ≤ 1/((n+2) log (n+2))`, because `n + 2 ≤ J(n+2)`.
declarations.name: internal_le_cheap

declarations.doc: **The expensive valley sits below the first internal**: `v ≤ t = J(n)` for odd `n ≥ 9`. The route through `n³ ≤ t²` forces a `3/2` exponent and lands on a degree-nine comparison. Naming the witness avoids it entirely. With `s = ⌊√n⌋` and `s'` the largest odd number at most `s`, the witness is `n·s'`: * `(n s')² = n² s'² ≤ n² · n = n³`, so `n s' ≤ ⌊√(n³)⌋ = t`; * `(n s')³ = n³ s'³ ≥ n³ · n = n⁴`, since `n < (s+1)² ≤ s'³` once `s ≥ 3`; * and `n s'` is odd, being a product of two odds. Everything is degree three.
declarations.name: expensiveValley_le_floorPower

declarations.doc: And below the later internals: `v ≤ t₊ = J(n+2)`, by monotonicity of `J` on odds.
declarations.name: expensiveValley_le_floorPower_succ

declarations.doc: **The last ordering.** The internal majorant sits below the expensive-valley majorant, so the three class contributions are linearly ordered — cheap, expensive, internal — and `majorize_three` applies to Theorem 4.7's display.
declarations.name: internal_le_expensive

declarations.doc: **The minimum's successor is odd**, so the minimum is always a *cheap* valley. Theorem 4.7's display puts one valley at `n` and `o−e−1` further cheap ones at `n+2`, for `o−e` cheap valleys in all. That is only an upper bound if the minimum is one of them: if the minimum started an `OE` circuit there could be `o−e` cheap valleys *besides* it, and the majorant would exceed the display, since `1/((n+2)log(n+2)) > 1/(v log v)`. It cannot. If `J(n)` were even it would be an even cycle state, hence at least `n²` by `cycleMin_even_ge_sq`; but `J(n) = ⌊√(n³)⌋ < n²` because `n³ < n⁴`. So the minimum is followed by another odd letter and sits in a block with a run of at least two.
declarations.name: cycleMin_succ_odd

declarations.doc: On a realized itinerary the letter at `i` is odd exactly when the state is.
declarations.name: follows_get_odd_iff

declarations.doc: `J(n) > n` for odd `n ≥ 3`, since `(n+1)² ≤ n³`.
declarations.name: lt_floorPower_odd

declarations.doc: **The cycle's last state is even.** Were it odd, the return `J(x) = n` with `x ≥ n` odd would force `x = n` and hence `J(n) = n`, which `lt_floorPower_odd` forbids. So the word ends in `E`, the even letters outnumber the valleys, and the prefix count gives `#valleys ≤ e`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_last_even

declarations.doc: The three class bounds: the minimum, the first internal, and the even floor.
declarations.name: threeBounds

declarations.doc: **The three-term bound.** Valleys charged at `n`, internals at `t`, evens at `n²`; the valley count may be replaced by any larger `kA` with the total held fixed, since `n ≤ t` makes the exchange downhill. No `EE` hypothesis.

declarations.doc: `J` fixes only `1` among positive integers: even states strictly descend and odd states at least `3` strictly ascend.
declarations.name: floorPower_eq_self_iff

declarations.doc: A cycle has period at least two: period one would make its minimum a fixed point.
declarations.name: cycleMin_length_ge_two

declarations.doc: **Every cycle itinerary reads `OO…E`.** It starts odd because the minimum is odd; its second letter is odd because the minimum cannot start an `OE` circuit; and it ends even because the return would otherwise fix the minimum. declarations.doc: **The certified comparison, in one statement.** `cycleMin_defect_finance` bounds the relative defect by the `6/5` unroll of the inverse-log sum, and `cycleMin_threeTerm` bounds that sum by the three-term charge. The floor `400` is the one `cycleMin_defect_finance` carries; the published table runs at `n > 10^6`.

declarations.doc: Gap-cell identity (Lemma B pattern): the increment of `⌊·⌋` across a shift `δ` is `⌊δ⌋` plus the carry `𝟙[{x} ≥ 1 − {δ}]`.
