declarations.doc: Level-2 gap identity (Lemma N pattern): along any real-valued sequence `Y`, the integer gap `⌊Y (n+h)⌋ − ⌊Y n⌋` is the floor of the smooth increment plus a 0/1 carry read off the fractional parts. With `Y = (m ∘ ·)^{3/2}` this is the companion's `g₂ = ⌊ΔY⌋ + κ₂`.
declarations.name: seq_floor_gap

declarations.doc: The carry of the gap identity is 0 or 1.
declarations.name: gap_carry_mem

declarations.doc: Double-gap identity (Lemma R2 of the two-step parity companion): the second difference of the level-2 gap `g₂ n = ⌊Y (n+h₁)⌋ − ⌊Y n⌋` along a shift `h₂` is the floor of the double increment `Δ₂Δ₁Y` plus a 0/1 carry on the first increment plus the difference of the two Lemma-N carries. Two composed instances of `seq_floor_gap`.
declarations.name: seq_floor_gap_second

declarations.doc: Carry as a difference of sawtooths (Lemma 5.1(ii) of the parity-discrepancy note): the 0/1 carry `𝟙[{a} + {b} ≥ 1]` equals `{a} + {b} − {a + b}` exactly, for all reals. This is the identity that lets the kernel argument expand each carry additively by finite Fourier series.
declarations.name: carry_eq_fract_add_sub_fract

declarations.doc: The exact product rule for second differences over four base points (the algebraic skeleton of the master identity, Lemma 5.1(iv) of the parity-discrepancy note): with the values of `c` and `f` at `n`, `n+d₁`, `n+d₂`, `n+d₁+d₂` written `ca, cb, cc, cd` and `fa, fb, fc, fd`, the doubly differenced product decomposes into the doubly differenced `f` weighted by the shifted `c`, two mixed terms, and the doubly differenced `c` weighted by `f`.
declarations.name: second_difference_product_rule

declarations.doc: Parity bridge: `⌊x⌋` is odd exactly when `{x/2} ≥ 1/2`. This is the exact fractional-part reduction that converts the parity sums of the discrepancy program into interval discrepancies.
declarations.name: floor_odd_iff_half_le_fract_half

declarations.doc: Gap transfer (Theorem 4.10): with `Λ = o log 3 − L log 2`, `n log n · min(Λ, 1) ≤ 2 L` for every cycle minimum `n ≥ 2`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_gap_transfer

declarations.doc: Any lower bound `ε ≤ 1` on the linear form `o log 3 − L log 2` transfers to the floor-free length bound `n log n · ε ≤ 2 L`. With Rhin's effective measure `ε = e^{−13.3(0.46057 + log L)}` (a hypothesis here, classical in the literature) this is Paper A Corollary 4.11.
declarations.name: cycleMin_length_of_gap

declarations.doc: The weaker printed Rhin budget `e^{−6.1256} L^{−13.3}`.
declarations.name: rhinBudget

declarations.doc: For `L ≥ 1` the printed budget is at most one.
declarations.name: rhinBudget_le_one

declarations.doc: **Corollary 4.11, first display.** Rhin's printed lower bound `L^{−13.3} ≤ Λ` is a hypothesis. The calculator comparison `2 e^{6.1256} < 915` is not used.
declarations.name: cycleMin_length_of_rhin

declarations.doc: The Diophantine budget `C * L^{-p}` fed to `cycleMin_length_of_gap`.
declarations.name: gapBudget

declarations.doc: For `L >= 1`, `C <= 1` and `p >= 0` the budget is at most one, which is what `cycleMin_length_of_gap` needs.
declarations.name: gapBudget_le_one

declarations.doc: **Power-budget gap transfer.** A Diophantine lower bound `C * L^{-p} <= o log 3 - L log 2` on a cycle gives the floor-free length bound `n log n <= (2/C) * L^{p+1}`. Instances: `p = 13.3`, `C = e^{-6.1256}` is Paper A Corollary 4.11 (Rhin, effective). `p = 4.1163051` is the Wu-Wang instance, exponent `5.1163051`, with `C = C_eps` implied.
declarations.name: cycleMin_length_of_gap_power

declarations.doc: **The same inequality read as a period lower bound.** Under the same Diophantine budget, a nontrivial cycle of minimum `n` has period at least `(C * n log n / 2)^{1/(p+1)}`. No descent floor enters: the bound grows with the minimum, which is the one direction the finite tables cannot supply. At `p = 13.3` (Rhin) the exponent in `n` is `1/14.3 = 0.0699...`; at `p = 4.1163051` (Wu-Wang) it is `1/5.1163051 = 0.1954...`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_period_ge

declarations.doc: **The closure threshold.** If the Diophantine budget holds on every nontrivial cycle and cycle minima obey the matching lower bound `n log n > (2/C) L^{p+1}`, then every cycle word based at a minimum `n >= 2` is empty: there is no nontrivial cycle. This is the numerical content of the standing reopen condition "a lower bound on the cycle minimum in terms of the period" (`docs/problems/juggler_cycle_method_ceilings.md`). Neither hypothesis is proved here. The Wu-Wang instance `p = 4.1163051` sets the unconditional target at `n >> L^{5.1163051}`; since `p >= 1` for every irrational, no instance of this scheme can ask for less than `n >> L^{2}`.
declarations.name: no_cycleMin_of_gap_and_minimum

declarations.doc: **Wu-Wang instance of the transfer.** `C * L^{-4.1163051} <= Lambda` gives `n log n <= (2/C) L^{5.1163051}`, against Corollary 4.11's `L^{14.3}`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_length_of_wuWang

declarations.doc: **Wu-Wang period lower bound.** Every nontrivial cycle has `L >= (C n log n / 2)^{1/5.1163051}`, floor-free.
declarations.name: cycleMin_period_ge_wuWang

declarations.doc: **The exponent walk is the rotation orbit.** With `u_k = a_k·log₂3 − k`, the walk position is `log₂3` times the fractional part of `k·θ` — so `C_L`, the average of the observable along the walk, is a Birkhoff average of the rotation by `θ`.

declarations.doc: **The ergodic sum is the walk sum.** This is what Lemma 5.6's "in particular `C_L` is a Birkhoff average of the rotation" means: at phase `0`, the `k`-th term of the rotation's ergodic sum is the observable at the exponent walk's position after `k` steps. declarations.doc: **The sawtooth form of the carry**, the elementary identity the manuscript displays: `[{A}+{B} ≥ 1] = {A} + {B} - {A+B}`. Both sides equal `{A}+{B}-{A+B}` because `{A}+{B} ∈ [0,2)`.
declarations.name: carry_as_sawtooth

declarations.doc: **The substitution engine.** One step of the level-2 bookkeeping: the increment of the defect `θ₂ = {Y}` across a shift equals the sawtooth of the gap minus the carry. Every substitution in Lemma 5.1(iv) is this lemma.
declarations.name: fract_diff_level2

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(ii), the double gap.** With `v = ⌊Y⌋`, `g₂ = Δ₁v`, `W = Δ₁Y` and `ΔΔY = Δ₂W`, the second difference of the integer part is `Δ₂g₂ = ⌊ΔΔY⌋ + κ'' + Δ₂κ₂` — two applications of the carry identity, first to `Y` at shift `d₁`, then to `W` at shift `d₂`.
declarations.name: lemma51_double_gap

declarations.doc: **The product rule over four base points.** With `ΔΔg = g₁₂ - g₁ - g₂ + g₀`, `(Δ₂c)(n+d₁) = c₁₂ - c₁` and `(Δ₁c)(n+d₂) = c₁₂ - c₂`, `ΔΔ(cf) = c₁₁·ΔΔf + (Δ₂c)(n+d₁)·Δ₁f + (Δ₁c)(n+d₂)·Δ₂f + (ΔΔc)·f`. The manuscript says "verified by expanding both sides over the four base points"; that expansion is `ring`.
declarations.name: double_difference_product

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(iv), the master identity.** The doubly differenced kernel phase `ΔΔ(c·θ₂)`, with `θ₂ = {Y}` the level-2 defect, decomposes exactly into four terms, in each of which the non-smooth factor is a *bounded* bracket: * `(ΔΔc)·θ₂`, with `θ₂ ∈ [0,1)`; * `(Δ₂c)(n+d₁)·({W} - κ₂)`, with `W = Δ₁Y` and `κ₂` the level-2 carry; * `(Δ₁c)(n+d₂)·({W'} - κ₂')`, with `W' = Δ₂Y`; * `c₁₁·({ΔΔY} - κ'' - Δ₂κ₂)`. No unbounded smooth part survives the differencing — which is the whole purpose of the lemma. The proof is the product rule of Section 3 together with three applications of `fract_diff_level2`.
declarations.name: lemma51_master

declarations.doc: **Every bracket is bounded by `2`.** This is what the decomposition buys: the three carry brackets and the defect itself are all `O(1)`, so the doubly differenced phase carries no growing amplitude.
declarations.name: lemma51_brackets_le_two

declarations.doc: **The first mean value theorem, made explicit.** In root coordinates `a = √A`, `b = √(A+j)`, the increment of `x^(3/2)` is `(3/2)(b² - a²)·c` with `c = (2/3)(a² + ab + b²)/(a + b)`, and `a ≤ c ≤ b`. So `ξ₁ = c² - A` lies between `0` and `j`, exactly as the manuscript needs — with no appeal to the mean value theorem.

declarations.doc: **The inner mean value, made explicit.** For `F' = (3/2)x^(1/2)` and `F'' = (3/4)x^(-1/2)`, the increment `F'(A+B) - F'(A)` equals `B·F''(η)` *exactly*, with `√η` the **arithmetic mean** of `√A` and `√(A+B)`. Written in root coordinates `a = √A`, `b = √(A+B)`: `(3/2)(b - a) = (b² - a²)·(3/4)/((a+b)/2)`, and `(a+b)/2 ∈ [a, b]`.
declarations.name: mvt_sqrt_diff_explicit

declarations.doc: **The manuscript's own form of the second mean value.** There is a genuine `ξ₂ ∈ [m, m+β₁+β₂]` with `D = β₁β₂ F''(ξ₂)`, `F'' = (3/4)x^(-1/2)`. The witness is `√ξ₂ = (3/4)β₁β₂/D`, and the two-sided bound above is exactly what places it in range.

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1(iii) is now unconditional.** The two mean values the manuscript appeals to are supplied: the first explicitly (`mvt_cube_explicit`), the second through one application of the mean value theorem plus the explicit inner witness (`second_difference_two_sided`). declarations.doc: **The two digit implementations are the same algorithm.** `greedyDigits` folds `(r, ds) ↦ (r % q, ds ++ [r / q])` over the descending list `thetaDenomsDesc`, while `ostroDigit thetaDenomFn L 12 i` is `ostroRem … i / thetaDenomFn (12 - i)` with `ostroRem … (i+1) = ostroRem … i % thetaDenomFn (12 - i)`; and `thetaDenomFn (12 - i)` for `i = 0 … 12` *is* `thetaDenomsDesc`, entry for entry. So the fold's step and the recursion's step coincide, and unfolding thirteen levels of each leaves the same thirteen atoms in a different association. This replaces a compiled-runtime scan of all `301994` window lengths, and is stronger than it: the scan bounded `L`, and there was never any reason to.

Retiring it costs the sharpening and nothing else: no theorem, kill or period bound consumed the `37`, the downstream results already use this structural cap, and `window_digit_max` still records — kernel-checked — that `37` is attained at `L = 275632`. The window's lower endpoint is no longer needed and is kept only so the interface Paper A's appendix names is unchanged: `greedyDigitSum_le` holds for every `L < 301994`, so the structural bound is the more general statement.

declarations.doc: **Step (i) of Lemma 5.2b.** The wave replacement, under the middle-band cap `u ≤ 300 k h₂ P^(1/8)` — which *is* the band condition `μ ≤ 60 λ₀`, since `60·4.2/0.84 = 300`. Powers enter only through `p18 = P^(1/8)`, `p54 = P^(-5/4)`, `p98 = P^(-9/8)` and the relation `p18 · p54 = p98`. The conclusion carries the shape `k(h₁+h₂)`, which is what lets it combine with step (ii) *before* conversion — the step the earlier draft skipped, bounding and converting the two terms separately and printing `202.5 + 16 = 219`. The constant is `(9/32)·300 = 84.375`, printed as `84.38`. The cap is `300` and not `186` because of the erratum at Lemma 5.2b: the anchor curvature is `27/128`, not `135/1024`, and `λ₀`'s ceiling `2.6` opens to `4.2`. The superseded chain is kept below under `_precorrection`, as `step5b_c7_printed` keeps the manuscript's weaker `1/288`.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_i

declarations.doc: The same step under the pre-correction anchor `135/1024`, where the cap was `186 = 60·2.6/0.84` and the constant `(9/32)·186 = 52.3125`. Retained because the manuscript's erratum lists `186 → 300` and `52.9 → 85.3` explicitly, and a reader checking that list should find both ends of it here.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_i_precorrection

declarations.doc: **Step (ii) of Lemma 5.2b.** The `β`-product replacement contributes `(27/128)·4.3 = 0.9070`, printed as `0.91`. The manuscript notes that `0.95` would not do, because it pushes the sum in (i) past `85.3`; both halves of that are recorded here.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_ii_constant

declarations.doc: The same constant under the pre-correction anchor, `(135/1024)·4.3 = 0.567`, printed as `0.57`; the erratum's factor is exactly `8/5`. An earlier draft carried `8` here — fourteen times the pre-correction value — and that `8` is the source of the `16` in the old `219 = 202.5 + 16`.
declarations.name: interpolant_step_ii_precorrection

declarations.doc: **The assembly.** Steps (i) and (ii) share the shape `k(h₁+h₂)P^(-9/8)`, so they add before conversion: `84.38 + 0.91 = 85.29`. Then `k(h₁+h₂) ≤ 2 P^(1/12)` by (C3),(C4) gives `170.58 ≤ 170.6`, with `p112 = P^(1/12)`, `p2524 = P^(-25/24)` and `p112 · p98 = p2524`. The manuscript prints the rounder `171`; `170.6` is what `p0_certificate.interpolant_error` uses and is what the nine anchor rows of the threshold certificate are solved against.
declarations.name: interpolant_assembly

declarations.doc: The same assembly under the pre-correction anchor: `52.32 + 0.57 = 52.89` and `105.78 ≤ 106`.
declarations.name: interpolant_assembly_precorrection

declarations.doc: The gain over the earlier `219`, on the `P^(-25/24)` coefficient: `1.28`, which is what Appendix A.5 claims. The pre-correction chain gave `106` and so a factor above `2`; the erratum at Lemma 5.2b spends most of that back, and `1.28` is what is left. The second term `0.11 P^(-5/6)` of the interpolant error is untouched and is co-dominant at `P₀`, so the *total* error gains less than either figure there.
declarations.name: interpolant_gain

declarations.doc: **The differenced (D3) budget is dominated**, at margin 4 and better: `6 K h P^(-13/8) ≤ ¼ · 0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` reduces, after multiplying by `p^39`, to `6K ≤ 0.0875 u p^21`, which holds by `K ≤ p^3` and `u ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_differenced_dominated

declarations.doc: **The undifferenced budget is not dominated.** At the (C1) extreme `K = p^3` and `u = h = 1`, the ratio of `3 K P^(-5/8)` to the Stage-4 curvature `0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` is `(3/0.35) p^6 = 8.57 P^(1/4)` -- it exceeds the curvature by an unbounded factor, so Lemma 3.3 at that scale does not apply and the two can cancel outright.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_printed_not_dominated

declarations.doc: **The size of the gap.** The undifferenced budget exceeds the differenced one by exactly `P/(2h) = p^24/(2h)`; at `h ≤ P^(1/8)` that is at least `½P^(7/8)`.
declarations.name: stage6_D3_gap

declarations.doc: **Regime A: the undifferenced budget is dominated.** `3 K P^(-5/8) ≤ ¼·0.35 u h P^(-3/4)` holds as soon as `u h ≥ (12/0.35) K P^(1/8)`, and `12/0.35 = 34.28…`. Written at `P = p^24`, after multiplying by `p^15`.
declarations.name: wideD3_regimeA_dominated

declarations.doc: **Regime B is a small-`uh` regime.** By (C1), `K ≤ p^3`, so regime B forces `u h < 34.3 p^3 = 34.3 P^(1/8)`… and with `u h ≤ P^(1/2)` from the hypotheses of (i) this is the range where the Stage-4 curvature is weakest.
declarations.name: wideD3_regimeB_small

declarations.doc: **The frozen `G` steps by one, so `f'` jumps at every cell boundary.** The jump is `(9/8) u (ν+2h)^(-1/4)`; the point is only that it is *bounded below*, which no choice of the continuous decoration can affect. Over `N` cells the total sweep of `f'` is at least `N` times that.
declarations.name: wideD3_frequency_sweep

declarations.doc: **The cells are flat in regime B.** At the sawtooth curvature scale `0.282 u P^(-5/4)`, over a cell of length `ℓ ≤ 0.95 P^(1/2)/h` the phase departs from linear by `≤ 0.282 u P^(-5/4) ℓ² ≤ 0.26 u P^(-1/4) h^(-2)`, so the second-derivative test is the wrong tool and Kusmin–Landau is the right one.
declarations.name: wideD3_cells_flat

declarations.doc: **Regime B, case (a): the dyadic Kusmin–Landau total is the printed second term.** A cell total `(ℓ/q)^(1/2)` summed over `1.5 h P^(1/2)` cells, with `ℓ ≤ 0.95 P^(1/2)/h` and `q ≥ 0.946 u P^(-1/4)`, gives `≤ 1.6 (h/u)^(1/2) P^(7/8)`. Written at `P = p^8` (so `P^(1/2) = p^4`, `P^(3/8) = p^3`, `P^(7/8) = p^7`) and with the two square roots cleared.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseA_total

declarations.doc: **Regime B, case (b) is confined to small `uh`.** `|D_i| < q/(2ℓ)` forces `φ''` within `O(u h P^(-3/4))` of `½ u h P^(-3/4)`, so `|φ''| ≤ Φ₂` confines the case to `u h ≤ 6 k h₁ h₂ P^(1/8)`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_confined

declarations.doc: **Where case (b) closes outright.** Its second term is `1.1 u P^(3/4)`, inside `P^(7/8)` exactly when `u ≤ 0.9 P^(1/8)`. At `P = p^8`: `1.1 u p^6 ≤ p^7` iff `u ≤ 0.9 p`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_closes

declarations.doc: **Case (b) confines the decoration.** Its defining condition `|Ψ' - q/ℓ| < q/(2ℓ)` with `q/ℓ = (27/16) u h ν^(-3/4)` and `Ψ' = (27/32) u h ν^(-3/4) + φ''` pins `0 < φ'' < (27/16) u h ν^(-3/4)`. So in the only case left open, `|φ''|` is at most `27/16` times `u h ν^(-3/4)` -- the wide budget is never attained there.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_confines_phi

declarations.doc: The confinement in the form used: `φ''` is at most `4.83` times the Stage-4 curvature `0.35 u h ν^(-3/4)`, since `(27/16)/0.35 = 4.821…`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_ratio

declarations.doc: **The cell frequencies have bounded gaps.** In case (b), `Ψ' ∈ [27/32, 81/32] u h ν^(-3/4)`, so with `ℓ = (2/3) ν^(1/2)/h` the gaps `α_{i+1} - α_i = Ψ' ℓ` lie in `[0.562, 1.688] u P^(-1/4)`: a strictly increasing sequence of bounded ratio `3`.
declarations.name: wideD3_caseB_gaps

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, the `r = 3` piece.** Where `|f'''|` is good at full scale, `f''` is strictly monotone and any two points of `{|f''| ≤ V}` are within `2V/c`. In the manuscript `c = c₃S/P`, giving the length `2PV/(c₃S)` — the `O(PV/S)` term of Lemma 3.9(i). The mean value theorem is *used* here, not assumed.
declarations.name: sublevel_diam_of_deriv_lower

declarations.doc: **Strong convexity, midpoint form.** If `t ↦ g t - (c/2)t²` is convex then `g` satisfies the midpoint inequality with quadratic defect `(c/8)(y-x)²`. This is exactly what `g'' ≥ c` supplies, and it is the only consequence of the `r = 4` hypothesis that the length bound uses.
declarations.name: midpoint_defect_of_convexOn

declarations.doc: **Lemma 3.9, the `r = 4` piece.** Where `|f''''|` is good at full scale, `f''` is strongly convex (after a sign flip) and the sublevel set has diameter at most `4√(V/c)`. In the manuscript `c = c₄S/P²`, giving `P(V/(c₄S))^(1/2)` — the `(V/S)^(1/2)` term of Lemma 3.9(i), and the term that produces the exponent `89/96`. The hypothesis `hmid` is the `≤ 2 zeros` structure: on the piece, `f''` does not dip below `-V` between the two points.
declarations.name: sublevel_diam_of_strong_convexity

declarations.doc: The two bounds combined, in the shape Lemma 3.9(i) prints: the `r = 3` piece contributes `O(PV/S)` and the `r = 4` piece `O(P(V/S)^(1/2))`, and since `V ≤ S` the second dominates. This is why the manuscript displays only `C(E) P (W/S)^(1/2)`.
declarations.name: sublevel_second_term_dominates

declarations.doc: The `j`-th letter of the backward word at phase `phi`: the barrier rises `j` steps back.
declarations.name: backWord

declarations.doc: Subtracting a sub-unit amount that the fractional part cannot absorb wraps once.
declarations.name: fract_sub_wrap

declarations.doc: And absorbs it otherwise.
declarations.name: fract_sub_stay

declarations.doc: **The letter is an arc anchored at `j * b`.** Written against `(j+1) * b`, the condition `fract (phi - (j+1) * b) >= 1 - b` says exactly that `phi` lies within `b` of `j * b`. This is why the flips sit on the orbit rather than anywhere else.
declarations.name: backWord_iff_fract_lt

declarations.doc: **Constant on the arc.** Between `j * b` and `(j+1) * b` the letter is on.
declarations.name: backWord_of_mem_arc

declarations.doc: **Constant on the gap.** Between `(j+1) * b` and the next orbit point the letter is off.
declarations.name: not_backWord_of_mem_gap

declarations.doc: **The letter depends on the phase only through its position relative to the anchor.**
declarations.name: backWord_congr

declarations.doc: **Shifting the phase shifts the word.** `w_(j+1) (phi + b) = w_j (phi)`, which is the relation the cocycle of `J-phase-shift-is-one-update-and-R-halves` is built from.
declarations.name: backWord_shift

declarations.doc: The barrier at depth `t`: a surviving word needs at least this many odd letters.
declarations.name: barrier

declarations.doc: How much the barrier rises in one step.
declarations.name: barrierRise

declarations.doc: **A non-rising step costs nothing.** If the barrier does not rise at `d`, then any odd-count history that survives to `d` also survives to `d+1`, whatever the next letter is — the count is monotone, so no choice can fall below a barrier that did not move. This is the whole reason the raw jump repeats.
declarations.name: survives_succ_of_no_rise

declarations.doc: Conversely a survivor to `d+1` survives to `d`, so the extension map is onto the survivors of one more letter. Together with `survives_succ_of_no_rise` this is the bijection that makes the count double.
declarations.name: survives_of_survives_succ

declarations.doc: **When the barrier does not rise.** Exactly when the next point has not yet passed the current ceiling. For `b = beta` this is the Sturmian condition that indexes the measured `s_k`; stated this way it needs no fractional parts.
declarations.name: noRise_iff_le_ceil

declarations.doc: **A rising step kills exactly the words sitting on the barrier that draw `E`.** If the barrier rises at `d`, a survivor to `d` fails to reach `d+1` precisely when its count is exactly the barrier and the next letter contributes nothing. Every other survivor extends both ways, as in `survives_succ_of_no_rise`. Counting consequence, one line and not formalised here: writing `N_d` for the survivors of length `d` and `M_d` for those of them on the barrier, each survivor has two extensions and exactly the `M_d` on-barrier ones lose a single extension, so `N_(d+1) = 2 * N_d - barrierRise * M_d` uniformly in both cases, and dividing by `2^(d+1)` gives `P_(d+1) = P_d - barrierRise * Q_d / 2` with `Q_d = M_d / 2^d` the mass on the barrier. Verified as an exact integer identity for `d = 1 .. 39` in the tests.
declarations.name: dies_iff_on_barrier

declarations.doc: **Off the barrier, a rising step costs nothing either.** The complement of `dies_iff_on_barrier`: a survivor strictly above the barrier extends both ways even when the barrier rises, which is why only the on-barrier mass appears in the count.
declarations.name: survives_succ_of_above_barrier

declarations.doc: The two updates on the conditional profile, indexed by whether the barrier rises. `rise = false` shifts mass up; `rise = true` shifts it down and drops what falls below the barrier. Both average the two neighbours, which is the fair coin.
declarations.name: update

declarations.doc: **A non-rising step halves the boundary value.** `m = 0` is reachable only from `m = 0`, so `update false pi 0 = pi 0 / 2` with no other contribution. Since the non-rising update also preserves total mass, no renormalisation intervenes, and a PERTURBATION of the boundary value halves too -- which is why `R`'s jump amplitudes satisfy `a_(k+1) = a_k / 2` exactly at every `k` where the Sturmian word vanishes.
declarations.name: update_false_at_zero

declarations.doc: The difference of two profiles inherits it, which is the statement the jump rule needs: whatever the two words agree on afterwards, a boundary gap halves per non-rising step.
declarations.name: update_false_sub_at_zero

declarations.doc: A rising step does NOT halve it: the boundary picks up the neighbour, so no rule of this kind holds at `s_k = 1`, matching the measured ratios there, which do not settle.
declarations.name: update_true_at_zero

declarations.doc: **A rising step preserves the ratio cone.** Adding the bound at the two sites is the whole proof: the updated value at a site is an average of the two old neighbours.
declarations.name: update_true_ratio

declarations.doc: **A non-rising step preserves it too, away from the barrier.**
declarations.name: update_false_ratio

declarations.doc: **And at the barrier it fails.** A non-rising step sends mass up, so the ratio at `m = 0` is at least one and no cone with `s < 1` survives there. The defect is one site wide.
declarations.name: boundary_ratio_at_least_one

declarations.doc: The odd-count window of a length: `2 ^ (L - 1) ≤ 3 ^ o < 2 ^ L`. A minimal certificate of length `L` must have `o` odd letters for an `o` in this window, and the window holds at most one such `o`.
declarations.name: CertWindow

declarations.doc: **The window holds at most one power of three.** Consecutive powers of two differ by a factor of two and `3 > 2`, so two distinct powers of three cannot both land in `[2 ^ (L - 1), 2 ^ L)`.
declarations.name: certWindow_unique

declarations.doc: The window bounds the odd count by the length: `3 ^ o < 2 ^ L` forces `o ≤ L` because `2 ^ o ≤ 3 ^ o`.
declarations.name: certWindow_le

declarations.doc: The length-`(L-1)` prefix of a minimal certificate does not contract. For `L = 1` this is vacuous and the bound `2 ^ 0 ≤ 3 ^ 0` holds outright.
declarations.name: minimalCert_prefix_not_gap

declarations.doc: **A minimal certificate ends in `E`.** An odd last letter would need `3 * 3 ^ o < 2 ^ L` while the prefix gives `3 ^ o ≥ 2 ^ (L - 1)`, i.e. `3 < 2`.
declarations.name: minimalCert_concat_even

declarations.doc: **The odd count of a minimal certificate is inside the window of its length.**
declarations.name: minimalCert_window

declarations.doc: `O^o E^(L-o)`: all the odd letters first.
declarations.name: blockWord

declarations.doc: **The window is attained.** When some power of three lies in `[2 ^ (L-1), 2 ^ L)`, the word `O^o E^(L-o)` is a minimal certificate: every proper prefix either is all odd (where `3 ^ k > 2 ^ k`) or is `O^o E^j` with `j < L - o`, where the window's lower bound `2 ^ (L-1) ≤ 3 ^ o` is exactly what stops it contracting early.
declarations.name: blockWord_isMinimalCertificate

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1 for every length.** A minimal certificate of length `L ≥ 1` exists exactly when some power of three lies in `[2 ^ (L - 1), 2 ^ L)`. The manuscript's list is the case `L ≤ 5`.
declarations.name: minimalCert_exists_iff

declarations.doc: The contrapositive, which is the form the plateaus use: no power of three in the window means no minimal certificate of that length at all.
declarations.name: no_minimalCert_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: `3, 6, 9, 11, 14` carry no minimal certificate: no power of three lies in their windows. These are exactly the lengths where the certificate density does not move.
declarations.name: window_empty_three

declarations.doc: The first five carrying lengths give the manuscript's list back: `L = 1, 2, 4, 5` have windows, `L = 3` does not.
declarations.name: window_one

declarations.doc: The odd counts the manuscript's five certificates carry are the windows' values: `E` has none, `OE` one, `OOEE` two, and both `OOOEE` and `OOEOE` three.
declarations.name: lemma51_odd_counts_are_the_windows

declarations.doc: A window at `L` holds `3 ^ o` exactly when `3 ^ o` has `L` binary digits.
declarations.name: certWindow_iff_natLog

declarations.doc: **The carrying lengths are A020914.** A minimal certificate of length `L` exists exactly when `L = ⌊o log₂ 3⌋ + 1` for some `o`, written here as `Nat.log 2 (3 ^ o) + 1` so that no real number enters.
declarations.name: minimalCert_exists_iff_natLog

declarations.doc: The first carrying lengths, read off the characterisation rather than listed: `3 ^ 0 … 3 ^ 4` have `1, 2, 4, 5, 7` binary digits, so those are the lengths, and `3, 6` are absent because no power of three has that many digits.
declarations.name: carrying_lengths_head

declarations.doc: The minimal certificates of length `d`.
declarations.name: minimalCertWords

declarations.doc: `M_d`, the number of minimal certificates of length `d`.
declarations.name: minimalCertCount

declarations.doc: A one-letter extension survives exactly when its base survives and it does not contract.
declarations.name: prefixNoncontracting_concat

declarations.doc: A one-letter extension is a *minimal* certificate exactly when its base survives and it does contract.
declarations.name: isMinimalCertificate_concat

declarations.doc: **The extensions of the survivors are exactly the survivors and the new minimal certificates.**
declarations.name: extensions_eq_survivors_union_certs

declarations.doc: **`N_{d+1} + M_{d+1} = 2 N_d`.** Each survivor of length `d` has two extensions, and each extension either survives or contracts for the first time.
declarations.name: neverNegCount_add_minimalCertCount

declarations.doc: **A survivor's odd extension never contracts.** One more odd letter multiplies the odd side by three while the even side only doubles.
declarations.name: not_exponentGap_concat_odd

declarations.doc: The survivors of length `d` whose `E`-extension contracts: those sitting on the barrier at a step where it rises. This is `b_d M_d` of the boundary-mass row.
declarations.name: onBarrierWords

declarations.doc: **The minimal certificates of length `d+1` are exactly the `E`-extensions of the on-barrier survivors of length `d`.**
declarations.name: minimalCertWords_succ

declarations.doc: Hence the counts agree, which is the cardinality step the boundary-mass row leaves unformalised.
declarations.name: minimalCertCount_succ

declarations.doc: **`N_(d+1) = 2 N_d - b_d M_d`, in the shape the boundary-mass row states it.** The recursion doubles exactly when `onBarrierCount d = 0`, and those lengths have a closed form: `M_d = 0` iff `d` lies in OEIS A054414, `1 + floor (n / (1 - log 2 / log 3))`, apart from `d = 1`, where `E` contracts at once; `M_d /= 0` iff `d` lies in A020914, `floor (n * log 2 3) + 1`, the laboratory's own distinguished length. The two partition the positive integers, so the plateaus of `density_flat_of_window_empty` below are a Beatty complement rather than a list. Checked to `d = 200` in `research.juggler_sequence.oeis_neighbourhood`; A054414 is the only one of the four sequences around this recursion that the laboratory had not already named.
declarations.name: neverNegCount_succ_sub_onBarrier

declarations.doc: **The certified count doubles and gains the new minimal certificates.**
declarations.name: certifiedWordCount_succ

declarations.doc: **The density gains exactly the cylinder measure of the new minimal certificates.** `PaperBFiveStepDensity.five_cylinders_card_sum` is this at `d = 4 → 5`, read across the five words at once.
declarations.name: density_succ

declarations.doc: No new minimal certificate means no movement in the density.
declarations.name: density_succ_of_no_new_cert

declarations.doc: An empty odd-count window leaves no minimal certificate of that length.
declarations.name: minimalCertCount_eq_zero_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: **The plateau law.** When no power of three lies in `[2 ^ d, 2 ^ (d+1))`, the certificate density at depth `d + 1` equals the density at depth `d`. With `beta = log 2 / log 3` that is the rotation missing an integer; the proof mentions no real number.
declarations.name: density_flat_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: The plateaus the enumeration found, now as consequences rather than observations: `7/8` at both `d = 5` and `d = 6`, `237/256` at both `d = 8` and `d = 9`. These three are the first plateau lengths after `d = 3`: the full list is OEIS A054414 without its initial `1`, so the next are `14, 17, 19, 22, 25, 28, 30`.
declarations.name: density_flat_five_to_six

declarations.doc: **The telescoping identity.** For `d ≤ K`, `2 ^ (K - d) · N_d = Σ_{j = d+1}^{K} 2 ^ (K - j) · M_j + N_K`. It is `neverNegCount_add_minimalCertCount` summed and nothing else.
declarations.name: neverNegCount_telescope

declarations.doc: The same identity with the certificate tail on the left, which is how Section 6 of the manuscript uses it: the mass of certificates appearing strictly after depth `d` and no later than `K` is exactly what separates the two survivor counts.
declarations.name: minimalCert_tail_eq

declarations.doc: **A free length is a full cylinder extension.** When no power of three lies in the window at `d + 1`, the survivors of length `d + 1` are exactly the survivors of length `d` with either letter appended.
declarations.name: neverNegWords_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: The hypothesis in the form the window theorem supplies it.
declarations.name: minimalCertWords_eq_empty_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: **At a free length every additive functional of the survivor set factorises.** For any `f` into an additive commutative monoid, `∑_{v ∈ S_{d+1}} f v = ∑_{w ∈ S_d} (f (w ++ [E]) + f (w ++ [O]))`. This is the single statement behind the separately recorded plateaus: the summand `1` gives `N_{d+1} = 2 N_d`, a character gives the vanishing Fourier coordinate, a weight gives the amplitude law.
declarations.name: sum_neverNegWords_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: The counting corollary, to show the factorisation really does contain the doubling.
declarations.name: neverNegCount_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: A nonempty word that contracts, with no proper nonempty contracting prefix. This is the exact reading of Paper B Lemma 5.1's "contracting words ... with no proper contracting prefix".
declarations.name: IsMinimalCertificate

declarations.doc: The five words of Lemma 5.1.
declarations.name: certE

declarations.doc: Formal cylinder measures of the five certificates sum to `7/8`.
declarations.name: certificate_measures_sum

declarations.doc: An `E`-rooted word of length ≥ 2 is never minimal: its first letter already contracts.
declarations.name: not_minimal_of_even_head

declarations.doc: An `OE`-rooted word of length ≥ 3 is never minimal.
declarations.name: not_minimal_of_OE_prefix

declarations.doc: Length one: only `E` contracts.
declarations.name: length_one

declarations.doc: Length two: only `OE`.
declarations.name: length_two

declarations.doc: At length three no new certificate appears: `3^2 > 2^3`.
declarations.name: length_three

declarations.doc: Length four: only `OOEE`.
declarations.name: length_four

declarations.doc: Length five: `OOOEE` and `OOEOE`.
declarations.name: length_five

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.1.** The minimal certificates of length at most five are exactly `E`, `OE`, `OOEE`, `OOOEE`, and `OOEOE`.
declarations.name: lemma51

declarations.doc: The five named words are indeed the complete list through length five.
declarations.name: lemma51_complete

declarations.doc: The per-letter power map `p_q`: `3/2` after an odd letter, `1/2` after an even one. These are the only two values a Juggler step contributes.
declarations.name: step

declarations.doc: `iter w = ∏ p_q` over the letters of `w`. For a prefix of length `t` this is the iterate exponent `e_t`, so that `J^t(n)` sits at scale `n^(e_t)`.
declarations.name: iter

declarations.doc: Every step exponent is positive.
declarations.name: step_pos

declarations.doc: Every iterate exponent is positive. This is the only fact about the values `3/2` and `1/2` that the criterion below uses.
declarations.name: iter_pos

declarations.doc: **Splitting.** `e` over a concatenation is the product of the two pieces. This is the composition of power maps, and everything below is a consequence.
declarations.name: iter_split

declarations.doc: **The chain rule.** `E = e_{t-1} / e_s`: the product of the step exponents strictly between letters `s` and `t` is the ratio of the iterate exponents at `t-1` and at `s`. `pre` is the prefix of length `s`, so `iter pre = e_s`; `mid` is the block of letters `s+1 … t-1`, so `iter mid = E` and `iter (pre ++ mid) = e_{t-1}`.
declarations.name: chain_rule

declarations.doc: The coefficient of `θ_s` in letter `t`'s phase, in units of `k`: it is `E / 2`, with `E` the composed map of `chain_rule`.
declarations.name: coeff

declarations.doc: The exponent that coefficient sits at: `e_{t-1} - e_s`.
declarations.name: coeffExponent

declarations.doc: **The second-order identity.** The squared-defect term sits at `e_{t-1} - 2 e_s`, and that equals `e_s (E - 2)`.
declarations.name: second_order

declarations.doc: **The `E < 2` criterion.** The second-order exponent is negative exactly when `E < 2`. The equivalence is one-line given `second_order` and `iter_pos`, and that is the point: `2` is where the squared term stops growing, forced by the squaring and by nothing about which words survive.
declarations.name: linearise_iff

declarations.doc: The companion direction, stated positively: a defect whose composed map reaches `2` has a second-order term that does not decay.
declarations.name: no_linearise_iff

declarations.doc: The number of odd letters in a word: `o_t`.
declarations.name: oddCount

declarations.doc: **The exponent walk, exactly.** `e_t = 3^(o_t) / 2^t`. Taking `log₂` gives `u_t = o_t log₂ 3 - t`, the walk the Paper C work is built on; this is that statement before any logarithm, so it is exact.
declarations.name: iter_eq_pow

declarations.doc: **The criterion in the counts.** `E < 2` is the exact integer inequality `3^a < 2^(a+b+1)`, with `a` the odd letters of the block and `a + b` its length. No real logarithm and no floating point anywhere.
declarations.name: lt_two_iff_counts

declarations.doc: **Order independence.** The criterion does not see the order of the block, only how many of each letter it holds. Immediate from `iter_eq_pow`, and not obvious from the product form.
declarations.name: iter_eq_of_counts

declarations.doc: The same statement for the criterion itself.
declarations.name: lt_two_congr

declarations.doc: `3 ^ a = 2 ^ n` only for `a = n = 0`.
declarations.name: three_pow_eq_two_pow

declarations.doc: The walk is never back at its starting level after a letter: `e_t = 1` only for the empty word.
declarations.name: iter_eq_one_iff

declarations.doc: Hence on a non-empty word the two readings of non-contraction agree.
declarations.name: one_le_iff_one_lt

declarations.doc: A prefix that has not contracted by step two is `OO`, and then `e_2 = 9/4`, which already exceeds the branch-run threshold `2`.
declarations.name: noncontracting_two_forces

declarations.doc: The threshold itself: `9/4` is above the `2` at which branch runs stop existing, so the second letter of a non-contracting word already sits above it. `3 > 2 ^ (3/2)` is the same fact in the walk's coordinates.
declarations.name: two_lt_nine_quarters

declarations.doc: Theorem 5.3's kernel monomial `(3k/4) n^(9/8)`: coefficient `3/4` in units of `k`, at exponent `9/8`.
declarations.name: printed_thm53

declarations.doc: A worked instance of the criterion: two odd letters give `E = 9/4 ≥ 2`, so the defect two letters back may not be linearised — this is the `9/4` shape the screen's other threshold also names, here as a statement about `E` alone.
declarations.name: two_odd_not_safe

declarations.doc: One odd and one even give `E = 3/4 < 2`, which is safe.
declarations.name: odd_even_safe

declarations.doc: Relative entropy `D(p ‖ q) = p log(p/q) + (1-p) log((1-p)/(1-q))`. Same formula as `OneSided.klDiv`; defined here so this module does not import the fate layer.
declarations.name: klDiv

declarations.doc: The strict form of `1 - x⁻¹ ≤ log x`.
declarations.name: one_sub_inv_lt_log

declarations.doc: Strict Gibbs: the relative entropy is strictly positive off the diagonal.
declarations.name: klDiv_pos

declarations.doc: `D(q ‖ 1/2) = log 2 + q log q + (1-q) log(1-q)`: the binary relative entropy, expanded.
declarations.name: klDiv_half_eq

declarations.doc: The Chernoff factor of Theorem 6.1, as the manuscript writes it.
declarations.name: theta

declarations.doc: The printed form is `exp(-D(q ‖ 1/2))`.
declarations.name: theta_eq_exp_neg_klDiv

declarations.doc: The estimate: the Chernoff factor is strictly below one away from the fair point.
declarations.name: theta_lt_one

declarations.doc: The form Theorem 6.1 uses: the bound is strictly below `1/2` at every depth.
declarations.name: theta_pow_lt

declarations.doc: Finite additivity of density: finitely many classes of density `r` have density `card * r`.
declarations.name: density_of_finite_union

declarations.doc: The `d -> infinity` step: eventually below every member of a null sequence means null.
declarations.name: tendsto_zero_of_eventually_le

declarations.doc: Theorem 6.1's shape: a density dominated at every depth by a vanishing bound is zero.
declarations.name: exceptional_density_zero

declarations.doc: The length-`d` words carrying a descent certificate: those with a contracting prefix. The complement of `RateFreeDensity.neverNegWords d` inside `allWords d`.
declarations.name: certifiedWords

declarations.doc: `#C_d` as a count of words.
declarations.name: certifiedWordCount

declarations.doc: Certified and never-negative words partition `allWords d`.
declarations.name: certifiedWords_compl

declarations.doc: `allWords d` has `2 ^ d` elements, in `ℕ`. `FateEnergyAtoms.card_allWords` states this over `ℝ`, but that module sits in the fate layer; Paper B should not import it for a counting fact.
declarations.name: card_allWords_nat

declarations.doc: `#C_d + N_d = 2^d`: every word is certified or never-negative, never both.
declarations.name: certifiedWordCount_add_neverNegCount

declarations.doc: **Theorem 5.2's density, as a count.**
declarations.name: four_step_density

declarations.doc: **Theorem 5.4's density, as a count.** This is what `PaperBCertificates.certificate_measures_sum` and `DepthFourFive.cor64_density` assert as an identity between five rational literals: here the `7/8` is the number of certified words over the number of words.
declarations.name: five_step_density

declarations.doc: **Depth six adds nothing.** The density is still `7/8`, so Section 5 stopping at five costs no certificate.
declarations.name: six_step_density

declarations.doc: The length-`d` words extending `c`: the cylinder of `c` cut to depth `d`. A set of **words**, unlike `FateChernoff.cylinder`, which is the set of odd starts in `(y, 2y]` realizing a given word.
declarations.name: wordCylinder

declarations.doc: **The five cylinders cover the certified words at depth five.**
declarations.name: five_cylinders_cover

declarations.doc: **And they are disjoint**, because their sizes add to the size of the union. `16 + 8 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 28`, which is the main-term arithmetic Theorem 5.4 prints as `1/2 + 1/4 + 1/16 + 1/32 + 1/32`.
declarations.name: five_cylinders_card_sum

declarations.doc: The printed measures are the cylinder counts.
declarations.name: printed_measures_are_counts

declarations.doc: Starts in `{1,…,N}` carrying a descent certificate by depth `d`.
declarations.name: certifiedCount

declarations.doc: A start's depth-`d` itinerary extends `c` exactly when its depth-`|c|` itinerary is `c`.
declarations.name: prefix_itinerary_iff

declarations.doc: **Summing depth-`d` class counts over a cylinder gives the prefix class count.** This is the step that lets Theorem 5.4's five summands be the quantities Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 4.6, 4.10 and 4.12 estimate.
declarations.name: sum_classCount_cylinder

declarations.doc: **Theorem 5.4's assembly over real starts.** The certified count at depth five is the sum of the five printed prefix-class counts. Combined with Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 4.6, 4.10 and 4.12 -- none of them proved anywhere in this repository -- this is the equality the paper's `7N/8 + O_ε(N^(127/128+ε))` rests on.
declarations.name: certifiedCount_five_eq

declarations.doc: **Depth six contributes nothing.**
declarations.name: no_minimal_certificate_six

declarations.doc: **Depth seven contributes exactly three.**
declarations.name: minimal_certificates_seven

declarations.doc: The next rung of the table: `115/128`, not `7/8`.
declarations.name: seven_step_density

declarations.doc: The gain over Theorem 5.4 is exactly the three new cylinders.
declarations.name: seven_step_gain

declarations.doc: The printed error exponents of Theorems 3.1, 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4, in increasing order. This is what licenses "absorbing the smaller four-step error".
declarations.name: error_exponents_ordered

declarations.doc: **Absorption.** At `N ≥ 1` the smaller exponent is dominated.
declarations.name: error_absorb

declarations.doc: **The count assembly, with the analysis as hypotheses.** Five class counts, each within its own error of its printed main term, add to `7N/8` within the sum of the errors. Every hypothesis here is an analytic estimate this repository does not prove.
declarations.name: five_step_error_assembly

declarations.doc: Survivors graded by their surplus `h` above the barrier. Counts, so `Nat`.
declarations.name: Profile

declarations.doc: One step against a barrier letter that does **not** rise, so a walker at height `h` arrives from `h` by staying or from `h - 1` by climbing, and nobody is killed.
declarations.name: stepFlat

declarations.doc: One step against a barrier letter that **rises** by one, so a walker at height `h` arrives from `h + 1` by staying or from `h` by climbing. The walkers at height `0` that do not climb fall through the barrier and are lost.
declarations.name: stepRise

declarations.doc: The survivors sitting exactly **on** the barrier, as a profile: a point mass at `0`.
declarations.name: barrierMass

declarations.doc: **The exchange cost.** Climbing before killing and killing before climbing agree at every height above the barrier, and differ at the barrier by exactly the mass standing on it. Everything is `Nat`; the two orders are genuinely comparable, one dominating the other.
declarations.name: stepRise_stepFlat_eq_add_barrierMass

declarations.doc: Killing before climbing never counts more than climbing before killing.
declarations.name: stepFlat_stepRise_le

declarations.doc: A barrier word, read in the order its letters are applied; `true` is a rise.
declarations.name: run

declarations.doc: Every letter acts linearly, so a whole history does.
declarations.name: run_add

declarations.doc: **What a discontinuity costs.** Transposing one adjacent rise-then-flat pair of barrier letters changes the whole later history by exactly the history of a single point mass on the barrier at the moment of the swap.
declarations.name: run_stepRise_stepFlat

declarations.doc: The transposed history is never the larger one.
declarations.name: run_stepFlat_stepRise_le

declarations.doc: A point mass on the barrier is unmoved by a rising letter: the walker must climb, and climbing from the barrier lands back on the barrier. This is why the history opened by a transposition is the survivor problem itself, started from one walker, rather than some other problem.
declarations.name: stepRise_barrierMass

declarations.doc: Totals over a height window, the quantity the counts are read through.
declarations.name: total

declarations.doc: The exchange cost at the level of totals.
declarations.name: total_run_stepRise_stepFlat

declarations.doc: A flat letter counts each window once and the window below it once more: nothing is killed, and the only asymmetry is that the top height has nowhere to have come from.
declarations.name: total_stepFlat

declarations.doc: A rising letter loses exactly the barrier mass `v 0`, and nothing else.
declarations.name: total_stepRise

declarations.doc: **A Sturmian zero kills nothing.** Below a window the profile has not reached, a flat letter exactly doubles the total. This is the whole content of the observed law that jump amplitudes are multiplied by a clean factor across such a step. Not a duplicate of `sum_neverNegWords_succ_of_window_empty` in `PaperBCertificateRecursion`, though the two were mistaken for one another on 2026-09-19 and neither file said otherwise. They are incomparable, and meet at exactly one point. That one prints `∑_{v ∈ S_{d+1}} f v = ∑_{w ∈ S_d} (f (w ++ [E]) + f (w ++ [O]))` for every additive commutative monoid and every `f`: general in the FUNCTIONAL, specific to the survivor word set, and hypothesised on the certificate window being empty. This one is the counting functional alone, but on an abstract graded `Profile` with no word set in sight, and its hypothesis `v H = 0` is a truncation width — it says the window `total (H+1)` is wide enough to hold the shifted mass, not that the step is free. Freeness is not a hypothesis here at all; it is carried by which operator is applied, `stepFlat` rather than `stepRise`. So neither implies the other. The word-set theorem cannot reach an abstract profile, and one functional cannot reach all of them. They coincide when that one is taken at `f ≡ 1` and this one at the survivor height profile, where both read `N_{d+1} = 2 N_d`. The transposition results below need the abstract carrier, because a transposition rearranges the barrier word and there is no single `d` whose word set to sum over.
declarations.name: total_stepFlat_eq_two_mul

declarations.doc: Against a rising letter the total doubles less the barrier mass, exactly.
declarations.name: total_stepRise_add_barrierMass

declarations.doc: **The walk has fallen past the barrier**, where the level `Λ` enters as `c = 2 ^ Λ`. At `c = 1` this is `exponentGap`.
declarations.name: exponentGapAt

declarations.doc: **A minimal certificate at level `c`**: the walk passes the barrier at the last step and at no earlier one.
declarations.name: IsMinimalCertificateAt

declarations.doc: **The shifted window.** At level `c` the odd count of a length-`L` minimal certificate is pinned to an `o` with `2 ^ (L - 1) ≤ 3 ^ o c < 2 ^ L`.
declarations.name: CertWindowAt

declarations.doc: **A whole-number level is only a shift of the length.** At `c = 2`, that is `Λ = 1`, the window at length `L` is Paper B's window at length `L - 1`. This is worth stating because it says where the new content is and where it is not. It is proved here at `c = 2` only; the same re-indexing holds at `c = 2 ^ k` by the same argument. So a whole-number level proves nothing Paper B did not already have, and the content of this file is at the *fractional* levels -- which is also the only place its strict barrier agrees with Paper C's non-strict one. `certWindowAt_twelve_empty_at_paperC_level` is the worked instance at such a level.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_two_iff

declarations.doc: **At most one power of three lands in the shifted window**, for the same reason as at level zero: consecutive powers of two differ by `2` and `3 > 2`, and scaling both sides by `c` does not change that.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_unique

declarations.doc: **The last letter is `E` at every level.** The proof is Paper B's with the barrier moved: an odd last letter forces `3 < 2`.
declarations.name: minimalCertAt_concat_even

declarations.doc: **The odd count of a level-`c` minimal certificate lies in the shifted window.**
declarations.name: minimalCertAt_window

declarations.doc: **The empty-window theorem, at every level.** When no power of three lies in the shifted window at `L`, no word of length `L` is a minimal certificate at level `c`. At `c = 1` this is `no_minimalCert_of_window_empty`, now derived rather than asserted (`no_minimalCert_of_window_empty_of_level`). For `c > 1` it is the word-level input to the level-`Λ` cylinder identity, and it is the statement Paper C's bad sets satisfy **at every non-integer level**; at integer levels the two conventions part, as the module docstring records.
declarations.name: no_minimalCertAt_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: The contrapositive: a length that carries a level-`c` certificate has a power of three in its shifted window.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_of_minimalCertAt

declarations.doc: The certificate predicates agree at level zero, not merely the gap predicates.
declarations.name: isMinimalCertificateAt_one_iff

declarations.doc: **Paper B's empty-window theorem, obtained from the level-carrying one at `c = 1`.** The module docstring claims Paper B's statements are the `c = 1` case of these; this is that claim discharged rather than asserted.
declarations.name: no_minimalCert_of_window_empty_of_level

declarations.doc: The odd count of a window is bounded by the length, at any level at or below the start.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_le

declarations.doc: **Length twelve is free at Paper C's level.** For every scale `c` between `2.37` and `2.38` -- that is, every level `Λ` between `log₂ 2.37 = 1.2450` and `log₂ 2.38 = 1.2511`, a range containing the `1.2486` the spectrum work runs at -- no power of three lies in the window at `L = 12`, so no word of length twelve first passes the barrier there. The two neighbouring powers of three miss from opposite sides: `3 ^ 6 c ≤ 1735` is below `2 ^ 11 = 2048`, and `3 ^ 7 c ≥ 5183` is above `2 ^ 12 = 4096`. The bracket is about the window, not about the convention. It contains the lattice point `c = 64/27 = 2.3704`, where `3 ^ 3 c = 2 ^ 6` and the two barriers part. That costs this theorem nothing, since it is stated in the strict convention throughout, but the bracket should not be read as a range on which the conventions agree.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_twelve_empty_at_paperC_level

declarations.doc: The consequence, at that level: no word of length twelve is a minimal certificate.
declarations.name: no_minimalCertAt_twelve_at_paperC_level

declarations.doc: The word has not passed the barrier at any prefix: alive at level `c`.
declarations.name: prefixNoncontractingAt

declarations.doc: The empty word never passes a barrier at or below the start. This is the one place the structural argument needs `1 ≤ c`, and it is why the level-`c` recursion has the hypothesis.
declarations.name: not_exponentGapAt_nil

declarations.doc: A one-letter extension is alive exactly when its base is alive and it does not pass.
declarations.name: prefixNoncontractingAt_concat

declarations.doc: A one-letter extension first passes exactly when its base is alive and it does pass.
declarations.name: isMinimalCertificateAt_concat

declarations.doc: The words of length `d` still alive at level `c`.
declarations.name: aliveWordsAt

declarations.doc: The words of length `d` that first pass the barrier at level `c` exactly at their end.
declarations.name: minimalCertWordsAt

declarations.doc: **The extensions of the alive words are the alive words and the new first-passages.**
declarations.name: extensionsAt_eq_alive_union_certs

declarations.doc: An empty shifted window empties the first-passage set at that length.
declarations.name: minimalCertWordsAt_eq_empty_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: **A free length is a full cylinder extension, at level `c`.**
declarations.name: aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: **At a free length every additive functional of the alive set factorises, at level `c`.** This is the statement the frozen-statistic observations rest on: the summand `1` gives the doubling of the counts, a character gives the vanishing Fourier coordinate, and the weight `a ^ oddCount` gives the tilted count multiplying by `1 + a`.
declarations.name: sum_aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: **The shifted window is attained.** When a power of three lies in the shifted window, `O^o E^(L-o)` first passes the barrier at level `c` exactly at its end. The two prefix branches are Paper B's, and each keeps working for its own reason: an all-odd prefix has `3 ^ k c ≥ 3 ^ k ≥ 2 ^ k`, which is where `1 ≤ c` is used, and a prefix `O^o E^j` with `j < L - o` is blocked by the window's lower bound, which already carries the `c`.
declarations.name: blockWordAt_isMinimalCertificateAt

declarations.doc: **The level-`c` empty-window theorem, as a biconditional.** A word of length `L ≥ 1` first passes the barrier at level `c` exactly when a power of three lies in the shifted window. This is Paper B's `minimalCert_exists_iff` at every level.
declarations.name: minimalCertAt_exists_iff

declarations.doc: Alive and first-passing are exclusive: a first passage passes at its own length.
declarations.name: aliveAt_disjoint_certsAt

declarations.doc: **A length is free exactly when it is a full cylinder extension**, at every level. The forward direction is Section 8; the converse is the realisation half, and together they make a frozen statistic an exact diagnostic rather than a one-way hint.
declarations.name: aliveWordsAt_succ_iff_window_empty

declarations.doc: The counting corollary: a free length doubles the alive count at every level.
declarations.name: card_aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty

declarations.doc: `3 ^ o` is `2` to the power `o log₂ 3`.
declarations.name: three_pow_eq_rpow

declarations.doc: `3 ^ o · 2 ^ Λ` is `2` to the power `o log₂ 3 + Λ`.
declarations.name: three_pow_mul_rpow

declarations.doc: **The shifted window is an inhomogeneous Beatty condition.** At level `Λ ≥ 0` the length `L ≥ 1` carries the odd count `o` exactly when `⌊o log₂ 3 + Λ⌋ = L - 1`. At `Λ = 0` this is `certWindow_iff_natLog`, since `Nat.log 2 (3 ^ o) = ⌊o log₂ 3⌋`.
declarations.name: certWindowAt_iff_floor

declarations.doc: Paper C's convention: the barrier is reached, not passed.
declarations.name: exponentGapAtLE

declarations.doc: Off the lattice, the two conventions are the same predicate.
declarations.name: exponentGapAt_iff_le_of_offLattice

declarations.doc: On the lattice they are not: the block word of the witnessing pair separates them.
declarations.name: exists_disagreement_of_onLattice

declarations.doc: **The two conventions agree on every word exactly off the lattice.**
declarations.name: exponentGapAt_agrees_iff

declarations.doc: **Every whole-number level is on the lattice**, at `o = 0`. This is the half the earlier prose had right, and it is the only half it had right.
declarations.name: integer_level_onLattice

declarations.doc: One step of the Beatty boundary moves the floor by `1` or `2`.
declarations.name: floor_step_bounds

declarations.doc: **No two adjacent lengths are both free.** Above the bottom edge `⌊Λ⌋ + 1`, at least one of `L` and `L + 1` carries a window. The proof takes the least `o` whose boundary value reaches `L - 1`. If it is `0` the bottom-edge hypothesis pins it at `L - 1` exactly; otherwise its predecessor fell short, and one step moves the floor by at most `2`, so the value lands on `L - 1` or `L`.
declarations.name: carrying_in_adjacent_pair

declarations.doc: The same fact read on the cylinder identity: it never applies at two consecutive lengths, so the alive count never doubles twice running.
declarations.name: not_cylinder_twice

declarations.doc: The binomial generating function.
declarations.name: sum_choose_mul_pow

declarations.doc: The exponential Markov step on the word count.
declarations.name: chernoff_tail

declarations.doc: The density form: the same bound divided by `2^n`.
declarations.name: chernoff_density

declarations.doc: At the optimal tilt the bound is exactly `theta q ^ n`: the manuscript's optimisation, as an identity.
declarations.name: tilt_gives_theta

declarations.doc: **The rate and the relative entropy are one function.** Paper B minimises a moment generating function and calls the answer `rho`; Paper C writes a relative entropy to the fair coin. The two are negatives of each other identically -- no positivity hypothesis is needed, because both sides are the same arrangement of `b log b`, `(1-b) log (1-b)` and `log 2`.
declarations.name: neg_logRho_eq_klHalf

declarations.doc: **The odds ratio at `beta`.** `beta / (1 - beta) = log 2 / log (3/2)`: the identity that puts both tilts in closed form, and the reason `log (3/2)` appears where one expects `log 3 - log 2`.
declarations.name: beta_odds

declarations.doc: **Paper C's tilt, in closed form.**
declarations.name: lamStar_beta_closed

declarations.doc: Paper B's tilt parameter: Paper C's, read in the walk-value coordinate.
declarations.name: thetaStar

declarations.doc: **The two tilt parameters differ by exactly `log 3`.**
declarations.name: thetaStar_mul_log_three

declarations.doc: **And why they must.** On words of length `t` with `o` odd letters the walk value is `o log 3 - t log 2`, so tilting by it with parameter `theta` is tilting by the odd count alone with parameter `theta * log 3`, times a factor that depends only on `t`. The measures agree; the parameters are the same number in two coordinate systems.
declarations.name: tilt_coordinate_change

declarations.doc: Paper C's odd-fraction threshold at level `C`: the bad-word condition at depth `d = C L` is `u_d > -L`, which forces the odd fraction above this.
declarations.name: pC

declarations.doc: **Paper B is the level-zero member.** `L = 0` is `C` to infinity, and there Paper C's threshold is Paper B's.
declarations.name: pC_tendsto_beta

declarations.doc: Paper C's exponent per unit of `C`, in bits.
declarations.name: eOverC

declarations.doc: **And so do the exponents.** `e(C)/C` converges to Paper B's rate in bits.
declarations.name: eOverC_tendsto

declarations.doc: `log (rho b)` written out: `-b log b + (b-1) log (1-b) - log 2`.
declarations.name: logRho

declarations.doc: **The closed form, in logs.**
declarations.name: log_rho_eq

declarations.doc: The Chernoff exponent as a function of the tilt `lam` and the barrier slope `b`.
declarations.name: chernoffExp

declarations.doc: **The rate is the exponent at the tilt**, at every slope.
declarations.name: chernoffExp_at_lamStar

declarations.doc: **The tilt is a stationary point of the exponent**: the `lam`-derivative vanishes there. This is the double root, in the tilt variable.
declarations.name: chernoffExp_lam_deriv

declarations.doc: **The slope derivative of the rate is the tilt.** `d/db log (rho b) = -lamStar b`.
declarations.name: logRho_deriv

declarations.doc: The ceiling gap is nonnegative: the barrier is never below its line.

This is the formal content of "the proved upper bound `θ(β)^d` is sharp up to the polynomial `d^(3/2)`": the model IS `θ(β)^d · d^(-3/2)`, and bound and truth differ from it by the bounded prefactor alone.

Under the meander shape the truth is Theta of the model, so the proved bound overshoots by exactly `d^(3/2)` times a bounded prefactor — packaged here next to the bound itself, one symbol for the ledger.

declarations.doc: **The tilt exponentiates to the odds ratio.**

declarations.doc: **The tilt is exactly the mean-zero one.** Tilting a fair coin by `exp (lamStar * X)` gives `Bernoulli b`, so the walk `o_t - t*b` has mean zero under the tilted law. This is the statement that `b` is the threshold rather than a convenient nearby value.
declarations.name: lamStar_mean_zero

declarations.doc: The minimised moment generating function, in closed form.
declarations.name: rho

declarations.doc: **`rho` is the tilted normaliser.** `exp (-lamStar * b) / (2 * (1 - b))` is what the change of measure produces; this says it equals the closed form, which is `theta b`.
declarations.name: rho_closed_form

declarations.name: gap

declarations.doc: **The gap is `1 - fract x`** away from the integers, which is where `psi`'s argument comes from: at depth `d` the endpoint cannot be closer to the barrier than this.
declarations.name: ceil_sub_eq_one_sub_fract

declarations.doc: **The barrier moves by `0` or `1`.** So the killed walk does not run against a straight line but against the Sturmian word of `b`, which is what makes the remaining local limit theorem a different problem from the classical one.
declarations.name: sturmian_step

declarations.doc: `beta = log 2 / log 3`, the threshold of the whole construction.
declarations.name: beta

declarations.doc: **At `beta` the tilt is mean zero**, which is the sentence "the walk stays nonnegative exactly when at least a `beta` fraction of the letters are odd".
declarations.name: beta_mean_zero

declarations.doc: **The rate is the closed form at `beta`.** Recorded as a numerical agreement to `1.1e-16` in `J-theorem-six-one-threshold-is-slack`; it is an algebraic identity.
declarations.name: beta_rho_closed

declarations.doc: The tail ratio of the quasi-stationary profile: `(1 - b) / b`.
declarations.name: tailRoot

declarations.doc: **The tail ratio is the tilt.** `tailRoot b * exp (lamStar b) = 1`, so the rate at which the conditional profile decays away from the barrier is the reciprocal of the tilt that makes the walk mean zero. Stated multiplicatively to stay inside field algebra.
declarations.name: tailRoot_mul_odds

declarations.doc: At the tail ratio, `1 + 1/r` collapses to `1/(1-b)`. One of the two substitutions that turn the characteristic exponent into `-KL(b ‖ 1/2)`, which is `log rho`.
declarations.name: one_add_inv_tailRoot

declarations.doc: And `1 + r` collapses to `1/b`. The other substitution.
declarations.name: one_add_tailRoot

declarations.doc: **The tail ratio is the stationary point of the characteristic exponent.** The exponent `(1-b) log((1+1/r)/2) + b log((1+r)/2)` has derivative proportional to `b - (1-b)/r`, vanishing exactly at `tailRoot b`. Its value there is `log rho`, by the two substitutions above together with `rho_closed_form`, so the characteristic equation has a DOUBLE root — the critical case, and the structural reason a polynomial factor accompanies `rho^d`.
declarations.name: stationary_iff_eq_tailRoot

declarations.doc: **The rate is symmetric in the slope.** Swapping a slope for its complement exchanges the two entropy terms and fixes their sum.
declarations.name: logRho_symm

declarations.doc: **The gap to the minimum is a relative entropy.** `chernoffExp lam b - logRho b` is `D(b || p)` at the probability the tilt itself names, `p = exp lam / (1 + exp lam)`.

declarations.doc: **Step 5b, the raised-threshold device.** Lemma 3.9 is applied to the global interpolant `Λ` at threshold `W = V + E`, where `E` bounds `|f - Λ|`. Off the sublevel set `{|Λ| ≤ W}` this returns control of `f` itself: `|f| ≥ V`, and `f` carries the sign of `Λ`. This is what makes the former comparison `V ≥ 10 |f - Λ|` unnecessary. The factor `10` was not merely margin: it forced `V` upward exactly where the Lemma 3.9 hypothesis `V ≤ c₇S/2` forced it down, so the two pinned the normalisation `κ` near `1/3`. With this lemma `κ` falls to `1/12`, and both `P₀` and the non-vacuity point `P₁` improve together.
declarations.name: sublevel_raised_threshold

declarations.doc: The device is sound for *any* nonnegative `V`, in particular for the small `V` that the old comparison forbade: the admissible range is `[0, c₇S/2 - E]`, not `[10E, c₇S/2]`.
declarations.name: raised_threshold_admissible

declarations.doc: Row `st6D1-modeindex`. Lemma 5.2(iii) closes its mode accounting with `|w| ≤ |B₀| + R₀ ≤ 2R₀`, which needs the widened `θ`-coefficient under Stage 2's truncation: `5P^(1/4) ≤ R₀ = P^(5/16)`. With `P = t^16` that is `5t⁴ ≤ t⁵`, i.e. `t ≥ 5`, so `P ≥ 5^16 = 1.53·10^11`. Alone among the rows this one is *exact* rather than conservative: `t₀ = 5` is the crossing. Appendix A.6 does not tabulate it, and it is what pins `R₀` from below. At the printed offset bound `|j| ≤ 3` the constant is `7` and the row reads `P ≥ 7^16 = 3.32·10^13`, which would make it the largest `c₇`-free row and cut A.5's lever from `120` to `1.08`.
