declarations.name: row_5b_j0_window

declarations.doc: Row `5b-Npieces`. The common refinement of gap cells, anchor runs and sawtooth windows has at most `3.5 P^(13/24)` pieces. Under `P = t^48`: cells `3t^26 + 2`, anchor runs `22t^15`, windows `5t^16`, against `3.5t^26`. `t ≥ 1.46`, `P ≥ 7.7·10^7`.
declarations.name: row_5b_Npieces

declarations.doc: Row `5b-lam0-range`, upper half. Lemma 5.2b's `λ₀ ∈ [0.62, 3.90]` opened to `[0.56, 4.2]`: the `O(P^(-1/4))` and the `±1` in the `β`-bounds must not push `3.90` past `4.2`. Clearing denominators with `P = t⁴` gives `3.90(t+1)(3t²+1)² ≤ 37.8 t^5`; `t ≥ 17`, `P ≥ 8.4·10^4`.
declarations.name: row_5b_lam0_upper

declarations.doc: Row `5b-lam0-range`, lower half: `0.62(t-1)(3t²-1)² ≥ 5.04 t^5`.
declarations.name: row_5b_lam0_lower

declarations.doc: Row `39-beta`. The `β̃`-substitution error `2.31 P^(-1/2) ≤ ρ₀`; `P = t²`, `t ≥ 4288`, `P ≥ 1.8·10^7`.
declarations.name: row_39_beta

declarations.doc: Row `39-wave`. The wave remainder `(3750/7) P^(-5/6) ≤ ρ₀`; `P = t^6`, `t ≥ 15.9`, `P ≥ 1.6·10^7`. The `3750/7 = 300/0.56` carries both the corrected floor and the `u`-cap `300` that rose with it.
declarations.name: row_39_wave

declarations.doc: Row `5a-competitors`. Every Step 5a competitor ratio is `≤ 1/4` (domination at margin 4). Under `P = t^48` the four ratios are `1.3 t^(-6)`, `13 t^(-27)`, `9 t^(-52)`, `3 t^(-6)`; the last binds. `t ≥ 1.52`, `P ≥ 5.4·10^8`.
declarations.name: row_5a_competitors

declarations.doc: Row `5b-E<=c7S`. The interpolant error alone against the Lemma 3.9 budget: `E ≤ c₇S/2` at `S = 0.56 P^(-5/8)`. Multiplying by `P^(5/8)` and substituting `P = t^48` gives `170.6 + 0.11 t^10 ≤ (7/5800) t^20`. This is the floor of the method as `κ → 0`: `t ≥ 1.84`, `P ≥ 4.1·10^12`.
declarations.name: row_5b_E_only

declarations.doc: Row `5a-W<=c7S`. Step 5a's balance comparison at the larger scale `S ≥ 0.60 P^(-5/8)`: `(1/12)√0.6 t^13 + 0.11 t^10 + 170.6 ≤ (3/2320) t^20`, with `(1/12)√0.6 ≤ 0.06455`. The `0.60` is Step E's own floor and did not move with the erratum; only `E` did. `t ≥ 1.91`, `P ≥ 2.9·10^13`.
declarations.name: row_5a_binding

declarations.doc: **Row `5b-W<=c7S`: this is `P₀`.** Step 5b's balance comparison at the lower end `S = 0.56 P^(-5/8)`, with `V = (1/12)S^(1/2)P^(-11/24)`, `E = 170.6 P^(-25/24) + 0.11 P^(-5/6)` and `c₇ = 1/232`. Multiplying by `P^(5/8)` and substituting `P = t^48` gives `a t^13 + 0.11 t^10 + 170.6 ≤ b t^20` with `a = (1/12)√0.56 ≤ 0.06237` and `b = 0.56/464 = 7/5800`. `t ≥ 1.92`, i.e. `P ≥ 4.0·10^13`; the probe's bisection reports `3.59·10^13`. This row is the maximum over all thirty, hence `P₀`. Both `a` and `b` grew with the corrected anchor, `a` as a square root and `b` linearly, which is why the row closes earlier than it did at `0.35`.
declarations.name: row_5b_binding

declarations.doc: Row `thm63-rem`. The Lemma 6.2 linearization remainder `P^(43/96)` is inside `P^(1 - 1/96) = P^(95/96)`; `P = t^96`. Holds for every `P ≥ 1`.
declarations.name: row_thm63_rem

declarations.doc: **Lemma 5.2b, step (i).** The frozen gap satisfies `G = ⌊δ⌋ + κ` with `κ ∈ {0,1}`, so `|G - δ| = |κ - Int.fract δ| ≤ 1`. This is the bound that produces the `84.375 k(h₁+h₂)P^(-9/8)` of the interpolant error.
declarations.name: gap_error_le_one

declarations.doc: The bound `1` is **attained**: at `δ` an integer and `κ = 1`.
declarations.name: gap_error_one_attained

declarations.doc: **Recentring cannot halve it.** The error `κ - Int.fract δ` ranges over a set of diameter `> 1` — it contains `1` (at `κ = 1`, `δ = 0`) and `-3/4` (at `κ = 0`, `δ = 3/4`) — so no constant shift `θ` of the interpolant brings every value within `1/2`. This is why the paper's `1` is not replaced by `1/2`.
declarations.name: gap_error_not_halved_by_recentring

declarations.doc: Tilted mass of the odd continuations at depth `d`: `Σ_{|w|=d} μ(w ++ [O]) x^{o(w)}`.
declarations.name: oddMass

declarations.doc: The tilted odd share `s_θ(d)` with `x = e^θ`: odd continuations over the whole tilted mass at depth `d` (Lean's `a / 0 = 0` when no mass).
declarations.name: tiltedShare

declarations.doc: Odd continuations carry at most the parents' tilted mass.
declarations.name: oddMass_le_weightGen

declarations.doc: One depth: `Z_{d+1} ≤ Z_d + (x-1)·oddMass_d`.
declarations.name: weightGen_succ_le

declarations.doc: One depth in share form: `Z_{d+1} ≤ Z_d (1 + (x-1) s_d)`.
declarations.name: weightGen_succ_le_share

declarations.doc: The per-depth factor is dominated by `a_q exp(c_q (s - q)^+)`.
declarations.name: one_add_le_exp_excess

declarations.doc: Proposition 9.3: the tilted mass at depth `d` is at most `Z_0 · a_q^d · exp(c_q Σ_{t<d} (s_t - q)^+)`.
declarations.name: weightGen_le_pressure

declarations.doc: Theorem 9.2 with Proposition 9.3: the mass of words with at least `k` odd letters is at most `Z_0 a_q^d exp(c_q Σ (s_t - q)^+) / x^k`.
declarations.name: count_le_pressure

declarations.doc: The no-momentum hypothesis at one scale and depth: the tilted odd share exceeds `q` by at most `δ d` in total over the depths below `d`.
declarations.name: NoMomentum

declarations.doc: Under no momentum the mass of words with at least `k` odd letters is at most `Z_0 · a_q^d · exp(c_q δ d) / x^k`: the Tao-type count with its Chernoff-form exponent, kernel-checked.
declarations.name: count_le_of_noMomentum

declarations.doc: At the re-centring tilt `x = p(1-q)/(q(1-p))` the per-step exponent is the relative entropy: `p log x - log(1 + (x-1) q) = D(p ‖ q)`.
declarations.name: tilt_exponent_eq_kl

declarations.doc: AM–GM in the form used below: a product of `d` positive reals is at most the `d`-th power of their mean (Jensen for `Real.log`).
declarations.name: prod_le_mean_pow

declarations.doc: The product form of the telescoping: `Z_d ≤ Z_0 ∏_{t<d} (1 + (x-1) s_t)`.
declarations.name: weightGen_le_prod

declarations.doc: The mean-share hypothesis: the tilted odd share averages at most `q` over the depths below `d`. No positive part: depths with share below `q` compensate depths with share above it.
declarations.name: MeanShare

declarations.doc: No momentum against `q` with slack `δ` gives mean share at most `q + δ`.
declarations.name: meanShare_of_noMomentum

declarations.doc: Under the mean-share hypothesis the depth-`d` tilted mass is at most `Z_0 a_q^d`, with no exponential slack: AM–GM on the product form.
declarations.name: weightGen_le_of_meanShare

declarations.doc: The Tao-type count under the mean-share hypothesis: `#{o_d ≥ k} ≤ Z_0 a_q^d / x^k`, with no exponential slack.
declarations.name: count_le_of_meanShare

declarations.doc: The tilted odd share is a share: it never exceeds `1`.
declarations.name: tiltedShare_le_one

declarations.doc: AM–GM over an arbitrary finite index set.
declarations.name: prod_le_mean_pow_finset

declarations.doc: The mean-share hypothesis away from an exceptional set of depths `E`. Nothing at all is assumed on `E`.
declarations.name: MeanShareOff

declarations.doc: With no exceptional depths this is `MeanShare`.
declarations.name: meanShareOff_empty

declarations.doc: **Exceptional depths cost a factor `x` each, and nothing more.** Under `MeanShareOff` the depth-`d` tilted mass is at most `Z_0 · x^{|E ∩ [0,d)|} · a_q^{|[0,d) \ E|}`.
declarations.name: weightGen_le_of_meanShareOff

declarations.doc: The Tao-type count with an exceptional set of depths.
declarations.name: count_le_of_meanShareOff

declarations.doc: **Every bounded prefix of depths is free.** Taking the exceptional set to be the first `k` depths, no assumption whatever on those depths costs more than the constant factor `x^k`. This is Paper C section 9.3(a): the depth-five split, and every split to any fixed depth, cannot bear on the reduction.
declarations.name: initial_depths_are_free

declarations.doc: A tower biased below `a_q/x` has geometrically decaying relative weight.
declarations.name: tower_ratio_lt_one

declarations.doc: At `q = 1/2` the tower tolerance is `(1+x)/(2x)`.
declarations.name: tower_tolerance_half

declarations.doc: `j` iterated integer square roots of `x` equal `s` exactly when `s^(2^j) ≤ x < (s+1)^(2^j)`: the intermediate floors are transparent.
declarations.name: sqrt_iter_eq_iff

declarations.doc: On an even run the Juggler map is iterated `Nat.sqrt`.
declarations.name: floorPower_iter_of_even

declarations.doc: An odd step followed by `j` even steps is the integer `2^(j+1)`-th root of `n^3`: the value `⌊n^{3/2^(j+1)}⌋`, one floor, no nesting.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_even_run

declarations.doc: The cell of the value after `O E^j`: `s^(2^(j+1)) ≤ n^3 < (s+1)^(2^(j+1))`.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_even_run_eq_iff

declarations.doc: The `OE` fiber of `FateContagion` is the case `j = 1`.
declarations.name: floorPower_oe_eq_iff

declarations.doc: The two coprime odd factors `y` and `y + 2` cannot have a cubic product.
declarations.name: odd_mul_add_two_ne_cube

declarations.doc: A cube cannot be one below the successor square of an odd natural number.
declarations.name: cube_add_one_ne_odd_succ_sq

declarations.doc: An odd cube strictly below this even square has upper complement at least three.
declarations.name: cube_add_three_le_odd_succ_sq

declarations.doc: The prescribed odd branch has the strengthened upper cell when both endpoints are odd.
declarations.name: odd_image_upper_gap

declarations.doc: Every actual odd-to-odd Juggler edge has upper square complement at least three.
declarations.name: floorPower_odd_image_upper_gap

declarations.doc: Exact rotation rule: the letter at position `k` with `a` odd letters already used is even iff `2^(k+1) ≤ 3^a` (that is, `u ≥ 1`).
declarations.name: hugIsEven

declarations.doc: Number of odd letters among the first `k` letters of the exact hug itinerary.
declarations.name: hugOdds

declarations.doc: Letter of the exact hug itinerary at position `k` (`true` = even).
declarations.name: hugLetter

declarations.doc: The exact hug itinerary of length `L`.
declarations.name: hugWord

declarations.doc: Lower window invariant: the exact rule never lets the walk go negative — `2^k ≤ 3^(hugOdds k)`, that is `u_k ≥ 0`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_ge

declarations.doc: Upper window invariant: the exact rule never overshoots — `3^(hugOdds k) < 3·2^k`, the subtraction-free form of `3^(hugOdds k − 1) < 2^k`, that is `u_k < 1 + α`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_lt

declarations.doc: Minimality: `hugOdds k` is the least odd budget with `2^k ≤ 3^a`. This is the integer form of `o_min(k) = ⌈k log 2 / log 3⌉` and the "forcing exactly `o_min` odds" clause of Paper A Lemma 5.6.
declarations.name: hugOdds_least

declarations.doc: Strict lower window for positive prefix lengths: powers of two and three never meet, so `2^k < 3^(hugOdds k)`. Hence `hugOdds k` is exactly the finance table's `o_min(k) = min {o : 3^o > 2^k}`: it satisfies the strict inequality, and `hugOdds_least` gives minimality among all such budgets.
declarations.name: hugOdds_pow_gt

declarations.doc: Combinatorial core of the hug exchange (Paper A Theorem 5.4): the exact hug itinerary is prefix-minimal among admissible exponent walks. Admissibility of an odd-count profile `a` at prefix `k` is `u_k ≥ 0`, in integer form `2^k ≤ 3^(a k)`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_le_of_admissible

declarations.doc: **Cycle itineraries dominate the hug itinerary** (corollary of `cycleMin_prefix_pow_le` and `hugOdds_least`): on a minimum-based cycle itinerary, every prefix carries at least as many odd letters as the exact hug itinerary of the same length. This is the cycle-native form of the hug adversary — the rotation itinerary is the pointwise cheapest odd-count profile any hypothetical cycle can present.
declarations.name: cycleMin_prefix_odds_ge_hug

declarations.doc: Full-itinerary instance: a minimum-based cycle itinerary of length `L` has at least `hugOdds L` odd letters.
declarations.name: cycleMin_odds_ge_hug

declarations.doc: One step adds at most one odd letter.
declarations.name: hugOdds_succ_le

declarations.doc: The odd count is monotone in the prefix length.
declarations.name: hugOdds_mono

declarations.doc: The odd count grows at most linearly: `hugOdds (j + m) ≤ hugOdds j + m`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_add_le

declarations.doc: Budgeted hug rule at total length `L`, odd budget `o`, position `k`, with `a` odd letters already used: forced even when the odd budget is exhausted, forced odd when the remaining letters must all be odd, otherwise the exact rule.
declarations.name: budgetedIsEven

declarations.doc: Number of odd letters among the first `k` letters of the budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, o)`.
declarations.name: budgetedOdds

declarations.doc: The budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, o)`.
declarations.name: budgetedWord

declarations.doc: At the exact budget `o = hugOdds L`, neither budget clause fires: the budgeted rule at position `k < L` with the exact count agrees with the exact letter.
declarations.name: budgetedIsEven_hug

declarations.doc: At the exact budget, the budgeted and exact odd counts agree at every prefix.
declarations.name: budgetedOdds_eq_hugOdds

declarations.doc: **Itinerary identity** (Paper A Lemma 5.6, discrete side): the budgeted hug itinerary at `(L, hugOdds L)` equals the exact hug `L`-prefix. Together with `hugOdds_pow_ge` and `hugOdds_least` this says the exact rule forces exactly the minimal admissible odd budget, so the budget never binds.
declarations.name: budgetedWord_eq_hugWord

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the record length `L = 84` has exact odd budget `53`, matching the finance table.
declarations.name: hugOdds_84

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the generator `L = 1054` has exact odd budget `665`, matching `three_pow_step_gt_two_pow_step`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_1054

declarations.doc: Sanity instance: the window seed `L = 50508` has exact odd budget `31867`, matching the finance table.
declarations.name: hugOdds_seed

declarations.doc: Lattice bridge: the survivor-lattice base point `(Lstar, Ostar) = (25781, 16266)` of `RunSurvivorLattice.lean` is a hug pair — its odd count is the exact hug count at its length. Together with `hugOdds_1054` (the step generator `(1054, 665)`) and `hugOdds_seed` (the seed `(50508, 31867) = 2·(25781, 16266) − (1054, 665)`), all survivor-lattice generators lie on the hug diagonal `o = hugOdds L`.
declarations.name: hugOdds_lattice_base

declarations.doc: The hug counts along the certified convergent denominators of `θ` (`theta_convergent_denominators` in `OstrowskiSandwich.lean`): these are the finance table's `o_min` values at each block length.
declarations.name: hugOdds_convergent_denoms

declarations.doc: The per-state walk charge at reduced log-base `ν` and weight `W`: `g = 1/(e^{Wν}·W·ν)`. With `W = 2^u` and `ν = log n'` this is the paper's `g(u) = 1/(n'^{2^u}·2^u·log n')`.
declarations.name: stateCharge

declarations.doc: The charge is antitone in the weight: heavier states are cheaper to visit. This is the paper's "`g` is strictly decreasing in `u`" in the (non-strict) form the envelope uses.
declarations.name: stateCharge_antitone

declarations.doc: The weight profile of the exact hug itinerary: `hugWeight k = 3^{hugOdds k} / 2^k`, the pointwise-least admissible walk weight.
declarations.name: hugWeight

declarations.doc: The hug weight is pointwise below every admissible weight profile (real form of `hugOdds_le_of_admissible`).
declarations.name: hugWeight_le_of_admissible

declarations.doc: On a minimum-based cycle, the hug weight is pointwise below the realized walk weight (real form of `cycleMin_prefix_odds_ge_hug`).
declarations.name: hugWeight_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: **Hug charge maximality.** For any admissible odd-count profile `a` (every prefix satisfies `2^k ≤ 3^{a k}`) and any reduced log-base `ν > 0`, the total walk charge is at most the hug charge. This is the analytic half of Paper A Theorem 5.4, strengthened from the fixed-`(L,o)` class to all admissible walks.
declarations.name: hug_charge_maximal

declarations.doc: **The charge is *strictly* antitone in the weight.** `stateCharge_antitone` is the non-strict form the envelope uses; this is the paper's "`g` is strictly decreasing in `u`", which is what a uniqueness statement needs.
declarations.name: stateCharge_strictAnti

declarations.doc: Equal charges force equal weights.
declarations.name: stateCharge_inj

declarations.doc: **Theorem 5.4, the strict half: the hug itinerary is the *only* maximiser.** If an admissible odd-count profile attains the hug charge over a prefix, it *is* the hug profile there. `hug_charge_maximal` gives the inequality; strict antitonicity turns equality of the sums into equality of every term, and `3^·` is injective.
declarations.name: hug_charge_unique

declarations.doc: **Defect sum is bounded by the walk charge at the reduced base.** On a minimum-based cycle with `n ≥ 400` and positive reduced log-base `ν = log n − D`, each cyclic defect `1/(x_k log x_k)` is bounded by the charge of the realized weight: exponentiating the transport inequality gives `x_k ≥ e^{w_k ν}` and `log x_k ≥ w_k ν`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_defect_le_charge

declarations.doc: **Defect sum is bounded by the hug charge at the reduced base** (the §5.2 consequence composed with Theorem 5.4): on a minimum-based cycle with `n ≥ 400` and positive reduced log-base, the cyclic defect sum is at most the hug charge of the same length. This is the full structural half of the walk-charge envelope. The identification of that hug-charge sum with `hugCharge` is `hugCharge_eq_scaled_stateCharge` in `HugChargeEnvelope.lean`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_defect_le_hug_charge

declarations.doc: Parameterized majorant `−log(1−t) ≤ c·t` for `0 ≤ t ≤ 1 − 1/c`: `log(1/(1−t)) ≤ t/(1−t)` and `1/(1−t) ≤ c` on the threshold interval. Instances: `c = 1.05` on `t ≤ 1/21` (transport) and `c = 6/5` on `t ≤ 1/6` (defect finance).
declarations.name: neg_log_one_sub_le_mul

declarations.doc: Even step, lower side: for even `x ≥ 441`, `log T(x) ≥ (1/2)·log x − 1.05/√x`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_even_ge

declarations.doc: Odd step, lower side: for odd `x ≥ 9`, `log T(x) ≥ (3/2)·log x − 1.05/(x·√x)`.
declarations.name: log_floorPower_odd_ge

declarations.doc: The walk weight `w_k = 2^(u_k) = 3^(a_k)/2^k` — rational.
declarations.name: walkWeight

declarations.doc: One more letter adds one to the odd count exactly when that letter is odd.
declarations.name: oddCount_take_succ

declarations.doc: An odd letter multiplies the walk weight by `3/2`.
declarations.name: walkWeight_succ_odd

declarations.doc: An even letter halves the walk weight.
declarations.name: walkWeight_succ_even

declarations.doc: Above-anchor prefixes keep `w_k ≥ 1` (`aboveAnchor_prefix_pow_le` in weight form).
declarations.name: one_le_walkWeight_aboveAnchor

declarations.doc: Cycle minimality forces `u_k ≥ 0`, that is `w_k ≥ 1` (`cycleMin_prefix_pow_le` in weight form).
declarations.name: one_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: The walk weight is never negative.
declarations.name: walkWeight_nonneg

declarations.doc: Accumulated transport deficit along the first `k` letters: `0.7/(n√n)` per odd letter, `1.05/n` per even letter.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit

declarations.doc: One-step recurrence for the running prefix deficit.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_succ

declarations.doc: The prefix deficit is monotone in the prefix length.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_mono

declarations.doc: The transport deficit over the full word: `D = 1.05·e/n + 0.7·o/(n·√n)`.
declarations.name: transportDeficit

declarations.doc: The prefix deficit in closed count form.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_eq

declarations.doc: The full-itinerary prefix deficit is the transport deficit.
declarations.name: prefixDeficit_length

declarations.doc: Upper envelope on any realized prefix (floors only lose): `log x_k ≤ w_k · log n`. Log form of `power_bound_word`; no anchor hypothesis.
declarations.name: follows_log_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: Transport invariant along a descent-free prefix: `w_k·(log n − D_k) ≤ log x_k` with the running prefix deficit. The single transport induction; the cycle form is the closed instance.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_transport_prefix

declarations.doc: **Transport on descent-free prefixes** (log form): on `AboveAnchor n w` with `n ≥ 400`, every state satisfies `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k` with `D = 1.05·e/n + 0.7·o/(n·√n)`.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_transport

declarations.doc: Transport invariant along the cycle: closed instance of `aboveAnchor_transport_prefix`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_transport_prefix

declarations.doc: **Transport to a reduced base** (Paper A Theorem 5.3, log form): on a minimum-based cycle with minimum `n ≥ 400`, every state satisfies `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k` with `D = 1.05·e/n + 0.7·o/(n·√n)`. Exponentiating gives `x_k ≥ (n e^{−D})^{w_k}`. Closed instance of `aboveAnchor_transport`.
declarations.name: cycleMin_transport

declarations.doc: **Flight envelope** (fly-height sandwich): on a descent-free prefix with anchor `n ≥ 400`, `w_k·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k ≤ w_k·log n`. At the prefix peak `H` with `W = max_k w_k` this gives `W·(log n − D) ≤ log H ≤ W·log n`: the fly exponent `log H / log n` equals the peak walk weight up to `O(D·W/log n)`. Not a halt theorem and not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_flight_envelope

declarations.doc: Weight form of a walk-height hypothesis: `2^(k+B) ≤ 3^{a_k}` (the exponent walk is at height `≥ B` doublings at step `k`) gives `2^B ≤ w_k` for the walk weight `w_k = 3^{a_k}/2^k`.
declarations.name: two_pow_le_walkWeight

declarations.doc: **Walk-height law** (divergence rate): on a descent-free prefix with anchor `n ≥ 400`, a walk height of `B` doublings at step `k` (`2^(k+B) ≤ 3^{a_k}`) forces `2^B·(log n − D) ≤ log x_k`; exponentiating, `x_k ≥ (n·e^{−D})^{2^B}` — heights along a descent-free prefix are doubly exponential in the walk height. Composed with the walk-divergence theorem (`J-flight-walk-divergence`; human glue: pigeonhole plus `cycle_strict_envelope`), every descent-free flight realizes this rate along an unbounded walk. Not a halt theorem and not a divergence theorem.
declarations.name: aboveAnchor_height_of_walk

declarations.doc: `q_{n-k}` with value `0` when `k > n`.
declarations.name: qShift

declarations.doc: `E_i(s) = s₁ q_{i-2} + s₂ q_{i-1} + s₃ q_i`.
declarations.name: energy

declarations.doc: Coefficient row `u_i = (q_{i-2}, q_{i-1}, q_i)`.
declarations.name: adjointU

declarations.doc: Left action of `A = [[0, 0, 3], [1, 0, 1], [0, 1, 2]]` on a row vector.
declarations.name: mulRowA

declarations.doc: Constructional identity: `E_{i-1}(T_w s) = E_i(s) - w q_{i-1}`.
declarations.name: energy_step

declarations.doc: MSD word applied from the left: first control is the highest remaining place.
declarations.name: foldSteps

declarations.doc: `∑_t ws[t] * q (start - 1 - t)`. Matches Python `consumed_sum`.
declarations.name: consumedSum

declarations.doc: After an MSD word of length `k` from remaining `n+k`, `E_n(fold s) = E_{n+k}(s) - ∑_j w_j q_{n+k-1-j}`. KNOWN packaging of `energy_step`, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_telescope

declarations.doc: MSD recurrence word `B* = (1,-2,-1,-3)`. `val(B*) = q_{n+3}-2q_{n+2}-q_{n+1}-3q_n = 0`. KNOWN `q_rec`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: recurrenceWord

declarations.doc: The set of integer controls `w` with `E_{n-1}(T_w s)` in a fixed interval `[lo, hi]` is consecutive. This is `energy_step` plus `q > 0`, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_control_interval

declarations.doc: `∑ q`-weights of a zero word vanish.
declarations.name: consumedSum_replicate_zero

declarations.doc: Homogeneous motion `A^k = T_0^k` preserves energy in the sliding index: `E_n(A^k s) = E_{n+k}(s)`. This is `energy_telescope` on the zero word, not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: energy_homogeneous

declarations.doc: Determinant of three row vectors.
declarations.name: tripleDet

declarations.doc: Consecutive adjoints are independent: `det = 3^{n-2}` for `n ≥ 2`. Neighboring energies invert `s` over `ℚ`. Not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: adjointDet_eq

declarations.doc: Homogeneous residual matrix `A`. `step 0 = A`.
declarations.name: applyA

declarations.doc: Affine unfolding: `T_ws(s) = A^{|ws|} s + T_ws(0)`.
declarations.name: foldSteps_affine

declarations.doc: Control particular from the origin: `s = −∑_j A^{k-1-j} e₃ w_j`. KNOWN variation of constants, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: particularSum

declarations.doc: From the origin, an MSD word unfolds by variation of constants: `foldSteps ws origin = particularSum ws`.
declarations.name: origin_particular

declarations.doc: From the origin, `(c_B)₃ = -val(B)`. KNOWN energy at `n=0`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: particular_s3

declarations.doc: From any start state, `(T_B(s))₃ = E_{|B|}(s) - val(B)`. KNOWN `energy_telescope` at remaining 0, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: fold_s3

declarations.doc: Length-`n` suffix acceptance is classified by the energy, not by residual coordinates: `foldSteps ws s` lands on `F` exactly when `energy |ws| s` equals the consumed sum of `ws`.
declarations.name: fold_on_F_iff

declarations.doc: Length-`|ws|` landing on `F` is classified by `E_{|ws|}`, not by `s`. KNOWN `fold_on_F_iff`, not a Myhill–Nerode calculus and not `L₀`.
declarations.name: same_energy_same_OnF

declarations.doc: Concatenation of particulars: `c_{UV} = A^{|V|} c_U + c_V`.
declarations.name: particular_concat

declarations.doc: Origin reset prefixes do not change the particular of a suffix. KNOWN `particular_concat` at `c_R=0`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: reset_prefix

declarations.doc: Two-start MSD split. Not `val(U) + C val(V)`. KNOWN, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: consumedSum_append

declarations.doc: `val(UV) = val(V) - E_{|V|}(c_U)`. KNOWN packaging, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: val_concat_energy

declarations.doc: Hub `(1,-2) ↦ (-3,-1,0)`. Regression, not infinitude.
declarations.name: hub_nonreset

declarations.doc: `B*` is a reset. KNOWN four-step evaluation, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: recurrence_word_reset

declarations.doc: `(B*)^k` stays at the origin. KNOWN packaging of the reset, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: reset_pow_origin

declarations.doc: `(B*)^k · (1,-2)` has particular the hub. Not a bound on `L₀`.
declarations.name: reset_pow_then_hub

declarations.doc: Complete-word zero-value is not a monoid. Witness `(1,-2)(1,-2)`.
declarations.name: complete_zero_not_monoid

declarations.doc: Impulse `A^r e₃` as a place-value triple. Underflow of `q` is 0.
declarations.name: impulsePlace

declarations.doc: `A^r e₃ = (3 q_{r-1}, 3 q_{r-2}+q_{r-1}, q_r)`. KNOWN place-value dictionary for `origin_particular`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: iterateA_e3

declarations.doc: `q_{-1} = 0`, and `qPrev (k+1) = q k`. Avoids wrapping `Nat` at `n = 1`.
declarations.name: qPrev

declarations.doc: `t_n = (q_{n-1}, -q_{n-2}, 0)` for `n ≥ 1`. Matches Python `kernel_family_state`.
declarations.name: kernelTarget

declarations.doc: Energy on `F`: `E_n(a,b,0) = a q_{n-2} + b q_{n-1}`.
declarations.name: energyOnF

declarations.doc: Integer reverse of `T_w`, using Euclidean `ediv`.
declarations.name: explicitPredecessor

declarations.doc: If `step w s = t` then `s` is the integer reverse `explicitPredecessor t w`: the step map is invertible over the integers. Inversion of `step`, not a bound on `L_0`.
declarations.name: unique_predecessor

declarations.doc: On `F`, the unique integer predecessor is `(b - a/3, w - 2(a/3), a/3)`. KNOWN inversion of `step`, not `L₀`.
declarations.name: predecessor_on_F

declarations.doc: Shared first coordinate of every integer preimage of `t_n`.
declarations.name: kernelPredFst

declarations.doc: Every origin-reachable state has first coordinate divisible by `3`.
declarations.name: origin_reachable_fst_dvd_three

declarations.doc: Every origin-reachable state other than the origin has an origin-reachable predecessor: some `s` and letter `w` with `step w s = t`.
declarations.name: origin_reachable_pred

declarations.doc: Enumeration of `ℤ/24ℤ`: residues with `n ≡ 0 or 4 (mod 8)` except `0, 12`.
declarations.name: four_residues

declarations.doc: Off `{0, 12} (mod 24)`, either `t_n` itself or every predecessor fails `3 ∣ s₁`.
declarations.name: not_exceptional_blocks

declarations.doc: For `n > 0` outside the residues `0` and `12` modulo `24`, the kernel family target `kernelTarget n` is not origin-reachable under unrestricted integer steps.
declarations.name: kernel_unreachable_of_not_exceptional

declarations.doc: Place-value sequence.
declarations.name: q

declarations.doc: The MSD recurrence of `Γ_NP`: `q (n+3) = 2 q (n+2) + q (n+1) + 3 q n`. Equivalently the word `B* = (1, -2, -1, -3)` has consumed sum zero at every start remaining `n + 4`.
declarations.name: q_rec

declarations.doc: The `3 q n` term drops modulo 3.
declarations.name: q_mod_three

declarations.doc: The triple `(q n, q (n+1), q (n+2))` in `(ℤ/3ℤ)³` has period 8.
declarations.name: q_triple_mod3_period8

declarations.doc: `q n ≡ 0 (mod 3)` iff `n ≡ 3 or 7 (mod 8)`.
declarations.name: q_dvd_three_iff

declarations.doc: Linear three-register recursor; equals `(q n, q (n+1), q (n+2))`.
declarations.name: qTriple

declarations.doc: The triple `(q n, q (n+1), q (n+2))` in `(ℤ/9ℤ)³` has period 24.
declarations.name: q_triple_mod9_period24

declarations.doc: Residual coordinates `(s₁, s₂, s₃)`.
declarations.name: State

declarations.doc: Interior difference alphabet. Not required for the origin obstruction.
declarations.name: controlAlphabet

declarations.doc: `T_w(s₁,s₂,s₃) = (3 s₃, s₁+s₃, s₂+2 s₃-w)`.
declarations.name: step

declarations.doc: On the accepting plane `F = {s₃ = 0}`.
declarations.name: OnF

declarations.doc: One unrestricted integer step.
declarations.name: StepRel

declarations.doc: Forward images of the origin. Not the live set `L₀`.
declarations.name: OriginReachable

declarations.doc: Two-step return to `F` lands on the ray `(3a, a, 0)` with `a = b - w`.
declarations.name: two_step_on_F

declarations.doc: Zero section on integers: ``I_0(x)=3x``.
declarations.name: I0

declarations.doc: ``I_a(n) mod m`` depends only on ``n mod m``.
declarations.name: iz_mod_of_congruent

declarations.doc: If ``|x| > 1`` then ``3|x|`` is composite.
declarations.name: i0_not_prime_of_natAbs

declarations.doc: Same residue mod ``210``, distinguished by ``I_0``.
declarations.name: sievePrime_I0_separator

declarations.doc: The jet-prime separator: `I0 1 = 3` is prime while `I0 4 = 12` is not, so the jet residual does not coincide with primality.
declarations.name: jetPrime_I0_separator

declarations.doc: The product of two least significant digits is again a trit: `-1`, `0` or `1`.
declarations.name: lsdZ_mul_is_trit

declarations.doc: `lsd` is multiplicative: `lsd (x * y) = lsd x * lsd y`.
declarations.name: lsdZ_mul

declarations.doc: Product expansion into digit and carry: `x * y = lsd x * lsd y + 3 * (lsd x * D y + lsd y * D x + 3 * D x * D y)`.
declarations.name: product_expansion

declarations.doc: Twisted Leibniz rule. Not the ordinary product rule.
declarations.name: D_mul

declarations.doc: The balanced-ternary rewrite of `2`: `2 = -1 + 3 * 1`.
declarations.name: rewrite_sum2

declarations.doc: The balanced-ternary rewrite of `-2`: `-2 = 1 + 3 * (-1)`.
declarations.name: rewrite_sum_neg2

declarations.doc: LSD-only addition carry. This is the standard balanced-ternary table.
declarations.name: addDigit

declarations.doc: `addDigit` splits a sum into digit and carry: `a + b = (addDigit a b).1 + 3 * (addDigit a b).2`.
declarations.name: addDigit_eq

declarations.doc: `D` is additive up to a single carry: `D (x + y) = D x + D y + c`, where `c` is the carry digit of `lsd x + lsd y`.
declarations.name: D_add

declarations.doc: `cmp3 x y = Trit.minus` when `x < y`.
declarations.name: cmp3_lt

declarations.doc: `cmp3 x x = Trit.zero`.
declarations.name: cmp3_eq

declarations.doc: `cmp3 x y = Trit.plus` when `y < x`.
declarations.name: cmp3_gt

declarations.doc: Antisymmetry: negating `cmp3 x y` gives `cmp3 y x`.
declarations.name: cmp3_antisym

declarations.doc: `cmp3` is translation invariant: `cmp3 (x + z) (y + z) = cmp3 x y`.
declarations.name: cmp3_translate

declarations.doc: Negating both arguments negates the comparison.
declarations.name: cmp3_neg

declarations.doc: Scaling both arguments by a positive constant leaves `cmp3` unchanged.
declarations.name: cmp3_mul_pos

declarations.doc: Scaling both arguments by a negative constant negates `cmp3`.
declarations.name: cmp3_mul_neg

declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the twisted Leibniz rule: the section derivative of a product, evaluated at `x`, in terms of the two factors' section derivatives and their least significant digits at `a`.
declarations.name: section_product_eval

declarations.doc: Pointwise form of the section chain rule: evaluating `sectionDeriv a (f.comp g)` at `x` feeds `eval x (sectionDeriv a g)` into `sectionDeriv (lsd (eval a g)) f`.
declarations.name: section_comp_eval

declarations.doc: Twisted Leibniz for the section derivative: `sectionDeriv a (f * g)` is the usual two-term rule with each factor twisted by the other's least significant digit at `a`, plus a `3`-scaled cross term.
declarations.name: section_product

declarations.doc: Section chain rule: `sectionDeriv a (f.comp g) = (sectionDeriv (lsd (eval a g)) f) .comp (sectionDeriv a g)` -- the outer factor is taken at the inner map's least significant digit, not at `a`.
declarations.name: section_comp

declarations.doc: The least significant digit of a composite is the outer map's least significant digit taken at the inner one: `lsd (eval a (f.comp g)) = lsd (eval (lsd (eval a g)) f)`.
declarations.name: rho_comp

declarations.doc: Overlapping critical pair at sites `0` and `1` joins after stripping.
declarations.name: overlap_join

declarations.doc: Raw Lean lists of the overlapping pair are not equal; stripping joins them.
declarations.name: overlap_minus5_two_raw

declarations.doc: `N1` difference at the deepest layer: `3(p^2 - q^2) + 3^k (p - q)`.
declarations.name: n1Resid_deepest_diff

declarations.doc: At the deepest layer, `N1` agreement modulo `3^k` is `3^(k-1) | p^2 - q^2`.
declarations.name: deepest_n1_iff

declarations.doc: At the deepest layer `N1` is congruent to `deepestN1 p` modulo `3^k`, for `k >= 2`.
declarations.name: deepest_n1_mod

declarations.doc: `N2` vanishes modulo `3^k` at the deepest layer.
declarations.name: deepest_n2_zero

declarations.doc: `N3` vanishes modulo `3^k` at the deepest layer.
declarations.name: deepest_n3_zero

declarations.doc: Agreement of the depth-`k-1` `N1` residuals to order `3^k` forces `3^(k-1)` to divide `(p - q) * (p + q)`. It is the square factorisation, not the layer description, that this statement carries.
declarations.name: deepest_sq_of_n1

declarations.doc: Two points of balanced width `m` whose difference is divisible by `3^m` are equal.
declarations.name: balWidth_dvd_sub

declarations.doc: Two points of balanced width `m` whose sum is divisible by `3^m` are negatives.
declarations.name: balWidth_dvd_add

declarations.doc: A packed jet has balanced width `m`.
declarations.name: packWord_integerJet_balWidth

declarations.doc: When `3^m` divides `n`, the jet packs to zero and `n = 3^m * D^m n`.
declarations.name: iterDZ_of_dvd

declarations.doc: When `3^m` divides `p^3`, `N0` is the exact quotient `p^3 / 3^m`.
declarations.name: n0Resid_of_dvd

declarations.doc: Decomposition of an `N0` difference into cube and jet parts.
declarations.name: n0_congr_decomp

declarations.doc: `3` is prime in the integers.
declarations.name: three_prime

declarations.doc: `3 | p^2` implies `3 | p`.
declarations.name: three_dvd_of_dvd_sq

declarations.doc: The zero exponent satisfies `k - 1 <= 2 * zeroExp k`, the square half of its definition.
declarations.name: zeroExp_sq

declarations.doc: The zero exponent satisfies `2k - 1 <= 3 * zeroExp k`, the cube half.
declarations.name: zeroExp_cu

declarations.doc: `N1` at zero is `3^(2m)`.
declarations.name: n1Resid_zero

declarations.doc: `N0` at zero is `0`.
declarations.name: n0Resid_zero

declarations.doc: At the deepest layer `3^k` divides `N1(0)`, for `k >= 2`.
declarations.name: deepest_n1_zero

declarations.doc: Divisibility by `3^(zeroExp k)` puts a point in the deepest zero fibre.
declarations.name: zero_fibre_of

declarations.doc: Conversely, membership of the deepest zero fibre forces `3^(zeroExp k) | p`.
declarations.name: zero_fibre_imp

declarations.doc: The deepest fibre criterion: `N1` and `N0` agreement modulo `3^k` together hold exactly when `p^2 = q^2` modulo `3^(k-1)` and the `N0` parts agree.
declarations.name: deepest_equiv_iff

declarations.doc: The deepest-layer sign condition for `p` against `-p`, in `N1` and `N0` together.
declarations.name: sign_deepest

declarations.doc: At depth `k-1-r`, `N2` residuals agree modulo `3^k` exactly when `p = q` modulo `3^r`: the deficit `r` is what the layer can see.
declarations.name: depthDeficit_n2_visibility

declarations.doc: At deficit zero the `N2` condition is automatic.
declarations.name: depthDeficit_zero_N2

declarations.doc: At deficit one the `N2` condition reduces to `3 | p - q`.
declarations.name: depthDeficit_one_N2

declarations.doc: At deficit two the `N2` condition reduces to `9 | p - q`.
declarations.name: depthDeficit_two_N2_visibility

declarations.doc: At deficit two, `N3` vanishes modulo `3^k` once `k >= 5`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_n3_zero

declarations.doc: At deficit two, `N2` is congruent to `2 * 3^(k-2) p` modulo `3^k`, for `k >= 5`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_n2_mod

declarations.doc: At deficit two, `N1` is congruent to `3p^2 + 3^(k-2) p` modulo `3^k`, for `k >= 6`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_n1_mod

declarations.doc: The deficit-two `N1` condition, reduced to a divisibility at order `k-1`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_n1_iff

declarations.doc: The deficit-two `N1` condition once `N2` has forced `9 | p - q`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_n1_after_n2

declarations.doc: The deficit-two fibre criterion: `N2` and `N1` agreement at depth `k-3` together, spelled out as the congruence modulo `9`, the order-`(k-1)` product condition, and `N0`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_equiv_iff

declarations.doc: At deficit two the `N2` sign condition holds exactly when `9` divides `p`.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_sign_n2_iff

declarations.doc: Deficit-two agreement at horizon `k` carries down to the finer horizon.
declarations.name: deficitTwo_horizon_refines

declarations.doc: `N1(p) - N1(q) = 3 (p - q)(p + q + 3^m)` -- the factorisation the fibre argument uses.
declarations.name: n1Resid_diff

declarations.doc: `N3(m) - N3(n) = 2 (3^(2m+1) - 3^(2n+1))`; `N3` does not depend on the point.
declarations.name: n3Resid_sub

declarations.doc: The third Newton coordinate of the residual family is `N2`.
declarations.name: newton_n2_eq

declarations.doc: At one depth, `3^k` divides the `N2` difference exactly when it divides `3^(m+1)(p - q)`.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n2

declarations.doc: Below the depth, `k <= m + 1`, the `N2` difference is divisible outright.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n2_of_le

declarations.doc: Above the depth, `m + 1 <= k`, the `N2` condition reduces to `3^(k-m-1) | p - q`.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n2_succ

declarations.doc: Two integers of balanced width `m` differ by at most `3^m - 1`.
declarations.name: balWidth_sub

declarations.doc: `N2` separates points of `P_m` once `2m + 1 <= k`: agreement to that order forces `p = q`. The width bound is what closes it -- the difference cannot reach `3^(k-m-1)`.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n2_injective

declarations.doc: `N3` residuals agree modulo `3^k` when `k` is below both depths.
declarations.name: n3_dvd_of_deep

declarations.doc: Cross-depth `N3` criterion: for `m <= n`, `3^k` divides `N3(m) - N3(n)` exactly when `k <= 2m + 1` or the depths coincide.
declarations.name: n3_dvd_iff

declarations.doc: The `N1` sign condition, reduced to divisibility of `2 * 3^(m+1) * p`.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n1_sign

declarations.doc: The `N2` sign condition, reduced to divisibility of `3^(m+1) * p`.
declarations.name: sameDepth_n2_sign

declarations.doc: An `N1` sign agreement implies the `N2` one: the odd pair is governed by `N1`.
declarations.name: sign_n2_of_n1

declarations.doc: `D^m` is odd: `D^m (-n) = - D^m n`.
declarations.name: iterDZ_neg

declarations.doc: `N0(p)` and `N0(-p)` agree modulo `3^k` exactly when `3^k` divides `N0(p)`; the sign survives only where the residual already vanishes.
declarations.name: sign_n0

declarations.doc: Horizon refinement at depth `k-2`: agreement of the `N2`, `N1` and `N0` residuals to order `3^k` carries down to order `3^(k-1)` for each of the three.
declarations.name: inter_horizon_refines

declarations.doc: The depth of the reduced `N0` residual.
declarations.name: n0_reduced_depth

declarations.doc: `N0(p)` and `N0(-p)` agree modulo `3^k` exactly when `3^k` divides `N0(p)`: the sign survives the reduction only where the residual already vanishes.
declarations.name: n0_sign_survives

declarations.doc: `N0` modulo a power of three sees only the input modulo a power of three.
declarations.name: n0_visible_mod

declarations.doc: Split a power of three: `3^a = 3^b * 3^(a-b)` for `b <= a`.
declarations.name: pow3_split

declarations.doc: The `N1` agreement condition at depth `k-1-r`, reduced to a divisibility at order `k-1`.
declarations.name: deficit_n1_iff

declarations.doc: Once `N2` is fixed, the depth-`k-1-r` `N1` residuals agree to order `3^k` exactly when `3^(k-1-r)` divides `d * (p + q + 3^(k-1-r))`, where `p - q = 3^r * d`.
declarations.name: n1_after_n2_iff

declarations.doc: `3^r | 2p` implies `3^r | p`.
declarations.name: three_pow_dvd_of_two_mul_pow

declarations.doc: If `3^r` does not divide `p`, some `s < r` is the exact valuation of `p`.
declarations.name: exists_val_lt

declarations.doc: For a unit `p` congruent to `q` mod 3, the sum `p + q` is a unit too.
declarations.name: not_three_dvd_add_of_unit

declarations.doc: `N2` together with `N1` separates units: on points of balanced width `k-1-r` with `p` prime to 3, agreement in both layers forces `p = q`, for every `r >= 1`.
declarations.name: n1_unit_injective

declarations.doc: The injectivity step at an exact valuation `s < r`.
declarations.name: n1_low_val_injective

declarations.doc: After `N2`, a point whose valuation is below `r` is determined: agreement of the `N1` residuals forces `p = q` on balanced width `k-1-r`, for `r >= 1` and `r + 1 <= k`.
declarations.name: n1_val_lt_injective

declarations.doc: Every nontrivial `N2`-then-`N1` fibre lies in `3^r ZZ`: distinct `p != q` of balanced width `k-1-r` that agree in both layers force `3^r | p`.
declarations.name: n21_fibre_in_pow

declarations.doc: The `N2` sign condition at depth `k-1-r` holds exactly when `3^r` divides `p`.
declarations.name: n21_sign_n2_iff

declarations.doc: The `N1` sign condition at depth `k-1-r` holds exactly when `3^r` divides `p`.
declarations.name: n21_sign_n1_iff

declarations.doc: `p` and `-p` agree in both the `N2` and `N1` layers exactly when `3^r` divides `p`.
declarations.name: n21_sign_iff

declarations.doc: On the scaled core `3^r u`, the `N1` condition reduces to the deepest `N1` at horizon `k - 2r`, once `2r + 2 <= k`.
declarations.name: n1_high_val_scaled

declarations.doc: The `r = 1` instance of unit injectivity.
declarations.name: n1_unit_r1

declarations.doc: The `r = 2` instance of unit injectivity.
declarations.name: n1_unit_r2

declarations.doc: The residual family in closed form: `eval x (cubicResid m p) = 3^(2m) x^3 + 3^(m+1) p x^2 + 3 p^2 x + D^m (p^3)`.
declarations.name: eval_cubicResid

declarations.doc: `cubicResid 0 0 = X^3` -- the family starts at the cube.
declarations.name: cubicResid_zero

declarations.doc: Constant coefficient of `cubic A B lin cst` is `cst`.
declarations.name: coeff_cubic_zero

declarations.doc: Linear coefficient of `cubic A B lin cst` is `lin`.
declarations.name: coeff_cubic_one

declarations.doc: Quadratic coefficient of `cubic A B lin cst` is `B`.
declarations.name: coeff_cubic_two

declarations.doc: Cubic coefficient of `cubic A B lin cst` is `A`.
declarations.name: coeff_cubic_three

declarations.doc: `cubic` is injective in its four coefficients.
declarations.name: cubic_inj

declarations.doc: `cubic` subtracts coefficientwise.

declarations.doc: **Target 4.** The block shift law. A singular branch with derivative valuation at least `w.length` is fully ternary along `w`, and the state it reaches is shifted by the *balanced value* of the word, scaled by the excess `3 ^ i`: 𝔇_w (3^j d + 3^(j+i) x) = (d + 3^i · packWord w) + 3^(j+i) x, j = |w|. At `i = 0` this is the leaf law: the `3 ^ e` words of length `e` reach the states `d + packWord w`, and `packWord` is injective on words of a fixed length, so those shifts run over a complete residue system modulo `3 ^ e`. That is what makes the shifted family separate residues; note the shift is the balanced value of the word and not its digit sum.

For integers H,N>=1, E>=0, and arbitrary points z_0,...,z_(N-1) on the product of two unit circles, suppose every nonzero integer pair (k,l) with abs(k),abs(l)<=H has normalized Fourier sum norm at most E. For real endpoints a<=b<=a+1 and c<=d<=c+1, the product B of the images of [a,b) and [c,d) then satisfies abs(count(z_n in B)/N-(b-a)*(d-c)) <= 5/sqrt(H+1)+(3+2*log(H))^2*E. Empty, full, wrapped arcs and sample boundary hits are included. The actual Fejer kernel, tails, saturated smoothing, coefficient mass and finite count transfer are proved; no smoothing estimate is assumed. This is the complete finite discrepancy obligation Q3, not the specific OOE Fourier rate or effective modular-return assembly.

Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage pending. For a finite-dimensional unit torus sequence whose every nonzero integer Fourier average tends to zero, empirical measures converge weakly to normalized Haar measure. Counts of every Borel set with Haar-null frontier, divided by N, tend to its Haar measure. For real fractional parts and fixed 0<=a_i<b_i<=1, every half-open product box has frequency product_i(b_i-a_i), including a_i=0 and b_i=1. Circle-arc volumes and null boundaries are proved; no box-frequency premise is assumed.

Kernel-checked qualitative Weyl criterion; advisory statement coverage pending. For any finite index type d and sequence x in the unit torus, if the averages of every nonzero integer Fourier monomial tend to zero, then averages of every continuous complex-valued function tend to its normalized Haar integral. Fourier integrals, the zero mode, finite linear combinations, contraction bounds and the passage by uniform approximation are proved, using Mathlib's dense Fourier span. Every nonempty open set is visited after every prescribed natural index T, using a nonnegative continuous function with positive Haar integral. For real representatives, any simultaneous open fractional-part box with 0<=a_i<b_i<=1 is visited arbitrarily late. The integer dot-product phase is identified with the torus monomial. No approximation or positive-measure assertion is assumed, and no quantitative discrepancy or shrinking-target claim is made.

Kernel-checked classical first-derivative estimate; advisory statement coverage pending. For a real sequence f, natural N and delta>0, if all N increments f(n+1)-f(n), 0<=n<N, lie in [delta,1-delta] and are monotone in either direction, then the norm of sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*f(n)) is at most 1/delta. The last increment uses f(N), and N=0 is included. The reciprocal chord identity, its constant real part and monotone imaginary part, Jordan sine lower bound, summation by parts and endpoint variation estimate are proved. If f is continuous on [a,a+N], has derivative g on the interior, and g is monotone with delta<=g<=1-delta, the same bound holds on the translated lattice a+n. A mean value point in each actual unit cell proves this transfer. For globally monotone increments, a positive prefix gap delta(N) gives averages tending to zero if N*delta(N) tends to infinity. No exponential-sum or variation estimate is assumed. Only the derivative band between zero and one is formalized; this is not Paper E's mixed-power cancellation, BoxRecurrence, or a termination theorem.

Kernel-checked; advisory statement coverage pending. Distinct positive noninteger real powers of A*t+B, A>0, with nonzero real scales have each fixed half-open box's volume as parameter frequency. If P has parameter density delta, and natural q,d>0, the number of distinct starts (1+q*t)^d<=X with P(t), divided by X^(1/d), tends to delta/q. The exact cutoff and injectivity are proved. For delta>0 and fixed c>1 every sufficiently large (X,cX] contains such a start. Finite changes of P preserve density. No effective rate is asserted.

Kernel-checked simultaneous recurrence for powers; advisory statement coverage pending. For a finite index type, distinct positive noninteger real exponents p_i, nonzero real scales w_i, real A>0 and B, every box 0<=a_i<b_i<=1 has arbitrarily late natural samples n with a_i<fract(w_i*(A*n+B)^p_i)<b_i for all i. The nonzero Fourier coefficients are shown to yield a nonzero mixed-power phase. Cancellation is discharged by the proved mixed-power theorem and the Fourier-to-box criterion. This is unconditional for each fixed family and fixed box; no uniform rate, shrinking target, or growing-depth conclusion is asserted.

Kernel-checked classical mixed-power cancellation; advisory statement coverage pending. Let S be a finite index set, p_i distinct positive noninteger real exponents, and c_i real coefficients with at least one nonzero. For every real A>0 and B, the averages (1/N)*sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*sum_(i in S) c_i*(A*n+B)^p_i) tend to zero. The main proof removes zero coefficients and chooses the largest remaining exponent. More generally, it suffices that a unique largest exponent lies strictly between some natural m and m+1 and has nonzero coefficient; lower exponents may be arbitrary real numbers. A derivative tower with D_0=f, a_0=c, a_(k+1)=a_k*(p-k), eventual derivative D_k'=D_(k+1), and D_k(x)/x^(p-k) tending to a_k gives cancellation when c!=0 and m<p<m+1. Actual positive fixed differences preserve this tower with exponent p-1 and leading coefficient h*c*p, proved using moving mean-value points. The base case follows from the proved first-derivative estimate, finite-prefix removal, and conjugation; higher orders follow by qualitative van der Corput. Real powers, finite addition, lower-order terms and positive affine progression changes are proved to satisfy the tower conditions. No cancellation, equidistribution, or analytic estimate is assumed in the concrete mixed-power theorem. This does not yet prove Fourier-to-box recurrence, the concrete Paper E exponent/box specialization, shrinking-target bounds, or termination.

Kernel-checked formalization of a classical quantitative second-derivative estimate; advisory statement coverage pending. For every natural N, real a, lambda>0 and C>=1, suppose f has derivative g and g has derivative q at every point of the closed interval [a,a+N]. If lambda<=q<=C*lambda throughout that interval, or -C*lambda<=q<=-lambda throughout it, then the norm of sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*f(a+n)) is at most 4*C*N*sqrt(lambda)+8/sqrt(lambda). The analogous hypotheses on [a,a+2*N] give the spacing-two bound 8*C*N*sqrt(lambda)+4/sqrt(lambda). N=0 and the endpoint one lattice step beyond the final summand are retained. The discrete proof assumes lambda*(j-i)<=d(j)-d(i)<=U*(j-i) for all 0<=i<=j<N, with d(n)=F(n+1)-F(n), U>=0; for every 0<delta<=1/2 it proves norm(sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*F(n)))<=(U*N+2)*(2*delta/lambda+2+1/delta). Integer-band partitioning counts both resonant ends and applies the proved Kusmin-Landau estimate to the middle block. Mean-value comparisons prove the continuous-to-discrete hypotheses. No cancellation or correlation bound is assumed. No Juggler production or discrepancy theorem is asserted. The subsequent OOEECurvature module proves actual carry-cell curvature and unweighted sums; carry Fourier errors and complete production remain outstanding in Lean.

Kernel-checked classical sublinear-power cancellation; advisory statement coverage pending. For every real c!=0 and 0<theta<1, the complex averages (1/N)*sum_(n<N) exp(2*pi*i*c*n^theta) tend to zero. For c>0, A>0, and c*theta*A^(theta-1)<=1/2, every shifted prefix has norm at most 1/(c*theta*(A+N)^(theta-1)). The proof derives the positive decreasing derivative and applies the proved first-derivative bound, proves existence of a suitable natural shift using derivative decay, removes a finite initial segment, and treats negative coefficients by complex conjugation. The finite-prefix removal lemma applies to any complex sequence whose shifted averages tend to zero. No power-phase cancellation premise is used. This is a single sublinear-power base case, not a theorem about higher or mixed powers, their shifted differences, or simultaneous-box recurrence.

Kernel-checked formalization of qualitative van der Corput; advisory statement coverage pending. For every complex sequence z and fixed real C>0 with norm(z(n))<=C for all natural n, if for every fixed positive natural d the complex averages (1/N)*sum_(n<N) z(n+d)*conj(z(n)) tend to zero as N tends to infinity, then (1/N)*sum_(n<N) z(n) tends to zero. For a unit-bounded sequence, the full shifted sum differs from its N-d-term overlap correlation by norm at most d for every N,d, including N<d. The normalized finite inequality has right side 2/H+(4/H)*sum_(1<=d<H) norm(correlation(z,N,d))/N for 1<=H<=N. The phase specialization proves cancellation for exp(2*pi*i*f(n)) from cancellation for every positive fixed difference f(n+d)-f(n). All difference-cancellation hypotheses remain explicit. This does not prove the power-phase estimates or BoxRecurrence needed for Paper E Theorem 4.1, and gives no quantitative or growing-depth uniformity.

Kernel-checked formalization of a classical finite van der Corput inequality; advisory statement coverage pending. For z:Nat->Complex, natural 1<=H<=N, and |z(n)|<=1 for n<N, put S=sum_(n<N) z(n) and T_d=sum_(n<N-d) z(n+d)*conj(z(n)). Then |S|^2<=2*N^2/H+(4*N/H)*sum_(1<=d<H)|T_d|. The overlap length is exactly N-d, without periodic completion or a cancellation hypothesis. The more general energy inequality H^2*|S|^2<=(N+H)*H*(N+2*sum_(1<=d<H)|T_d|) holds for every natural N,H under the same modulus bound. The module proves zero-padded row sums and overlaps, finite Cauchy-Schwarz, diagonal and off-diagonal bounds, and the odd-lattice specialization z(n)=exp(2*pi*i*f(a+2*n)) for every real-valued f on natural integers and natural a; each correlation is the exponential sum of the actual shifted phase difference over N-d terms. This supplies a classical finite input to the written OOEE estimate, not its correlation bounds, derivative tests, discrepancy estimates, poor-fibre theorem, or a termination or escape result.

The analogue of Paper C Theorem 1 for every nonempty backward-closed set is false for both ordinary Collatz shortcut signs. For C_plus(n)=n/2 on evens and (3n+1)/2 on odds, and C_minus(n)=n/2 on evens and (3n-1)/2 on odds, every multiple m of three has exactly the one predecessor 2m. Consequently A={3*2^k : k>=0} is infinite and backward-closed for both maps. Its injective geometric enumeration has reciprocal sum exactly 2/3, and every finite subset S of A has sum_{n in S} 1/n <= 2/3. The ray is not forward-closed: C_plus(3)=5 and C_minus(3)=4 leave it. It therefore does not itself refute a fate-specific almost-all-to-all implication. This is the exact obstruction to transferring the general backward-density engine, not a termination or nontermination result. Paper D version 1.1.0, docs/theory/collatz_3n_minus_1_m_cycles_note.md. THE ROUTE is that of the m <= 58 row (J-negative-m-cycles-excluded-through-58, now superseded) with a sixth lemma: negative Lemma 8 y >= 2^a + 1, the run identity, the cycle equation Lambda < m/(x_min - 1), the chaining u' < u^delta / 2, the exact enumeration of the admissible lengths by the three-gap walk below Rhin's ceiling K_3(m), the contracting-prefix sieve, and now the valley count; each admissible length is tested against two displays and excluded if either holds. THE NEW LEMMA (Lemma 6 of the manuscript) is the transposition of the arrangement behind Hercher's Main Theorem 21. The earlier lemmas relax the same system twice, once by putting every local minimum at the floor and once by dropping the objective, and both relaxations are loose at the same time because a cycle cannot have all its valleys at the floor and carry o odd steps. Writing b_i = log2 u_i over the local minima, the constraints are b_i >= L0 = log2(X0 - 1), b_{i+1} < delta b_i - 1 (Lemma 3) and sum b_i >= o (Lemma 1 summed), with Lambda < sum 2^(-b_i) (Lemma 2) the objective. The lemma keeps them together through a threshold rather than a vertex enumeration: for every T >= L0, at most R(T) of the minima lie at or below T, where R(T) is the largest r <= m with r T + sum_{t <= m-r} (delta^t T - (delta^t - 1)/(delta - 1)) >= o, the largest total the chaining allows once the gaps between the low minima are merged into one; then Lambda < R(T) 2^(-L0) + (m - R(T)) 2^(-T). The minimum over T is exact rather than a grid: the bound is piecewise in T with breakpoints T_r = (o + A_{m-r}) / (r + B_{m-r}) and falls with T on each piece. At T = L0 it is Lemma 2, so the refinement is never weaker than what it refines. AT 2^51: no admissible length below the ceiling for m <= 52; for 53 <= m <= 61 the admissible lengths are excluded, the closest with 0.1 bits to spare at m = 61, K = 83130157078217; at m = 62 that same length survives with 0.3 bits. At every finite residue level ell>=2, a strictly positive weight table satisfying either the normalized 3n-1 rows or the normalized 3n+1 rows of the fixed 1/50 grid must satisfy 1<=mu^(-100)+(mu^29+mu^(-21))/3 for every positive real grid rate mu used in those rows. The fourfold map and both child index maps are affine permutations; the three-lift minima sum to at most one third of the total weight. Equivalently, 3*mu^100<=3+mu^129+mu^79. In the explicitly stated at-most-linear rate range mu^50<=2, every such table has mu<5069/5000 and mu^5000<2^99, hence exponent 50*log_2(mu)<99/100. The harmonic rate mu^50=2 is impossible, since it would imply 2^79>=3^50, contradicting the strict integer inequality. AboveAnchor walk nonnegativity and hug domination: the Section 5 discrete walk layer ported from cycles to open trajectories. If AboveAnchor(n,w) with n >= 2, then every prefix length k <= |w| satisfies 2^k <= 3^{oddCount(w.take k)} (aboveAnchor_prefix_pow_le, AboveAnchorWalk.lean): a never-descending orbit segment keeps the exponent walk u_k >= 0, exactly the CycleMin hypothesis of cycleMin_prefix_pow_le with no cycle, by composing the defect-free upper envelope power_bound_contracts with the anchor hypothesis. Composed with hug minimality (hugOdds_least), every above-anchor prefix dominates the exact hug itinerary in odd count: hugOdds k <= oddCount(w.take k) (aboveAnchor_prefix_odds_ge_hug; full-word form aboveAnchor_odds_ge_hug). Hence a hypothetical descent-free flight carries odd density at least log 2 / log 3 in every prefix, and the hug adversary prices open descent-free flight, not only hypothetical cycles. Hypothesis: recurrent hug domination (flight note Sec. 5.5) forces O(y) >= O*(y) at every scale for every persistent divergent orbit, so that every Clotho basin is every-block unconditionally. Refuted twice. Structurally: every flight-note law bounds escape from below - a_k >= hugOdds(k) (aboveAnchor_prefix_odds_ge_hug), u_k >= 0, u_k >= log2(log x_k / log n), hug excess to infinity, linear peak growth - and none bounds it from above; the gate O(y) >= O*(y) is an upper bound on escape speed and nothing in the laboratory supplies one. Empirically: on the seven canonical high-flyers, at the first passage of every recorded decade from 1e6 to 1e5000, the gate is never met; the walk gain per odd step at passage is 0.08..0.58 against gates of 0.0006..0.04, between 28 and 650 times too fast (slowest passage: 1122603 at 1e5000, O = 67 odd steps in 96, gain 0.145, 240 times the gate 0.0006; 48443 reaches 1e5000 in 31 steps with 26 odd). Random odd starts near 1e6 never meet it either. So the Clotho every-block statement (J-clotho-basin-every-block-criterion) stays conditional on slow escape, and slow escape is neither forced nor observed: a persistent thread whose basin is every-block would be unlike every flight ever realised. Excludes nothing; not a halt theorem.

The Juggler-Collatz bridge, stated as theorems over the one shared object, the List Branch word, with no real number and nothing measured in any statement. COLLATZ IS WORD-AFFINE WITH THE CORRECTION POINTING UP: for the shortcut map C (x/2 on evens, (3x+1)/2 on odds) and w = parityWord x d the first d parities of the orbit of x, 2^d * C^d(x) = 3^(oddCount w) * x + wordConst w with wordConst w >= 0 a function of the word alone (word_affine; wordConst (odd :: w) = 3^(oddCount w) + 2 wordConst w, wordConst (even :: w) = 2 wordConst w, and wordConst w = 0 iff w has no odd letter). JUGGLER IS EXPONENT-AFFINE WITH THE CORRECTION POINTING DOWN: juggler_word_power restates power_bound_word as (image n w)^(2^|w|) <= n^(3^(oddCount w)) for a realised word. The same multiplier 3^o/2^d acts on x in one problem and on log n in the other, with corrections of opposite sign, and that is the whole of the sign flip on cycles: cycle_contracting (a positive shortcut cycle of length d >= 1 has 3^o < 2^d, because 2^d x = 3^o x + c with c >= 1 whenever the word has an odd letter and 2^d x = x is impossible otherwise) sits beside juggler_cycle_expanding = cycle_itinerary_formally_expanding (2^d < 3^o). TERRAS IN THIS VOCABULARY: parityWord_eq_iff, parityWord x d = parityWord y d iff x = y mod 2^d, and image_parityWord, the residues modulo 2^d map bijectively onto allWords d (allWords_card gives 2^d). Compiles with no sorry; #print axioms on word_affine gives propext and Quot.sound only, on the counting theorems propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Registered as an auxiliary Juggler module (not a paper review object); it imports Problems.Collatz.Shortcut, RateFreeDensity, PaperBCertificateRecursion, Envelope and CycleCore. WHAT IT IS NOT: no density, no asymptotic, no bound in either problem, and nothing about how the Juggler word attaches to n, which is Hypothesis FD. It records that the bridge of J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up is well defined at the word level, and it closes the gap that the Collatz half of the sign flip was previously only an algebraic lemma with the orbit identity assumed (Problems/Collatz/Cycles.lean expanding_excludes_positive_candidate): the identity is now derived by iterating shortcutC. NOTE 2026-09-19: CollatzBridge.lean now defines the shortcut map locally and is a layer module of Paper A's barrel; decidedAtResidues_card and neg_seventeen_inhabits_cycleMinShape live in the auxiliary CollatzBridgeLab.lean, same namespace, outside the barrel.

Paper B's survivor count is a Collatz residue count, in Lean. undecidedResidues_card: the number of residues r modulo 2^d whose parity word parityWord r d has no contracting prefix equals neverNegCount d, the N_d of RateFreeDensity; decidedAtResidues_card: the number whose word is a minimal certificate (first contracts at exactly d) equals minimalCertCount d, the M_d of PaperBCertificateRecursion. The Collatz walk charge, in natural numbers. Define evenCharge on words by evenCharge [] = 0, evenCharge (even :: w) = 3^(oddCount w) + 2 evenCharge w, evenCharge (odd :: w) = 2 evenCharge w -- in closed form the sum over even positions i of 3^(o - a_i) 2^i with a_i the odd letters before i. Then (wordConst_add_two_pow) wordConst w + 2^|w| = 3^(oddCount w) + evenCharge w, so the odd-step constant and the even-step charge differ exactly by the multiplier gap; (two_pow_mul_iter_add_one) for every start x and depth d, 2^d (C^d(x) + 1) = 3^o (x + 1) + evenCharge (parityWord x d): conjugating the odd step by z = x + 1 makes every correction come from an even step; (three_pow_mul_add_one_le) hence 3^o (x + 1) <= 2^d (C^d(x) + 1), the Collatz lower envelope, the mirror of power_bound_word with the inequality reversed because the +1s only push up; (cycle_even_charge) on a cycle, (x + 1) 2^d = (x + 1) 3^o + evenCharge w, i.e. the surplus (x_0 + 1)(2^K - 3^p) IS the even-step charge of the word -- the Collatz counterpart of Paper A's finance inequality n log n (3^o - 2^L) <= L 3^o, as an identity rather than a bound; (trivial_cycle_charge) the trivial cycle 1 -> 2 -> 1 has word OE, charge 2 and (1+1)(4 - 3) = 2, by decide +kernel. Read with 2^(-h_i) = 2^i/3^(a_i) 2^(-d)... precisely evenCharge w / (2^d) = 3^o sum over even steps of 2^(-h_i) up to the factor 3^o/2^d, this is the exact form of the statement whose analytic version is J-collatz-walk-charge-constant. Compiles with no sorry; standard axioms. Priority: the z = x + 1 conjugation of the odd step is classical (Simons-de Weger's up-run formula); the even-step reading of the affine constant is likely in Halbeisen-Hungerbuehler 1997's parity-word functional; not checked beyond Hercher 2023, which does not use it. Not a bound, not a halt theorem.

The height-only bound of J-collatz-walk-charge-constant is sharp, so composing the rotation-orbit average with Hercher's per-run averaging (Lemma 26 of Hercher 2023) gains nothing: the two read the same slack and the rotation average is its sharp reading. ARGUMENT (EXACT — HUMAN PROOF). The hug word with p odd letters -- the lowest non-negative walk, odd exactly when the height is below 1 -- has its odd steps at the heights frac(a alpha), a = 0..p-1, alpha = log2(3/2), so its odd-step sum of 2^(-h) is H(p) = sum_{a<p} 2^(-frac(a alpha)) by construction. Terras's bijection realises it: exists_residue_of_word (CollatzBridge.lean, the surjective half of image_parityWord) gives r < 2^K with parityWord r K equal to the hug word, and every x_0 = r mod 2^K follows it. Along a member x_0 far above 2^K the orbit stays above x_0 and x_j + 1 = 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1 + S_j) with S_j <= K, so x_0 sum_{odd} 1/x_j = H(p)(1 + O(K/x_0)). Hence any bound on the odd reciprocal sum that uses only x_j + 1 >= 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1) and x_j >= x_0 is at least H(p)/(x_0 + 1) up to O(K/x_0^2), and Hercher's (3/4) K/X_0 is a weaker evaluation of that same information, not a different source of it. NUMBERS. x_0 * sum_{odd} 1/x_j / H(p) = 1.000000000000 at p = 12, 53, 300, 665 (K = 19, 84, 475, 1054) with x_0 = r + 2^(K + 300), exact rational arithmetic; the realised residues are below 2^K and the orbits follow the hug word letter for letter. Not a kill, not a period bound, not a halt theorem.

The exact Collatz cycle condition, as a statement about the word. Over ℤ the affine identity of CollatzBridge.lean holds for every integer start (word_affine_int, two_pow_mul_iter_add_one_int: 2^d (C^d x + 1) = 3^o (x + 1) + evenCharge w, with shortcutZ x = x/2 on evens and (3x+1)/2 on odds and parityWordZ its word), so on every integer cycle (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w (cycle_equation_int); in ℕ, for a positive cycle of length d >= 1, (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w and hence 2^d - 3^o divides the even-step charge of the word (cycle_equation, cycle_dvd). CONVERSELY (cycle_of_equation): a start whose parity word w satisfies (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w with 3^o <= 2^d returns after d steps. So an integer cycle with word w exists exactly when the rational x_0 = wordConst w / (2^d - 3^o) is an integer whose parity word is w -- and the second condition is automatic, by Lagarias 1990 (lagarias-1990-rational-cycles): every word is the parity vector of exactly one rational with odd denominator, periodic under the map. That last step is not in Lean; it is checked computationally on 190069 minimal certificates (lengths <= 26) and 654279 expanding survivors (lengths <= 24), every one of whose rational cycles follows its own word and returns. PREFIX BOUND (prefix_bound_of_min): if the orbit has not dropped below x by step j then (x + 1)(2^j - 3^(a_j)) <= evenCharge (prefix), so at a cycle minimum every contracting prefix caps x + 1 by the prefix's own rational cycle value evenCharge/(2^j - 3^(a_j)) -- the exact form of Terras's 'all sufficiently large members drop' and the reason a cycle word at its minimum is a minimal certificate up to the delta exceptions of J-collatz-walk-charge-constant: it contracts only at the end, so its length is A020914(p) = the binary length of 3^p, a classical constraint (the lengths where M_d != 0, the empty-window theorem, once more). WHAT THIS IS: the cycle side of the bridge made exact -- Collatz positive cycles are minimal certificates of Paper B carrying an integer rational cycle, and the open problem is which minimal certificates have 2^K - 3^p | evenCharge w with quotient at least 2 (the trivial cycle is OE with quotient 2). Not a kill, not a bound, not a halt theorem.

The sign flip on cycles is the sign of x, and Juggler's cycle words are the words of Collatz's negative cycles. The family of all minimal exponent-descent certificate words is prefix-free: if two certificates are in the prefix relation, they are equal. For every natural n and L>0 with J^L(n)=n, put w=itinerary(n,L), A=wordConst(w), and D=3^oddCount(w)-2^L as a signed integer. Then D is nonzero and the global 2-adic code H(n) equals the rational A/D in the 2-adic field. The least periods of H(n) under the 3n-1 map and of -H(n) under the 3n+1 map both equal the least Juggler period of n. H(n) is an embedded ordinary integer if and only if D divides A. If H(n)=z for an integer z, then for every d the ordinary integer 3n+1 shortcut returns -z after d steps if and only if Juggler returns n after d steps. Period preservation follows from branch monotonicity on equal-code fibers; global injectivity is not assumed. This proves no word divisibility for actual Juggler cycles and excludes no new cycle. There is a code H from all natural Juggler starts to the 2-adic integers, constructed from compatible finite Collatz residues with no termination hypothesis. Its residue modulo two has the parity of the start. It satisfies H(J(n))=minusStep(H(n)) and -H(J(n))=plusStep(-H(n)), where the steps are the 2-adic 3n-1 and 3n+1 shortcut maps, and H(J^d(n))=minusStep^d(H(n)) for every d. For all natural r,d, H(n)=-r modulo 2^d if and only if the actual length-d Juggler itinerary of n equals the length-d 3n+1 itinerary of r. Consequently these conditions select exactly the same subset of any finite source set; no equidistribution estimate is asserted. On each start with a ReachesOne witness, H agrees in the 2-adic field with the previously defined rational terminatingCode. This is classical parity coding, not ordinary-integer transport or universal termination. The local Lean proof is compiled; the ledger label awaits advisory coverage review.

For every natural n with a witness h that its actual Juggler orbit reaches 1, terminatingCode n h is a positive rational number independent of the chosen hitting time: whenever J^d(n)=1 it equals codeAt n d, the inverse 3n-1 branch composition along itinerary n d applied to endpoint 1. At every such depth d its reduced denominator divides 3^oddCount(itinerary n d). Its denominator is odd and its reduced numerator has the same parity as n. Writing H for this code on the terminating basin, H(J(n))=minusStep(H(n)) and -H(J(n))=plusStep(-H(n)), where minusStep and plusStep select their rational shortcut branch using reduced-numerator parity. This is a theorem on the terminating basin only; it does not define the full infinite 2-adic code or assert universal termination or ordinary-integer transport.

If x is odd and T(x) is even, then T^2(x) < n^2 if and only if x^3 < n^8. This is the mixed odd-cube / even-square cell. The OE fiber of a perfect cube is full or exactly alternating. For every a >= 1 and every n with (2a)^4 <= n and n^3 < ((2a)^3+1)^4, floor(n^(3/2)) = Nat.sqrt (n^3) is even (even_cube_fiber_full); for every odd n with (2a+1)^4 <= n and n^3 < ((2a+1)^3+1)^4, Nat.sqrt (n^3) + (n - (2a+1)^4)/2 is odd (odd_cube_fiber_alternating), so consecutive fiber elements have opposite image parity. Both rest on the integer identity Nat.sqrt ((k^4+t)^3) = k^6 + 3k^2 t/2 for 3t <= 4k (cube_fiber_sqrt_even, cube_fiber_sqrt_odd, by Nat.eq_sqrt and nlinarith from the two square inequalities: n^3 - q^2 = (3/4)k^4 t^2 + t^3 >= 0 and (q+1)^2 - n^3 = 2k^6 + 3k^2 t + 1 - (3/4)k^4 t^2 - t^3 > 0), together with cube_fiber_range: 3t <= 4k on the whole fiber, since 3t >= 4k+1 gives (3k^4+4k+1)^3 >= 27(k^3+1)^4. The range bound is attained (3 t_max = 4k for many k) and the identity itself outlives the fiber to t < 1.63k. Mechanism: n^(3/2) = k^6 (1 + t/k^4)^(3/2) = k^6 + (3/2)k^2 t + (3/8)t^2/k^2 - ..., and the quadratic term stays below one on the fiber; the parity of k^6 + (3/2)k^2 t is 0 for even k and 1 + t/2 for odd k. So m = 10^6 = 100^3 has a full fiber (67 of 67), and every odd cube splits exactly in half. Mathlib's three axioms only. Now Lemma 4.7 of Paper C, with the Lean names in its Appendix A. Remark 4.8 there identifies the window's centre arithmetically: alpha_m = 0 exactly means 27 m^2 = 8 k^3, whose integer solutions are m = (2e)^3 and k = 6e^2, so the even cubes are the exact-solution locus of a Mordell-type equation and the extreme fibers are its near-solutions, spaced asymptotically m^(1/3) apart with about (3/2) M^(2/3) below M. The two sides differ in strength: the full side contains this proved infinite family, while an empty fiber needs a near-miss plus a phase condition and whether there are infinitely many is open. A standing caution: the fiber of a cube is deterministic, not a coin.

Paper C Lemma 4.5 and Corollary 4.6, corrected 9 September 2026. For H_m ≥ 2, let α_m be the centered residue of (3/2)m^{2/3}, β_m = α_m(H_m−1), θ_m = {n_1^{3/2}/2}, and S(β,θ) the measure of s in [0,1] with {θ+βs+s²/3}<1/2. Then G_m/H_m = S(β_m,θ_m) + O(H_m^{−1/2} + (1+|β_m|)/H_m). The square-root error covers tangencies of the quadratic phase to a discontinuity; the old global O(1/H_m) claim is retired. The estimate is useful on restricted drift ranges, not for arbitrary β of order H. The θ-average of S is 1/2; extreme values 0 or 1 are possible precisely for β in [−5/6,1/6]; the β-integral of the phase measure of S=0 is 25/108. The archived code uses beta_hat = αH rather than the corrected lemma parameter α(H−1), so its fit statistics are observations of that convention. A weighted mean share 1/2 is sufficient for a fair production; conditional equidistribution of θ is sufficient under the required error control and is not necessary. No distribution law on a fate class is proved.

For each integer b>=3, the size-switched map S_b on integers b<=x<b^3 uses floor(sqrt(x^3)) for x<b^2 and floor(sqrt(x)) otherwise. Its cycles have the separated-image rank rotation, coprime branch counts and ceiling mechanical words; 3^o>2^L. S_b is not Juggler: a full cycle is a Juggler cycle iff every low state is odd and every high state even. This parity compatibility is not established, and the construction refutes only attempts to get no-cycle from the listed parity-relaxed properties alone. Consolidated in Paper A Section 3.10 and formalized in the seven Cubic modules. The cited declarations and supporting modules are compiled kernel proofs. Conditional cycle-order theorem. Let C be a primitive nontrivial Juggler cycle with minimum m>1, maximum M<m^3, length L and o odd states; set e=L-o. If c_0=m<...<c_(L-1) lists its states, the odd states are exactly those below m^2 and J(c_i)=c_((i+e) mod L). Hence gcd(L,o)=1 and the odd count in the first k steps from m is ceil(k o/L), for 0<=k<=L: the exact ceiling mechanical word. Proof separates odd/even states and images, uses injectivity to eliminate possible floor ties, then ranks the resulting cyclic permutation. A non-mechanical primitive cycle or one with gcd(L,o)>1 must instead have M>=m^3+1. The height hypothesis is essential to this argument; no unconditional Christoffel claim, no parity obstruction, no new period exclusion. Per-block law of the E-closure of a finite seed set S: on the dyadic block B the density equals sum over x in S and k >= 1 of |[x^(2^k), (x+1)^(2^k)) meet B| times 2^(-k) / |B|; verified to 0.5 percent (measured/predicted 0.996..1.005) on a 40-seed closure to 4e7. One landing burst from x contributes S/(x B) in (1/x, 2/x], S = x^(2^k); OE bursts land at clock offset log2(4/3), in other blocks (six blocks of the test carry OE density with zero E density), adding 8..32 percent where both land. Hence for a Lachesis basin, whose cycle states land in every block by J-lachesis-basin-every-block, the E-visible density on a block at scale y is at least (1/ln y) sum_{x in C} 1/x and the E+OE part at most (3/ln y) sum_{x in C} 1/x. Finance's Lean inv-sum form (cycleMin_finance_inv_sum: (3^o - 2^L) ln n <= 3^o sum 1/x) gives sum 1/x >= theta(L) ln n, and every state >= n gives sum 1/x <= L/n; floor > cap is the finance kill of the pair (true at n = 1e10, L = 780239). At n = 3.5e8, L = 780239: sum 1/x in [6.83e-5, 2.23e-3], so on the valid range y >= n^(2^(1 + u_max)) the block density is in [2.97e-7, 2.90e-5] at y = 1e100 and [9.89e-8, 9.68e-6] at y = 1e300, against the single-seed 2/n = 5.7e-9 (the first draft quoted 1e12 and 1e68, below the threshold for u_max >= 2; withdrawn). A cycle that barely survives finance has sum 1/x pinned, hence a basin whose contagion-visible density is pinned to within the constant factor. Not a halt theorem; the full basin's density is bounded above only by the free term.

Every nontrivial Juggler cycle itinerary based at n ≥ 2 is formally expanding. The arithmetic tier beneath J-depth-one-main-term, machine-checked. For every finite Juggler word w realized at n, J^{|w|}(n)^{2^{|w|}} ≤ n^{3^{#O(w)}}. If n ≥ 2 and 3^{#O(w)} < 2^{|w|}, then J^{|w|}(n) < n.
