Paper B section 7's composed map is the exponent walk of the Paper C collision work, and its linearisation criterion is a unit climb of that walk. With the notation of J-paper-b-defect-coefficient-chain, e_t = 3^(o_t) / 2^t exactly, where o_t is the number of odd letters up to t (`iter_eq_pow`). Taking log base 2 gives e_t = 2^(u_t) with u_t = o_t log2(3) - t, which is the walk J-live-set-ladder-factorisation splits at, J-damping-at-running-minimum is about, and J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum measures the climb of. Hence E = e_{t-1}/e_s = 2^(u_{t-1} - u_s), and E < 2 says exactly that the walk climbs by less than one unit between the defect at letter s and the wave at letter t. Two consequences. (i) The criterion is an exact integer inequality in the counts: with a odd and b even letters in the block, E < 2 iff 3^a < 2^(a+b+1) (`lt_two_iff_counts`), so it never needs a logarithm or a float. (ii) It does not see the order of the block, only the two counts (`iter_eq_of_counts`, `lt_two_congr`), which is immediate from the closed form and invisible in the product form; 45 count pairs cover every block arising in words of length up to 10. The supporting declarations are `oddCount`, `oddCount_cons_O` and `oddCount_cons_E`. Kernel-checked, axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. This is a reformulation and not an improvement: no bound moves, no density exponent changes, and the collision hypothesis is untouched. What it buys is that two screens developed separately are one test in one coordinate, and that E is literally the amplification factor A_k of J-dominant-defect-at-walk-minimum rather than an analogue of it.

All three conditions of Paper B section 7's screen are functions of the exponent walk u_t = o_t log2(3) - t alone, and two of them are unit conditions on it. With e_t = 2^(u_t) (J-paper-b-E-is-the-exponent-walk): the branch-run condition e_{s-1} < 2 is u_{s-1} < 1, an absolute height; the linearisation criterion E < 2 is u_{t-1} - u_s < 1, a climb; and the 9/4 stopping threshold e_{t-1} - e_s > 9/4 is 2^(u_{t-1}) - 2^(u_s) > 9/4. Checked over every word of length 3 to 11: 4204 letters with a blocked defect, no mismatch on any of the three. Non-contraction is a condition on the same walk (1 <= e_t, i.e. u_t >= 0), so the property defining a contractor and the property tripping the branch-run hypothesis are one constraint at thresholds 0 and 1. At step two the first forces the second: a prefix not contracted by its second letter must be OO, since E gives u_1 = -1 and OE gives u_2 = log2(3) - 2 < 0, so e_2 = 9/4 > 2, the branch-run threshold, because 3 > 2^(3/2) (`noncontracting_two_forces`, kernel-checked; `two_lt_nine_quarters` is the threshold comparison). Every one of the 140 contractors at depths 4 to 13 begins OO. The forcing does NOT extend along the word and is not claimed to: the walk is not monotone, and OOOEOOEE has a blocked defect at s = 5 with u_4 = 0.755, below the threshold. What is measured rather than proved is that from depth ten the hypothesis fires on every contractor anyway (12 of 12, 30 of 30, 85 of 85), and that the least peak a contractor's walk can have rises 1.170, 1.340, 1.510 with depth. Not a halt theorem, no bound moves, and no density exponent changes.

Paper B's non-contracting word count and Paper C's bad-word count are one function at two levels. N_d of Proposition 7.1 counts length-d words whose walk u_t = o_t log2(3) - t stays at or above 0; bad_word_count(L, d) counts those whose walk never reaches -L. Both are the same dynamic program over (steps, odd letters), written independently in paper_b_prefix_count and collision_large_sieve, and N_d = bad_word_count(0, d) exactly for d = 1 to 16 (1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19, 38, 64, 128, 226, 367, 734, 1295, 2114). The agreement is exact and not approximate although one bound is strict and the other is not, because u_t = 0 would need 3^(o_t) = 2^t, which forces o_t = t = 0 (`three_pow_eq_two_pow`, `iter_eq_one_iff`, kernel-checked): the walk is never back at its starting level after a letter, so on a non-empty word the two readings of non-contraction coincide (`one_le_iff_one_lt`). The O-rooting costs nothing either, since a word starting E has u_1 = -1. TRANSFER, and its limit. Because the counts coincide, Paper C's tools apply to Paper B's object; the sharpest, the Wiener-Hopf ladder factorisation at the walk minimum (J-live-set-ladder-factorisation), does specialise correctly and computes with exact identity error 0 at L = 0.05 and 0.25. But it degenerates there: at L -> 0 the argmin sits at the start with probability 1, so every word is a positive excursion and the split has no descending side. The transfer is valid and empty at Paper B's level, which is worth recording so it is not attempted twice. Not a bound and not an improvement to either paper.

Paper B's formal layer now contains an estimate, where before it contained none. THE STANDING POSITION, stated in the paper's own barrel JugglerParityPaper.lean: 'Building it does not corroborate the paper's analysis. Every declaration reachable from here is an identity, a constant, or a threshold; not one of them is an estimate.' That was accurate and is the reason 49 axiom-checked declarations do not amount to corroboration, against Paper A's 335 and Paper C's 409. WHAT IS NOW PROVED. PaperBChernoff, six theorems, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. one_sub_inv_lt_log gives the strict form 1 - x^(-1) < log x for x > 0, x not 1, from Real.add_one_lt_exp. klDiv_pos is strict Gibbs: 0 < D(p||q) whenever p is not q, which the fate layer's klDiv_nonneg does not give. theta_eq_exp_neg_klDiv bridges the manuscript's printed theta q = q^(-q)(1-q)^(q-1)/2 to exp(-D(q||1/2)) -- the same identity the 16 September re-audit checks numerically to 1e-12. theta_lt_one is then the estimate: theta q < 1 for every q in (0,1) other than 1/2, with theta_pos and theta_pow_lt in the form Theorem 6.1 uses. WHY IT IS THE RIGHT ONE. klDiv_nonneg gives only theta <= 1, and a bound of 1^(d-1)/2 is vacuous at every depth; the strictness is what makes Theorem 6.1's density bound DECAY rather than merely fail to grow. It is the single inequality the whole of Section 6 is aimed at. WIRED IN, not merely present: the module is imported by the Paper B barrel, the barrel's claim is corrected to say one declaration is now an estimate and the rest are not, and the manuscript cites theta_lt_one at the point where theta_d < 1 is used. WHAT IS STILL NOT FORMALISED, and the module says so in its own header: the exponential Markov step, the binomial generating function, and the passage from surviving words to natural density are all still written mathematics. This formalises the inequality those steps are aimed at, not the steps. So Paper B's analytic core remains unformalised and the barrel still says the trust-boundary discussion governs. No bound moves.

The FD step is formalised as an inference, and Theorem 6.1 stays conditional -- which is what the manuscript already says and what the formalisation must not quietly improve on. WHAT FD IS. A HYPOTHESIS, not a result: 'Hypothesis FD. For every fixed d >= 1 and every odd-rooted word w of length d, #{n <= N : word_d(n) = w} = 2^(-d) N + o_w(N). No common error rate in d is assumed.' Theorem 6.1 is headed 'conditional density-one certificate theorem' and the manuscript's own table lists the density-one certificates as conditional on FD. So the task was never to prove the step; it was to state the hypothesis and derive the conclusion. WHAT IS PROVED. PaperBDensity, three theorems, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. density_of_finite_union: if each of finitely many classes has density r, their union has density card * r. That is the entire content of 'FD and a finite sum over surviving words show that the natural density is their number divided by 2^d' -- FD gives r = 2^(-d) for one class and finite additivity does the rest, which is exactly why the hypothesis is needed at each fixed d separately and why no uniformity in d is asserted. tendsto_zero_of_eventually_le: a nonnegative quantity eventually below c d for every d, with c d -> 0, tends to zero -- the 'letting d -> infinity proves the assertion' at the end of the proof. exceptional_density_zero combines them in the shape Theorem 6.1 uses. THE CHAIN NOW READS, formally: the bad words number at most 2^n theta q ^ n (PaperBMarkov.chernoff_density), theta q < 1 (PaperBChernoff.theta_lt_one), at the optimal tilt the two agree exactly (PaperBMarkov.tilt_gives_theta), and a density dominated at every depth by a vanishing bound is zero (PaperBDensity). WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVED, and the module header says so: Hypothesis FD itself, which is open; and that the bad set at depth d IS a finite union of word classes, which is the combinatorial reading of word_d and stays written mathematics. Theorem 6.1 is not formalised. Its inference from FD is. Paper B's barrel now names four modules beyond identities and thresholds and still says the analytic core -- Theorem 4.11, Theorem 5.4, Appendices A to C -- is unformalised. No bound moves.

Paper B Theorems 5.2-5.4, assembly half. Let certifiedWords d be the length-d parity words with a contracting prefix. (i) Their counts are 13, 28, 56, 115 at d = 4, 5, 6, 7, so the certificate densities are 13/16, 7/8, 7/8, 115/128; depth six adds nothing. (ii) At depth five the cylinders of E, OE, OOEE, OOOEE, OOEOE have sizes 16, 8, 2, 1, 1, are pairwise disjoint, and their union is exactly certifiedWords 5 (five_cylinders_cover, five_cylinders_card_sum) — so the printed 1/2+1/4+1/16+1/32+1/32 = 7/8 is the cylinder arithmetic and not a free-standing rational identity (printed_measures_are_counts). (iii) For every N the starts in {1,...,N} certified by depth five number classCount E N + classCount OE N + classCount OOEE N + classCount OOOEE N + classCount OOEOE N (certifiedCount_five_eq), via sum_classCount_cylinder and itinerary_take. (iv) 5/6 < 23/24 < 47/48 < 127/128 < 1 with N^e <= N^f for e <= f and N >= 1, which is the absorption the proofs assume. (v) five_step_error_assembly: five class counts within errors of their main terms add to 7N/8 within the sum of the errors. Every analytic count is a hypothesis: Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 4.6, 4.10, 4.12 are not proved here or anywhere in the repository, so this bounds no exponential sum and is not a density theorem or a termination statement.

Paper B Lemma 5.1 extends past its printed length five, decidably. No word of length six is a minimal certificate (no_minimal_certificate_six), which is why the certificate density is still 7/8 at depth six. Exactly three words of length seven are: OOEOOEE, OOOEOEE, OOOOEEE (minimal_certificates_seven). The depth-seven certificate density is therefore 115/128 = 7/8 + 3/128 (certifiedWordCount_seven, seven_step_density, seven_step_gain). The manuscript states nothing about lengths six or seven. This is combinatorics only: each of the three new words would need its own mixed-mode exponential-sum estimate before 115/128 became a density for the Juggler map rather than a count of words.

The jumps of Paper B's meander prefactor are the survivor sequence itself. Write N_d for the count of length-d parity words no prefix of which contracts, theta = beta^(-beta)(1-beta)^(beta-1)/2 for its exponential rate, and psi for the measured prefactor of J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic, a function of frac(d*beta) with beta = log2/log3. Then psi is discontinuous exactly on the rotation orbit, and its jump at frac(n*beta), left limit minus right limit, is a_n = a_1 * N_n / (2*theta)^(n-1) for every n >= 1; the jump at x = 0 is a_0 = 2*theta*a_1. There is exactly one constant in the statement, a_1, the amplitude at frac(beta), and it is CLOSED FORM: a_1 = 1/(2 theta sqrt(2 pi beta (1-beta))) = 0.427956804 (J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form). Values of 0.42623 and 0.426289 were recorded here earlier the same day as measurements and are withdrawn; both were about 0.4 percent low, and why is recorded with the closed form. Every other quantity is an exact integer over a power. WHY. psi(x) depends on x only through the barrier word read backwards from x, and crossing one point of the orbit transposes two adjacent letters, odd-then-even becoming even-then-odd, leaving the odd count and hence the barrier unchanged. The two histories differ by exactly the survivors standing on the barrier at the moment of the swap -- a single point mass -- which an odd letter fixes, so the difference is the survivor problem run again from one walker. That finite step is Lean-verified in PaperBJumpTransposition; the asymptotics that turn it into a statement about psi are measured, not proved. VERIFIED TWICE. A transfer-operator propagation using no measured data reproduces the identity to 2.3e-14 over n <= 3000. Independently, a one-parameter model of psi on d in [2e5,1e6] -- its jumps plus the linear rise periodicity demands -- gives a_1 = 0.42629, stable to 5e-4 across d-subranges, to 1e-4 as the number of modelled jumps runs from 1e4 to 1e6, and to between 0.03 and 0.35 percent against a freely fitted head amplitude for splits of the spectrum at n >= 5; the tightest split, a head of three jumps, reads 1.4 percent high. CONSEQUENCES. psi is of bounded variation. a_n is asymptotically 2*theta*a_1*psi(frac(n*beta))*n^(-3/2), so the jump of psi at the n-th orbit point is psi at that same point to a universal constant and a power. The barrier-index constants C_j = 2*a_1*theta^(1-j)*N_n/2^n, for any n with ceil(n*beta) = j, are now available at every j; the previous branch reached about j = 25 and no fit reaches further, because the column a fine jump contributes to any design collapses toward zero. WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. The jumps are not the function: jumps plus the linear rise leave a residual of 1.35e-02 against a level-fit noise floor of 4.4e-03, 89 percent of whose variance is a reproducible function of the coordinate and which does not shrink with d.

Transposing two adjacent barrier letters costs exactly the mass on the barrier. Grade the surviving parity words of a given length by their surplus h above the barrier. A barrier letter that does not rise acts by stepFlat v h = v h + v (h-1) and kills nothing; one that rises acts by stepRise v h = v (h+1) + v h and loses exactly v 0, the survivors sitting on the barrier. Then stepRise (stepFlat v) and stepFlat (stepRise v) agree at every height except zero and differ at zero by exactly v 0 (stepRise_stepFlat_eq_add_barrierMass). Since every later letter acts linearly (run_add), the whole difference between the two transposed histories is the history of a single point mass at the barrier (run_stepRise_stepFlat), and an odd letter fixes that point mass (stepRise_barrierMass). At the level of totals, a flat letter doubles below a window the profile has not reached (total_stepFlat_eq_two_mul) and a rising letter doubles less the barrier mass (total_stepRise_add_barrierMass). Everything is over the natural numbers; no real number appears in any statement, and the two orders are comparable with one dominating the other (run_stepFlat_stepRise_le). This is the finite core under J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence: it is why a discontinuity of the meander prefactor is not a new quantity but the survivor problem restarted from one walker. It does not say that the prefactor exists, that the d^(-3/2) is right, or that the propagated difference converges to the jump.

The 1/rho law for the jump amplitudes is the empty-window theorem, and carries nothing else. This cluster recorded that the ratio of consecutive jump amplitudes across a Sturmian zero -- an n with ceil(n*beta) = ceil((n-1)*beta) -- is exactly 1/rho = 1.0352968376, measured first to 7.6e-4 by a level fit and then to 2.1e-12 by a deterministic propagation. The law is exact and it is trivial. First, rho and theta are the same number, 0.96590655323343772361, under two names [CORRECTED 2026-09-20: this row recorded 0.9659065532355213, wrong from the twelfth significant digit, 2.08e-12 above the true value. The laboratory CODE was never wrong -- paper_b_prefix_count.chernoff_rate() returns 0.9659065532334377 and plain double precision gives 0.9659065532334378, so this was a transcription into prose and not a computation. The provenance of the wrong digits is unknown: they are not the double-precision value and not 1/(1.0352968376), which gives 0.9659065532530513. The quoted 1/rho = 1.0352968376 is a correct rounding of 1.0352968376210226 and stands. Note the row also quotes an agreement of 2.1e-12 for this law, the same magnitude as the error just removed; the two are not known to be related and the agreement was not re-derived here], which is what made the ratio look like an independent constant. Second, a Sturmian zero is an even barrier letter, an even letter kills nothing and doubles the survivor count exactly, and dividing by the normalisation 2*theta leaves 1/theta. The doubling is the statement of PaperBCertificateLengths that no minimal certificate exists at a length where no power of three lies in the window, seen from the amplitude side, and it is one line in Lean (PaperBJumpTransposition.total_stepFlat_eq_two_mul). The reading is retracted as a finding and kept as an identity. What survives is the direction it pointed: the content of the spectrum is entirely in the odd letters, which is what led to the closed form of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence.

THE EMPTY-WINDOW THEOREM IS NOT A LEVEL-ZERO STATEMENT, and this is the sixth thing it controls -- the one nobody had connected. Paper B's version says a minimal certificate of length L exists only when a power of three lies in [2^(L-1), 2^L), so at a length where none does the survivor set is a full cylinder. The argument never uses the level. A word whose walk first reaches <= -L at step d must end in E, since an odd last letter would need 3^(o+1) <= 2^(d-L) while the length-(d-1) prefix gives 3^o > 2^(d-1-L), i.e. 3 < 2 -- that is minimalCert_concat_even verbatim with the barrier moved. So the odd count is pinned in the SHIFTED window 2^(d-1-L) < 3^o <= 2^(d-L), and when no power of three lies there the L-bad set is a full cylinder too: B_d(L) = B_(d-1)(L) x {E,O}. VERIFIED by brute force over all 2^d words for d <= 15 at L = 0.5, 1.2486 and 3.0: the shifted-window prediction agrees with the enumerated set identity at every depth at every level, with no mismatch. At L = 0 the strict form disagrees with the laboratory's CertWindow at d = 1 and nowhere else, which is the left-endpoint convention (CertWindow takes 2^(L-1) <= 3^o) and not a discrepancy. WHY IT WAS MISSED. Paper B runs at L = 0 and Paper C runs entirely at L > 0. The laboratory carries a four-row dictionary between them -- J-paper-b-screen-is-a-walk-condition, J-paper-b-count-is-the-level-zero-bad-count, J-paper-c-exponent-is-paper-b-rate-at-level-zero, J-the-two-tilts-are-one-measure, all EXACT - HUMAN PROOF -- and it had only ever been driven from Paper C down to Paper B, where the transfer was recorded as valid and empty. The one Paper B word-level theorem never pushed the other way is the one that does not go empty. CONSEQUENCE ALREADY ON THE RECORD: J-bad-set-spectrum-cannot-win quotes the Wiener norm at d = 8, 12, 16, 20 for L = 1.249, and d = 12 and d = 20 are free lengths, so those two values are copies of d = 11 and d = 19. That row now carries the caution; its verdict is unaffected. NOW IN LEAN, necessity half, word level: Problems.Juggler.PaperBLevelWindow carries the level as a real scale c = 2^Lambda, so fractional levels are in range and not only integer ones. no_minimalCertAt_of_window_empty: when no power of three lies in the shifted window at L, no word of length L is a minimal certificate at level c. All kernel, on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Paper B is derived from it at c = 1 rather than asserted to be its special case (isMinimalCertificateAt_one_iff, no_minimalCert_of_window_empty_of_level). THREE QUALIFICATIONS, each found by an adversarial pass over the module rather than volunteered. (1) CONVENTION. The Lean reaches the barrier STRICTLY, following Paper B; Paper C's code reaches it NON-STRICTLY. CORRECTED 2026-09-19, and the first version of this qualification was wrong twice. The two coincide exactly when 3^o * 2^Lambda is never a power of two, i.e. when Lambda avoids the LATTICE {t - o log2 3}, and that is now a theorem rather than prose: exponentGapAt_agrees_iff. FIRST ERROR: I wrote that the lattice is the integers. It is not. o = 0 gives the integers; o >= 1 gives IRRATIONAL levels, which are non-integer. At Lambda = 2 - log2 3 = 0.415, c = 4/3, the certificate sets differ at seven of the first ten lengths. What makes 0.5 and 1.2486 safe is that they are RATIONAL and non-integer, since 3^a = 2^b forces a = b = 0 -- rationality, not non-integrality, and the two happen to coincide there. SECOND ERROR: I wrote that the disagreement sits at floor(Lambda) and floor(Lambda)+1. That is the o = 0 case written in the wrong variable. On a lattice point 3^o c = 2^t the FREE lengths differ at exactly t and t+1: measured, c = 8 (o=0, t=3) moves 3 and 4, and c = 4/3 (o=1, t=2) moves 2 and 3. Both errors were prose that a Lean statement forced me to make precise, which is the argument for stating conventions as theorems. Guarded in test_the_conventions_part_on_a_lattice, exact rational arithmetic. Witness at Lambda = 3: strict gives EEEE at length four and nothing at three, non-strict gives EEE at three and nothing at four. So the enumeration in test_empty_window_levels.py corroborates the module at its levels 0.5 and 1.2486 and NOT at its level 3.0, which checks the mirror statement. (2) INTEGER LEVELS ARE RE-INDEXINGS: certWindowAt_two_iff shows the window at c = 2 is Paper B's window at length L - 1, so whole-number levels prove nothing new and the content is entirely at fractional levels. A worked instance at such a level is certWindowAt_twelve_empty_at_paperC_level, covering every level between log2 2.37 = 1.2450 and log2 2.38 = 1.2511. (3) was ONLY NECESSITY and is now CLOSED. The realisation half is formalised: blockWordAt_isMinimalCertificateAt shows O^o E^(L-o) first passes the barrier at level c when the shifted window holds a power of three, so minimalCertAt_exists_iff is Paper B's minimalCert_exists_iff at every level. Both prefix branches survive the shift for their own reasons: an all-odd prefix by 3^k c >= 3^k >= 2^k, which is where 1 <= c is used, and a prefix O^o E^j by the window's lower bound, which already carries the c. CONSEQUENCE, and the reason it was worth doing: aliveWordsAt_succ_iff_window_empty makes the cylinder identity an IF AND ONLY IF. A length is a full cylinder extension exactly when its shifted window is empty, so a frozen statistic is an exact diagnostic of a free length rather than a one-way hint. The converse uses aliveAt_disjoint_certsAt, that alive and first-passing are exclusive. The enumeration in test_empty_window_levels.py already checked both directions -- it asserts (not window) == cylinder with no mismatch -- so the Lean and the test now agree in shape as well as in verdict. THE CYLINDER IDENTITY AT LEVEL c IS NOW FORMALISED, which qualification (3) previously also carried: aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty says the alive set at a free length is the previous one times the full alphabet, and sum_aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty that every additive functional of it factorises over the two extensions, for any AddCommMonoid and any f, with card_aliveWordsAt_succ_of_window_empty the counting case. All kernel. That is what downstream consumers use: a frozen statistic at a depth is that theorem at f equal to the statistic. The Finsets are classical rather than decidable because the predicate is real-valued, which is the price of carrying the level and is the same price Paper C's own LBad already pays. AND IT DOES NOT HELP PAPER C'S EXPONENT, checked rather than assumed. The free lengths have density 1 - 1/log2 3 = 0.369 at every level, so a third of all depths carry no first-passage mass. The mass does not thin, it piles onto the admissible lengths: over d = 10..18 the tail decays at 0.73 per length and 0.60 per admissible length at level zero, 0.71 and 0.58 at level 1.2486. The per-length figure is what an exponential bound in d uses and is unchanged by knowing which lengths are free. Worth a constant, not an exponent. It bears on neither no-cycle nor termination. CLOSED FORM ADDED: certWindowAt_iff_floor shows that at level Lambda >= 0 and length L >= 1, the shifted window holds odd count o exactly when floor(o log2 3 + Lambda) = L - 1. So the carrying lengths at level Lambda are the INHOMOGENEOUS Beatty sequence of slope log2 3 and intercept Lambda -- A020914 with an offset. The level moves the intercept and nothing else, which is why it moves WHICH lengths are free without moving how many: the free density is 1 - 1/log2 3 at every level, since that depends on the slope alone. At Lambda = 0 this is minimalCert_exists_iff_natLog, where Nat.log 2 (3^o) = floor(o log2 3) and no real number is needed. Kernel.

PROVED IN LEAN, at every level: above the bottom edge, no two adjacent lengths are both free. carrying_in_adjacent_pair says that for floor(Lambda) + 1 <= L, at least one of L and L+1 carries a window at level 2^Lambda. MECHANISM. The carrying lengths are floor(o log2 3 + Lambda) + 1 (certWindowAt_iff_floor). Since 1 < log2 3 < 2, one step moves that floor by 1 or 2 (floor_step_bounds), so the carrying lengths never skip two integers in a row. The proof takes the least o whose boundary value reaches L-1: if it is 0 the bottom-edge hypothesis pins it at L-1 exactly, and otherwise its predecessor fell short, so one step of size at most 2 lands on L-1 or L. WHAT IT SAYS ABOUT THE CYLINDER IDENTITY, which is the point: not_cylinder_twice. The alive set is never a full cylinder extension at two consecutive lengths, so the alive count never doubles twice running and a frozen statistic is always followed by a moving one. That bounds how much the free lengths can cluster, which nothing in the laboratory had said. OVERCLAIM CORRECTED 2026-09-19, the same day: an earlier version of this row called it the first constraint of its kind on the survivor growth. At level zero it is not new at all. The gaps of A020914 being 1 or 2 is the defining property of A022921, in OEIS since 23 October 2009 and elementary. What is not in the literature, as far as this laboratory can see, is the statement at every LEVEL Lambda -- the inhomogeneous case, where the Beatty sequence carries an intercept -- and the reading of it on the cylinder identity as not_cylinder_twice. The level-zero fact is A022921 and the row should not have implied otherwise. See J-certificate-length-is-the-dropping-time. THE BOTTOM EDGE IS A GENUINE EXCEPTION and the first form of the claim did not carry it: at Lambda = 3 the lengths 1, 2 and 3 are all free because the carrying sequence starts at 4. That is an artefact of where the sequence begins rather than a statement about the slope, and the hypothesis excludes exactly it -- the first carrying length is floor(Lambda) + 1 on the nose, so the hypothesis says the sequence has started. A computational sweep found the exception before it was written anywhere. All kernel, on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. It bears on neither no-cycle nor termination: it constrains the shape of the free set and says nothing about any orbit.

Theorem 6.1's Chernoff chain is now formal end to end, from the word count to a bound that decays. PaperBMarkov, four theorems, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], joining PaperBChernoff from earlier the same day. STATED COMBINATORIALLY, which is both closer to the manuscript and far cheaper: Paper B counts words of length d by their number of odd letters and divides by 2^d, so the statements are about binomial coefficients and finite sums rather than about a probability space. sum_choose_mul_pow is the binomial generating function, sum over k in range(n+1) of C(n,k) x^k = (1+x)^n, from Commute.add_pow. chernoff_tail is the exponential Markov step: for t > 0, the sum of C(n,k) over k >= a is at most exp(-t a) (1 + exp t)^n, proved by charging every word with at least a odd letters the factor 1 <= exp(t(k-a)), extending the sum to the full range and applying the generating function. chernoff_density is the same divided by 2^n, which is the manuscript's form. THE OPTIMISATION IS AN IDENTITY, NOT A DIFFERENTIATION. tilt_gives_theta: at t = log(q/(1-q)) and a = q n the right-hand side equals theta q ^ n exactly. The manuscript optimises t by differentiating; in Lean it is an equality between two closed forms, verified numerically to 1e-15 at q = 0.55, BETA, 0.75 and n = 1, 5, 20. That theorem is what joins this module to PaperBChernoff.theta_lt_one, so the chain reads: word count <= theta q ^ n, and theta q < 1. WHAT IS STILL WRITTEN MATHEMATICS, and both module headers say so: the passage from these word counts to the natural density of N minus C_d -- the FD step and the finite sum over surviving words -- and the identification of the surviving words as a binomial count in the first place. So Theorem 6.1 is not formalised; its Chernoff engine is. THE BARREL'S CLAIM IS NOW TWICE CORRECTED. It read 'not one of them is an estimate' until 16 September; it now names two modules that are, and still says the analytic core is unformalised and the trust-boundary discussion governs. Paper B's formal layer stands at 49 identities, constants and thresholds plus ten theorems of estimate, against Paper A's 335 and Paper C's 409 axiom-checked declarations. No bound moves.

The two papers' large-deviation exponents are one rate function of one walk, evaluated at the level each needs. The bad-word condition at depth d = CL is u_d > -L, so the odd fraction must exceed p(C) = (1 - 1/C)/log2(3), and Paper C's e(C) is C KL(p(C) || 1/2)/log 2. Paper B sits at L = 0, which is C to infinity, where p(C) tends to 1/log2(3) = BETA = log2/log3, the threshold its own Hoeffding step uses. So e(C)/C converges to Paper B's rate in bits, 0.050044473: measured gaps 4.8e-3 at C = 100, 4.9e-4 at 1000, 4.9e-5 at 10000, 4.9e-6 at 100000, i.e. like 1/C. With J-paper-b-count-is-the-level-zero-bad-count this closes the correspondence: the conditions, the counts and now the exponents are the same objects at two levels. COROLLARY, and it corrects a reading recorded earlier the same day. Paper B's Hoeffding exponent is nearly sharp, not lossy: chernoff_rate() returns the minimised MGF rho, so the sharp rate is -log(rho), which equals kl_bernoulli(BETA) = 0.034688185 exactly, against HOEFFDING_C = 0.034285201 -- a slack of 1.0118 per letter, the module's own 'right to one part in eighty'. Over 24 letters that contributes 1.01x of a total loss of 25.7x. Essentially all of the loss is the polynomial d^(-3/2) that meander_constant names, whose constant converges to about 10.8. An earlier entry described the loss as splitting between the endpoint-versus-path gap and Hoeffding's own constant, which is true of those two ratios but invites the wrong conclusion: the exponent contributes essentially nothing. Not a bound and not an improvement to either paper. IN LEAN. The corollary is the load-bearing part and is now machine-checked: `neg_logRho_eq_klHalf` proves -logRho b = klHalf b for EVERY real b, with no positivity hypothesis, because both sides are the same arrangement of b log b, (1-b) log(1-b) and log 2. That is the bridge -- Paper B's rate was in PaperBSlopeRate and Paper C's relative entropy was already in FateChernoff as klHalf, proved for the Chernoff count, and neither layer knew about the other. The level-zero limits follow: `pC_tendsto_beta` sends Paper C's threshold (1 - 1/C)*beta to beta, and `eOverC_tendsto` sends e(C)/C to klHalf beta / log 2, which is 0.050044473. All kernel-clean. NOT formalised: the counting statements either side of the dictionary.

Paper B's zero-drift tilt and Paper C's theta_C are one change of measure in two coordinate systems, and Paper B is the level-zero member. Paper C picks theta_C so the unconditioned tilted mean endpoint sits at the barrier -L; at L = 0, i.e. C to infinity, that is zero drift, which is the tilt meander_constant works under and the minimiser of the MGF chernoff_rate computes. The measures agree outright: the MGF minimiser gives tilted P(O) = 0.630929753 and p_C converges to BETA = 1/log2(3) = 0.630929754, with the tilted walk drift measured at -1.1e-9. The tilt PARAMETERS do not agree and should not, because the papers tilt by different statistics -- Paper C by the odd count o, Paper B by the walk value in nats. On words of fixed length t, e^{theta sum X} = e^{theta(o log 3 - t log 2)} = const(t) e^{(theta log 3) o}, so the coordinates differ by exactly log 3: theta_C = theta* log 3, verified to machine precision (0.536207535 against 0.488077132 times 1.098612289). Closed forms: theta* = log(log 2 / log(3/2))/log 3 and theta_C = log(log 2 / log(3/2)) = log(BETA/(1 - BETA)). This is the fourth and last level of the correspondence, after the conditions (J-paper-b-screen-is-a-walk-condition), the counts (J-paper-b-count-is-the-level-zero-bad-count) and the exponents (J-paper-c-exponent-is-paper-b-rate-at-level-zero): condition, count, exponent and measure are the same objects at two levels of one walk. Nothing here is a bound, and no result in either paper changes. IN LEAN. `beta_odds` proves beta/(1-beta) = log 2 / log(3/2), the identity behind both closed forms, and `lamStar_beta_closed` reads off Paper C's tilt as log(log 2 / log(3/2)). The coordinate change is `tilt_coordinate_change`: on words of length t with o odd letters the walk value is o log 3 - t log 2, so tilting by it with parameter theta equals tilting by the odd count alone with parameter theta * log 3, times a factor depending only on t -- which is why the parameters differ by exactly log 3 and should, recorded as `thetaStar_mul_log_three`. All kernel-clean. What is NOT formalised is that these tilts are the ones the two papers' arguments actually select; that is the content of the rows they come from, not of this dictionary.

d/ds log rho(s) = -log(s/(1-s)): the tilt that makes the walk drift-free is also the sensitivity of the rate to the barrier's slope. PROOF. Against a barrier of slope s the Chernoff rate is the Legendre transform of a fair coin, log rho(s) = -s log s + (s-1) log(1-s) - log 2. Differentiating, -log s - 1 + log(1-s) + (s-1) * (-1/(1-s)) = -log(s/(1-s)), the -1 cancelling against the last term. The second derivative is -1/(s(1-s)). CONSEQUENCE. lamStar = log(BETA/(1-BETA)) = 0.536207535136 already carried two roles that looked unrelated: the exponential tilt of the surviving profile, and through r* = (1-BETA)/BETA = e^(-lamStar) the base of its tail. This is a third that unifies them -- it is the derivative of the rate in the barrier slope -- and it is what converts a barrier error |BETA - p/q| into a rate error. MEASURED. Rational barriers realise it: the difference quotient between the 12/19 and 41/65 barriers agrees with -barrier_tilt at the midpoint slope to 1e-6, and the second-order term is confirmed too -- at 64/101, where |s - BETA| = 2.7e-3, the two-term Taylor matches the measured rate to 4e-5 relative. ONE FUNCTION, TWO DERIVATIVES. Write G(lam, s) = -lam s + log((1+e^lam)/2), so that log rho(s) = min_lam G. Stationarity in lam is the DOUBLE ROOT of J-rho-has-a-tail-variable-variational-formula: the minimiser is lamStar(s) and its exponential e^(-lamStar) = (1-s)/s is the tail base r*. The envelope in s is this row: d/ds min_lam G = -lamStar, and it is the vanishing lam-derivative that makes the envelope step legal. The double root and the slope derivative were recorded as separate facts; they are the two partial derivatives of G at one point. Verified at s = 0.579, BETA, 0.66: the minimiser matches barrier_tilt to 1e-7, e^(-lam) matches (1-s)/s to 1e-7, and the minimum matches log chernoff_rate_at to 1e-14. IN LEAN. `logRho_deriv` is this row and is kernel-clean; `chernoffExp_lam_deriv` is the vanishing lam-derivative that makes the envelope step legal rather than merely plausible; `chernoffExp_at_lamStar` is the identity that the exponent at the tilt IS the rate, at every slope; and `log_rho_eq` puts the closed form of PaperBTilt.rho into logs, over the definitions `logRho` and `chernoffExp`. All four print [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and nothing else. What is NOT in Lean is the measured content -- that a rational barrier of slope p/q really decays at rho(p/q) -- which stays in J-barrier-rate-is-the-chernoff-rate-at-its-slope as a measurement. Machinery: chernoff_exponent, barrier_tilt, chernoff_rate_at.

The Sturmian driving costs nothing in the Yaglom exponent and four percent in the constant, so q -> infinity is benign. THE QUESTION. For a RATIONAL barrier p/q the period map is autonomous, so the driven problem reduces to the undriven one at each q and Ocafrain's 1/t (J-yaglom-rate-is-one-over-d) applies there. The irrational Sturmian barrier is the limit q -> infinity, and that passage is benign only if the constant c in TV(pi_d, Pi_(phi_d)) ~ c/d stays bounded as q grows. MEASURED, at cap 1600 and d up to 32000, over six convergents of beta = log2/log3 spanning three orders of magnitude in the denominator. Exponents: -0.9987 (12/19), -1.0231 (41/65), -0.9961 (53/84), -1.0040 (306/485), -1.0055 (665/1054), -1.0055 (15601/24727). Constants at d = 4000: 20.2174, 20.6369, 20.0926, 20.1271, 20.1156, 20.1158. The constant does not merely stay bounded -- it CONVERGES, the last two convergents agreeing to six digits. THE RESIDUAL SCATTER IS PHASE, NOT DENOMINATOR: sweeping a full period at fixed q = 485 moves c between 19.7211 and 20.5154, a spread of 3.96 percent, which is the same size as the 19.89 to 20.64 range across q. THE CONSTANT BELONGS TO THE BARRIER, NOT THE START, which is what has to be true for it to cancel and leave d^-2 memory loss: delta_0 and delta_5 agree at once (19.68, 19.65 at d = 32000) and delta_20, delta_60 climb to the same value once d >> m^2. IT IS NOT HOMOGENISATION. Averaging the word over the diffusive scale would need d >> q^2, which at q = 24727 means d >> 6e8; the q = 1054 and q = 24727 rows already agree at d = 4000. What makes the family uniform is that EVERY barrier in it, rational or irrational, is a bounded perturbation of the SAME straight line: |ceil(t*s) - t*s| < 1 for every t and every s, with no constant depending on either. That is far inside the g_n = o(c_n) regime Denisov, Sakhanenko and Wachtel (arXiv:1801.04136) assume for moving boundaries. A CORRECTED MEASUREMENT. At cap 400 the constant appears to slide 19.6 -> 17.3 over d = 2000..32000 with exponent -1.0886; that drift is the truncation, not the dynamics. The truncated operator's gap is of order cap^-2, so the free d^-1 law holds only while d << cap^2. Raising the cap to 800 gives -1.0182 and to 1600 gives -1.0040 with a flat constant. Machinery: yaglom_constant. No bound moves and no fate is excluded; what moves is the record of what the Sturmian driving costs, from unknown to four percent of a constant. The uniformity comes from ceiling arithmetic and nothing deeper: ceil_sub_self_lt_one bounds a ceiling's distance from its argument, barrier_diff_lt carries that to two barriers at different slopes, barrier_diff_le_one_of_close turns closeness into a difference of at most one ceiling step, and rise_mem_zero_one confines each rise to {0,1}.

The never-contracting word count N_d of the rate-free density-one reduction (rows J-equidistribution-implies-density-one, J-rate-free-density-one) is identified with a binomial tail and provably decays, closing the link PaperBMarkov's header listed as written mathematics. (i) count_oddCount_ge: length-d parity words with at least a odd letters number exactly sum_{k=a}^{d} C(d,k), by Pascal induction on d. (ii) oddCount_ge_of_mem_neverNeg: every survivor w of length d has oddCount w >= ceil(d beta) with beta = log2/log3 (neverNeg_endpoint plus log monotonicity). (iii) neverNegCount_div_pow_le_theta: N_d/2^d <= theta(beta)^d, the tilt taken at the endpoint q = beta itself (the published proof tilts at the midpoint; the upper bound needs no threshold admissibility). (iv) neverNegCount_div_pow_tendsto_zero: N_d/2^d -> 0, since theta(beta) < 1 (PaperBChernoff.theta_lt_one, beta != 1/2 via 2^8 > 3^5). (v) neverCertified_density_zero: under FairClasses (the manuscript's Hypothesis FD: per-class #w(N) = 2^{-d} N + o(N) at each fixed depth), the never-certified starts in {1,...,N} have natural density zero -- the conditional Theorem 6.1 assembled end-to-end, with RateFreeDensity.uncertifiedCount_eq_sum supplying the union step that J-fd-step-is-formal-and-theorem-six-one-stays-conditional recorded as written mathematics, and PaperBDensity.exceptional_density_zero supplying the limit order N -> infinity before d -> infinity. (vi) Kernel-computed values: N_1..N_8 = 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 19; neverNegWords_five lists the depth-5 survivors OOOOO, OOOOE, OOOEO, OOEOO, the word count behind Corollary 6.4's 7/8 (uncertified_fraction_depth_five: 1 - 4/32 = 7/8); N_6 = 8 is the ledger's 'all eight children survive'. All kernel-trusted (decide +kernel for the values; no native_decide). What stays open is FD itself, the active conjecture juggler_tower_rate_free_equidistribution; the exact rate -log rho = 0.034688 (one part in eighty sharper than this endpoint-only Hoeffding majorant) is not formalised. Not a halt theorem; no unconditional density claim. The small-depth values are kernel-decided one per theorem: neverNegCount_one = 1, neverNegCount_two = 1, neverNegCount_three = 2, neverNegCount_four = 3, neverNegCount_five = 4, neverNegCount_six = 8, neverNegCount_seven = 13 and neverNegCount_eight = 19, each by decide +kernel rather than by a shared table.

The tail variable's minimum is Lean-verified and Paper B's open-questions section is brought up to it. THE LEAN. PaperBTailSpectrum proves what J-tail-spectral-gap-closes-like-one-over-root-q reads its numerics against, for h s z = log(1+z) - log 2 - (1-s) log z: the derivative is 1/(1+z) - (1-s)/z (h_hasDerivAt); it vanishes at the tail root (1-s)/s (h_deriv_eq_zero_at_tailRoot), which is why r* is the only positive root of the characteristic equation and why it is DOUBLE rather than simple; the second derivative there is s^3/(1-s) (h_secondDeriv_at_tailRoot) and is positive (h_secondDeriv_pos), which is the constant in the measured gap law |z - r*| ~ sqrt(4 pi k/(q h''(r*))); and the minimum VALUE is H(s) - log 2 (h_at_tailRoot), the binary entropy less log 2, which is log rho. That last identity is the same one PaperBAmplitudeCocycle.cocycle_average_eq reaches from the amplitude side, so the tail spectrum and the cocycle's single-valuedness are one statement approached from two directions. Seven theorems, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. Consolidates with PaperBSturmianBarrier and PaperBAmplitudeCocycle, both added the same day. WHAT IS NOT IN LEAN: the complex boundary-layer roots are located numerically, and nothing formal asserts the profile HAS this tail. THE MANUSCRIPT. Paper B's 'what is open, and what is excluded' passage is updated. The unproved link is unchanged -- that the iteration converges, R_d -> R({d beta}) -- but three things around it moved. The two attacks ruled out by measurement become three, and the third is ruled out by ARGUMENT: no exponential weight restores a spectral gap, since the log essential radius at weight r^m is the same expression whose stationary point is r*, meeting log rho there and strictly above it elsewhere, so a Foster-Lyapunov drift V(m) = theta^m is pinned at exactly rho and useless otherwise. The literature is named: Ocafrain's moving-boundary results give that no strict quasi-stationary distribution exists once the boundary moves, so the phase-indexed family is forced rather than chosen, and that a quasi-ergodic distribution exists for a finite state space with a periodic boundary by Darroch-Seneta, covering the truncated rational barrier -- while the general theorems assume a conditional Doeblin condition equivalent to exponential uniform convergence, which this process fails by being critical. And the driving is shown not to be the obstruction: the constant in TV ~ c/d is flat in q across six convergents from 19 to 24727. Also strengthened: psi was claimed bounded and is now stated as of bounded variation, with sum |a_k| = 4.58 and the warning that the exponent steepens with the window. PAPERS A AND C ARE UNCHANGED and deliberately so. Paper A's text -- 'with Rhin's effective measure this excludes every cycle with L^14.3 <= n log n / 915' -- is accurate as written, since the 915 arises in the Simons-de Weger conversion of Rhin's measure and the paper credits both separately; J-rhin-eight-has-no-computed-threshold confirms L^14.3 rather than changing it, and Paper A never claimed L^8.616. Paper C has no contact with any result of the day. Both are deposited with DOIs, so leaving them alone is the action, not the absence of one. No bound moves. PaperBTailSpectrum.tailRoot_pos records that the tail root is positive on 0 < s < 1, which is what lets the root be divided by. SUPERSEDED IN THE MANUSCRIPT, 20 September 2026: the differenced sum 4.58 and the steepening-exponent warning were replaced in Section 6 by the closed-form jump spectrum of J-paper-b-jump-spectrum-is-the-survivor-sequence and J-paper-b-jump-amplitude-is-closed-form; the Lean statement of this row is unchanged.

Paper B's Theorem 6.1 discards three quarters of its own exponent, and the discard is avoidable at no cost. THE STEP. The proof needs a Chernoff threshold q with 1/2 < q < p, p = log2/log3, satisfying p*d - 1 >= q*(d-1); the -1 is the leading O, spent before the binomial starts. The published proof takes q = (p+1/2)/2. THE SHARP CHOICE. The break-even threshold is q_d = p - (1-p)/(d-1), at which the step holds with EQUALITY, so it is the largest admissible threshold at depth d rather than one choice among many: PaperBThreshold.breakEven, breakEven_saturates, breakEven_admissible, and le_breakEven_of_admissible, all over any Field (order added only where used, via Admissible). q = p itself is genuinely blocked, and blocked only by p < 1 (self_not_admissible, beta_self_not_admissible, beta_lt_one). NO LARGE-d CLAUSE. The one remaining constraint is q_d > 1/2, which by breakEven_four and breakEven_three reduces to 5/8 < p <= 2/3, i.e. to the two integer facts 2^8 > 3^5 (256 > 243) and 2^3 < 3^2 (8 < 9): beta_gt_five_eighths, beta_le_two_thirds, breakEven_gt_half_four, breakEven_le_half_three, with first_usable_depth naming the depth. So the sharpened bound holds at every depth from d = 4 on, and the published 'for all sufficiently large fixed d' can be deleted. THE SIZE OF THE GAIN. chernoff_rate, which minimises E[e^(theta X)] for the step X in {log(3/2), -log2}, returns exactly theta(p) = 0.965906553233 to 1.1e-16: the walk stays nonnegative exactly when o*log3 >= d*log2, so the Cramer rate of the walk and the binomial large-deviation rate at threshold p are the same number, and Theorem 6.1's own inequality reaches it. Paper B reports 0.0085959587 per letter against the available 0.0346881850: 24.8%. CLOSED FORM. At q_d the bound is not merely sharp in rate; its constant is p. With KL(q) = -log theta(q) and KL'(q) = log(q/(1-q)), (1/2) theta(q_d)^(d-1) / rho^d -> (1/2) exp(KL(p)) exp((1-p) KL'(p)) = p^p (1-p)^(1-p) (p/(1-p))^(1-p) = p^p p^(1-p) = p -- every factor of (1-p) cancels. So the sharpened Theorem 6.1 reads dens(N minus C_d) <= p rho^d (1+O(1/d)) with both constants explicit and no unspecified 'some fixed t > 0'; the O(1/d) is confirmed to decay by exactly a factor 10 per decade of d from 1e3 to 1e5. WHAT IS LEFT. N_d/2^d ~ C rho^d d^(-3/2) with C = kappa G(1) = 10.90, so the sharpened bound overshoots by exactly the meander polynomial: truth/(p rho^d) * d^(3/2) measures 16.4, 17.0, 16.6 at d = 640, 1280, 2560 against C/p = 17.28. CORRECTED by J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic: C is not a constant, so those three numbers are samples of psi/p rather than approaches to a limit, and their wobble is the oscillation and not measurement noise. The sharpened bound and the d^(-3/2) exponent are unaffected. That is an independent route to the meander constant, using only the exact DP count and the sharpened Chernoff bound and none of the ladder-height transform. The published midpoint version by contrast overshoots by an exponentially growing factor -- 1.2e6 at d = 320, 6.9e17 at d = 1280, log-log slope 25.5 and rising -- so the gap it leaves is not a polynomial at all. WHAT DOES NOT MOVE. Theorem 6.1's conclusion is density one, which follows from any theta < 1 and is untouched; this is a rate, not a new theorem, and it excludes no cycle and proves no termination. It does close the gap between Theorem 6.1 as published and the measured constant: after sharpening, the only thing between the two is the meander factor already identified.

The exact reduction behind the almost-periodic prefactor of J-paper-b-meander-prefactor-is-almost-periodic, together with the one step of it that is NOT proved. Steps Y = X - BETA with X ~ Bernoulli(1/2), so Lam(l) = -l BETA + log((e^l+1)/2). THE TILT. Lam'(l) = -BETA + e^l/(e^l+1) vanishes exactly at lamStar = log(BETA/(1-BETA)) = 0.536207535136, where the tilted coin is Bernoulli(BETA) and the walk o_t - t BETA has mean zero and per-step variance BETA(1-BETA) = 0.232857400: PaperBTilt.expLamStar, lamStar_mean_zero, and beta_mean_zero at BETA itself. So BETA is the threshold for a structural reason rather than by fitting. THE RATE IS AN IDENTITY. rho = exp(Lam(lamStar)) = exp(-lamStar BETA)/(2(1-BETA)) = BETA^(-BETA) (1-BETA)^(BETA-1) / 2, which is exactly theta(BETA). J-theorem-six-one-threshold-is-slack recorded theta(p) = rho as agreeing to 1.1e-16; PaperBTilt.rho_closed_form and beta_rho_closed prove it, kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. THE CHANGE OF MEASURE. N_d/2^d = rho^d E~[e^(-lamStar S_d); S_t >= 0 for all t <= d], verified against the integer DP to 1e-12 at d = 50, 200, 500. WHERE THE PHASE COMES FROM. On the event S_d = m_d + (1 - fract(d BETA)) with m_d = o_d - ceil(d BETA) a nonnegative integer, and 1 - fract(d BETA) is exactly the least attainable endpoint: PaperBTilt.gap, with ceil_sub_eq_one_sub_fract naming it. Hence the exact factorisation N_d/2^d = rho^d e^(-lamStar (1 - fract(d BETA))) G(d) with G integer-indexed. THE BARRIER IS STURMIAN. m_(t+1) = m_t + X_(t+1) - b_t where b_t = ceil((t+1)BETA) - ceil(t BETA) is 0 or 1 (PaperBTilt.sturmian_step), the Sturmian word of BETA. So the killed walk runs against a Sturmian barrier, not a straight line, which is why the classical local limit theorem does not apply. THE TWO EFFECTS NEARLY CANCEL. The explicit factor rises by e^(0.9 lamStar) = 1.6203 across the circle while psi rises only 1.0606, so the integer part h falls by 1.527, measured. The small observed oscillation is the residue of two large opposed ones: a wider barrier gap costs e^(-lamStar(1-phi)) in the tilt and buys survival room in h. Stripping the elementary factor therefore does not simplify the problem -- it exchanges a 6% oscillation for a 53% one. WHAT REMAINS OPEN. Everything above is an identity. The existence of psi(phi) = e^(-lamStar(1-phi)) h(phi), i.e. the convergence of d^(3/2) G(d) along fract(d BETA) -> phi, needs a local limit theorem for this Sturmian-driven killed walk and is NOT proved here or anywhere in the laboratory. This row supplies the exact reduction that obligation is stated against; it proves no asymptotic and moves no bound. PaperBTilt.one_add_tailRoot is the inversion 1 + tailRoot b = b-inverse used to move between the tail variable and the base; it shares a basename with PaperBTailSpectrum.one_add_tailRoot, which states the same inversion in the spectral module's own variable, so the two must be cited qualified.

psi's discontinuity set is exactly the forward rotation orbit {k BETA mod 1 : k >= 0}, which identifies the unexplained second jump of J-psi-is-bounded-variation-with-an-ostrowski-spectrum and subsumes it into a cascade. THE MECHANISM IS EXACT. The Sturmian barrier increment is b_t = 1 iff fract(t BETA) >= 1 - BETA (PaperBTilt.sturmian_step), and fract((d-1-k)BETA) = fract(d BETA) - (k+1)BETA. The set {phi : phi - (k+1)BETA mod 1 >= 1 - BETA} is an arc of length BETA whose endpoints are k BETA and (k+1)BETA. So the barrier step k+1 from the end switches at k BETA, and taking the union over k the jump set is the whole orbit: countable, dense, with summable sizes. The k = 1 member is BETA = 0.6309, which is the jump at about 0.633 recorded as unexplained. MEASURED. At 512 bins over 20001 depths the nine largest jumps land on k BETA for k = 0 to 8 with no exception, each within 0.0006 of target against a bin width of 0.00195. Sizes from windows of width 0.02 either side: -0.07112, -0.03415, -0.01505, -0.01559, -0.01078, -0.00573, -0.00593, -0.00403, -0.00172 at k = 0 to 8, every one NEGATIVE. So psi drops crossing each k BETA upward and recovers smoothly between: a sawtooth on the orbit. The sizes pair up at k = (2,3), (5,6), (8,9), (10,11) -- differences of 3 = q_2 -- which is the three-distance structure of the orbit. From k = 8 the jumps fall to the level at which a window comparison also picks up psi's local slope (off-orbit controls read up to 0.0056), so they are not individually resolved and nothing is claimed for them. WHAT IT EXPLAINS. Both earlier readings, at once. Jumps give the k^(-0.79) Fourier decay, and a jump set which IS a rotation orbit gives the Ostrowski peaks, the transform of the jump measure being sum_k a_k e^(-2 pi i j k BETA). It also revises the attribution of the k = 0 jump: the explicit factor e^(-lamStar(1-phi)) jumps by e^(lamStar) = 1.7095 on the circle, but the measured net jump at 0 is only 7%, so h cancels most of it, consistent with the two-competing-effects reading. The jumps at k >= 1 come from h alone, the explicit factor being smooth away from 0. No bound moves; this is the structure of psi, not its existence, which remains open.

rho has a second variational characterisation, in the TAIL variable, dual to the Cramer one in the tilt variable -- and the minimum is attained with a DOUBLE root, which is the structural reason a polynomial factor accompanies rho^d. THE SET-UP. In the m coordinate the conditional law updates by two maps: T_0 pi(m) = (pi(m) + pi(m-1))/2 when the barrier does not rise, and T_1 pi(m) = (pi(m) + pi(m+1))/2 when it does, the latter losing pi(0)/2. A geometric tail r^m keeps its SHAPE under both -- T_0 multiplies its mass by (1+1/r)/2 and T_1 by (1+r)/2 -- so along a word with density BETA of rises the tail reproduces with factor [(1+1/r)/2]^(1-BETA) [(1+r)/2]^BETA. Setting that equal to rho is the characteristic equation for the quasi-stationary tail. THE DOUBLE ROOT. The exponent is stationary exactly at r* = (1-BETA)/BETA = exp(-lamStar) = 0.584962501, and there 1 + 1/r* = 1/(1-BETA) and 1 + r* = 1/BETA, so its value collapses to -[log2 + BETA log BETA + (1-BETA) log(1-BETA)] = -KL(BETA || 1/2) = log rho. The minimum TOUCHES log rho rather than crossing it: verified to 5.55e-17, and g(r* +- delta) > log rho at delta = 0.2, 0.05, 0.01, 0.001. So rho = min over r of that expression, attained at the tilt. WHY IT MATTERS. A simple root would give a pure geometric tail and a pure exponential decay; a double root is the critical case and produces the polynomial correction, which is where d^(-3/2) comes from. The tail ratio of the quasi-stationary profile being exactly exp(-lamStar) also ties J-boundary-fraction-is-the-clean-coordinate to J-paper-b-tilt-reduction-and-the-phase-factor: the rate at which the conditional profile decays away from the barrier is the same number that makes the walk mean zero. LEAN. The substitutions are one_add_inv_tailRoot and one_add_tailRoot, the identification of the tail ratio with the tilt is tailRoot_mul_odds, and the first-order condition is stationary_iff_eq_tailRoot, with tailRoot naming the quantity; all kernel-checked on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound alone. MEASURED, WITH A CAVEAT. The conditional profile's ratio pi(m+1)/pi(m) falls through r* from above around m = 60 to 80 and then continues below it, reading 0.5940, 0.5819, 0.5699, 0.5498 at m = 40, 80, 150, 300. Paper C Proposition 9.3 on the word-weight framework of RateFreeDensity. For a nonnegative word weight mu with WeightSplit (each word's two children carry at most the parent's weight) and x >= 1: the tilted generating function Z_d = weightGen mu x d satisfies Z_{d+1} <= Z_d + (x-1) oddMass_d (weightGen_succ_le) and Z_{d+1} <= Z_d (1 + (x-1) s_d) with s_d = tiltedShare mu x d = oddMass_d / Z_d (weightGen_succ_le_share); for 0 <= q, 1 + (x-1)s <= a_q exp(c_q max(s-q,0)) with a_q = 1 + (x-1)q, c_q = (x-1)/a_q (one_add_le_exp_excess); hence Z_d <= Z_0 a_q^d exp(c_q sum_{t<d} max(s_t - q, 0)) (weightGen_le_pressure), and with weight_markov the mass of words with at least k odd letters is at most that over x^k (count_le_pressure). This is the reduction M_{theta,q} => P_theta => Tao-type count, kernel-checked; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only. Also: NoMomentum mu x q delta d := sum_{t<d} max(s_t - q, 0) <= delta d is the hypothesis as a Lean proposition, and count_le_of_noMomentum gives the Tao-type count <= Z_0 a_q^d exp(c_q delta d) / x^k under it; tilt_exponent_eq_kl shows that at the re-centring tilt x = p(1-q)/(q(1-p)) the per-step exponent p log x - log(1 + (x-1)q) equals the relative entropy p log(p/q) + (1-p) log((1-p)/(1-q)), so the exponent of the count is d D(p||q) minus the excess term. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

Mean-share form of the no-momentum hypothesis. MeanShare mu x q d := sum_{t<d} s_t <= q d, with s_t the tilted odd share of the WeightSplit weight mu at tilt x. Then (weightGen_le_of_meanShare) Z_d <= Z_0 a_q^d with a_q = 1 + (x-1) q and no exponential slack, by the product form Z_d <= Z_0 prod_{t<d} (1 + (x-1) s_t) (weightGen_le_prod) and AM-GM (prod_le_mean_pow, Jensen for log); hence (count_le_of_meanShare) #{o_d >= k} <= Z_0 a_q^d / x^k, and on the live count (juggler_count_le_of_meanShare) #{n in [1,N] : live for d steps, oddCount >= k} <= N a_q^d / x^k. NoMomentum mu x q delta d implies MeanShare mu x (q + delta) d (meanShare_of_noMomentum), so the mean form is the weaker sufficient hypothesis: Paper C's M_(theta,q) bounds the positive excursions sum (s_t - q)^+; only the depth-average of s_t is needed, and depths with share below q compensate depths above it. The difference is depth-to-depth variation only, since s_t already averages over all starts at depth t. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

What the mean-share hypothesis does not need, machine-checked. Paper C section 9.3(a) and 9.3(b) were prose; these are the statements. (a) MeanShareOff mu x q d E := sum over t in [0,d) minus E of s_t <= q |[0,d) minus E|, with nothing whatever assumed on the exceptional set E. Then weightGen_le_of_meanShareOff gives Z_d <= Z_0 x^|[0,d) cap E| a_q^|[0,d) minus E|: each excluded depth costs exactly one factor of x and nothing more, because a single letter multiplies the tilted moment by at most x (tiltedShare_le_one). count_le_of_meanShareOff and juggler_count_le_of_meanShareOff carry it to the Tao-type count and to the live count of Juggler starts. meanShareOff_empty: the empty exceptional set is MeanShare, so this is a strict weakening of J-mean-share-form, which is itself a weakening of Paper C's M_(theta,q). (b) initial_depths_are_free: taking E to be the first k depths, no assumption at all on those depths costs more than the constant factor x^k, so every fixed-depth split, the depth-five one included, cannot bear on the reduction. This is why bounded-depth cylinder work is not a route, stated as a theorem rather than a warning. (c) tower_ratio_lt_one with tower_tolerance_half: an all-odd tower splitting with odd share beta at every level carries relative tilted weight (beta x / a_q)^t, so it is free exactly when beta < a_q/x; at q = 1/2 the threshold is (1+x)/(2x) = (1 + e^-theta)/2, which is the 0.836 the note quotes at theta_19. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.

Even steps never deepen the Juggler floor tower. For every j, Nat.sqrt^[j] x = s iff s^(2^j) <= x < (s+1)^(2^j) (sqrt_iter_eq_iff); on an even run floorPower is iterated Nat.sqrt (floorPower_iter_of_even); an odd step followed by j even steps equals Nat.sqrt^[j+1] (n^3), i.e. floor(n^(3/2^(j+1))) with one floor and no nesting (floorPower_odd_even_run, floorPower_odd_even_run_eq_iff); the OE fiber of FateContagion is the case j = 1. Hence the orbit value after a word is a nested tower with one level per odd letter and exponents 3/2^(j_r+1) fixed by the even runs: the tower height is the odd count, not the depth. Kernel-checked; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only.
